title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
summary: Christie Brinkley reveals how she keeps all three adult children coming home and why losing both parents deepened her devotion to family time.
story: Christie Brinkley, star of ‘American Summer,’ explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.
Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.
The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections.
The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital those themes aren't just on-screen. They're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.
CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS
Christie Brinkley's new movie, "American Summer, hit theaters Sept. 4. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids. ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that.

Christie Brinkley and daughters Sailor Lee Brinkley-Cook and Alexa Ray Joel arrive at the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit 2017 launch event at Center415 Event Space in New York City Feb. 16, 2017. (GC Images)
"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared.
"And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."
Christie Brinkley's children — Alexa Ray Joel, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook and Sailor Brinkley-Cook — remain a central part of her life. (Getty Images)

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.
WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."
Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley appear onstage at the Big Apple Circus in New York City Feb. 1, 2020. (Getty Images for Big Apple Circus)
Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."
Christie Brinkley's parents attend a pageant in Hawaii, date unknown. (Corbis via Getty Images)

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."
Family came first for Steve Guttenberg, who paused his acting career to help care for his father, Stanley Guttenberg. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"American Summer" is described as a homage to families in small-town America. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.
For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.
Christie Brinkley and Sailor Brinkley Cook attend the Solving Kids Cancer Annual Hamptons Luncheon at Tutto II Giorno in Southampton, N.Y., on Aug. 4, 2025. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "This [story] takes us back before there were cellphones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cellphones more often and just connecting with loved ones.

"And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach. I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'
Steve Guttenberg and Christie Brinkley in a scene from "American Summer." (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections. ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."
"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Christie Brinkley poses with son Jack at the opening night arrivals for Michael Moore's "The Terms of My Surrender" on Broadway at the Belasco Theatre in New York City Aug. 10, 2017. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)
Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher, a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.

Christie Brinkley attends Best Friends Animal Society's The Spirit of the Sanctuary"benefit Aug. 24, 2026, at Jill Rappaport's Last Buck Ranch in Water Mill, N.Y. (Getty Images)

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."

title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
summary: Jeff Foxworthy reveals why he brought back his iconic "redneck" jokes after 20 years for his Fox Nation special "The Joke's on Me," streaming now.
story: Foxworthy was able to turn what should have been an insult into a ‘compliment’ by turning it into a ‘badge of honor.’
Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck" and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment.
He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult ... into a badge of honor."
DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY
"I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said.

"I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger trucks. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me."
Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up routine. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one.

He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this" and stopped telling them.
"The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003, he said.
WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up.

After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back.
"I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said.
"And I say, ‘Well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last.’ It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it."
Foxworthy brought jokes about rednecks back into his act after realizing they still resonated with his audience. (Gary Gershoff/Getty Images)
He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club.

"It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'"
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes

Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke-writing process that goes into creating a special.

The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Foxworthy came up with the idea for his new special after watching a documentary about the Beatles. (Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
When Fox Nation approached him with the offer to do a stand-up special, he pitched them the behind-the-scenes idea.

"I said, 'But if you're willing to try something different, if you will show me note cards in hand, going into a club on a Tuesday night or a Wednesday night and just throwing these thoughts out.' Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said.

"You would think after 40 years, I would know. Now, I'll go in there with an idea, 'Oh, this is really funny.' And then nobody laughs. Or I'll have a card where I think this is so stupid, I'm embarrassed to say it, and you throw it out there and everybody's beaten the tables laughing. And you're like, really? And, so, I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'OK, we'll do it.'"
Foxworthy has hinted that this could be his last stand-up special but assures fans that doesn't mean he will never perform on a stage again.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Foxworthy hinted this may be his last stand-up special. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Beloved Benefit)
He told Fox News Digital he has reached a point in his life where the time he would rather spend with his grandkids or on his tractor.
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy clears up his comments about retiring from stand-up

"I've been on the road nonstop," he added. "I laugh at my music friends when they say they're on tour. I said, 'Well, tour implies it stops. At some point,' I said, 'I've been on tour since 1984.' It just never stopped. I still love stand-up. I just don't know that I'm willing. And, to be honest, I'm not sure I can do anything any better than this, which just feels like a good place to stop."

title: Brooke Hogan threatens to expose family receipts in 'final warning'
summary: Brooke Hogan threatened to release screenshots after Linda Hogan accused her of tossing the family aside, escalating their public estrangement.
story: HGTV ‘Rock the Block’ contestant Brooke Hogan tells Fox News Digital about her grief and healing journey after her father’s death.
Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's prepared to use them.

The 38-year-old daughter of late wrestling legend Hulk Hogan fired back after her mother, Linda Hogan, publicly lamented their yearslong estrangement and accused Brooke of tossing her family aside "like trash."
"This 👌 close to breaking out some screenshots – which are ONE of the many reasons WHY," Brooke wrote over a screenshot of her mother's Facebook post from Aug. 30 shared to her Instagram Story.
BROOKE HOGAN SAYS ‘I COULD HAVE SAVED YOU’ IN HAUNTING REGRET AFTER HULK HOGAN’S DEATH
Brooke Hogan threatened to bring out the "receipts" as her bitter family feud with mother Linda Hogan erupted again. (Brooke Hogan Oleksy/Instagram )
"I don't take CONSTANTLY dragging my name through the mud lightly," she continued.
"The selective amnesia isn't gonna work."
Brooke ended the message with two words: "Final warning."
The latest flare-up came after Linda shared old family photos on Facebook while expressing her frustration over her fractured relationship with her daughter.
"I posted these wonderful photos of Brooke my daughter with me and my ex-husband her father and my mom and dad and really .. the whole family ! Brooke is loved," Linda wrote.
"We feel hurt every day that she just tosses us aside .... like trash," she continued. "I want to make sure she remembers how it really was .. and can really see how much she was adored and loved."
Brooke's response suggested she remembers their family history differently and is prepared to make private communications public if the criticism continues.
The mother and daughter's latest exchange is another chapter in a fractured family that has played out publicly for years.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Brooke Hogan with her brother, Nick Hogan, and parents Hulk Hogan and Linda Hogan. (Michael Loccisano/FilmMagic)
Brooke first became famous alongside her parents, Hulk and Linda, and younger brother, Nick Hogan, on the VH1 reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which premiered in 2005.
The show followed the wrestling superstar and his family while also documenting Brooke's budding music career and her father's protective approach to his teenage daughter.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
The family dynamic changed dramatically after Linda filed for divorce from Hulk in 2007 after more than two decades of marriage. Their divorce was finalized in 2009.
Years later, Brooke became estranged from both parents, but she has made clear that her reasons for cutting contact with her mother were separate from the issues she had with her father.
Brooke addressed the family rift directly in a lengthy Instagram statement on March 27, 2025, insisting she had not chosen one parent over the other.

"No contact with my mom has nothing to do with my dad, and no contact with my father has nothing to do with my mother," Brooke wrote. "I have completely separate reasons for going no contact with each of my parents."
HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED
In the same statement, Brooke made serious allegations about her childhood and family relationships.

"I have been EXTREMELY verbally and mentally abused since childhood," she alleged. "Sadly, it would frequently turn physical. And sometimes it's not by the person you would assume, abuse comes in all shapes and sizes."
Brooke did not identify a specific person in that portion of her statement.
The Hogan family at the 2004 Radio Music Awards in Las Vegas in October 2004. (Frank Micelotta/Getty Images)
She also claimed she had been put in the position of publicly defending behavior within her family before eventually questioning what she had been told.
"I've been asked to defend poor behavior to the public and have done so out of love. Only to find I was misinformed, manipulated, and lied to," she wrote.
"I longed for a normal family, but it never came to fruition. I've repeatedly held my hand out to help them, only to have them pull me into the darkness with them.
"I've set boundaries that were not respected, which turned into a 'no contact' situation."
Her comments came after Linda publicly discussed the family's troubles in March 2025, reigniting attention around their strained relationship.
The conflict marked a dramatic departure from the image viewers were introduced to two decades earlier on "Hogan Knows Best."
Brooke was a teenager when the series premiered, with the show following her budding music career, dating life and her father's famously protective parenting.
WWE LEGEND HULK HOGAN'S DEATH REPORT RELEASED
Brooke previously told Fox News Digital that, despite her strained relationship with her father, she loved him. (Acey Harper/Getty Images)
In the years that followed, the family relationships viewers once watched on television became increasingly strained, with some of those disputes eventually playing out in public.
Her relationship with her father received renewed attention after his death on July 24, 2025.
Hulk, born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 after being hospitalized for cardiac arrest.
Hulk was survived by Brooke and Nick, whom he shared with Linda, as well as his wife, Sky Daily.
Despite being estranged from her father when he died, Brooke made clear in an April interview with Fox News Digital that her love for him had never disappeared.

"I’m honest with him now, and I talk to him all the time, even if that seems like I’m a cuckoo bird," she told Fox News Digital. "If he showed up today, I would just be like, ‘I love you so much, and I wish you would have just let me in.’"
Brooke also offered rare insight into why their relationship had become strained before his death.
Brooke said that she wanted to "save" her father before his death. (John Parra/WireImage)

"[It's] tough because, obviously, my dad and I weren't really speaking prior to his death — not because I didn't love him. … It's that he had become a little bit calloused in the direction he was going in his life and the people he was surrounding himself with," she said.

"I am the daughter that wanted to save him. And it's kind of, like, you can try to save somebody and if they don't want to be saved … it's a tough position to be in."
Her comments to Fox News Digital echoed what Brooke had emphasized in her March 2025 statement. Distancing herself from her father did not mean she had sided with her mother or vice versa.

story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts discuss George Clooney saying the United States government is run by the ‘least qualified people.’

The former reality star, who delved into politics this year with a run for mayor of Los Angeles, pulled no punches when he took to social media Friday to criticize Clooney and his wife, Amal.

"$500M net worth George Clooney could’ve permanently housed 8 homeless people for the rest of their lives with the money he spent on a single-use dress for his wife at a 4 hour event," Pratt claimed on X.

Spencer Pratt ran for mayor of Los Angeles on the Republican ticket before conceding in June. (Gilbert Flores/Getty Images)

title: Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan among stars who left fame behind before returning to Hollywood
summary: From Rick Moranis to Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan, these Hollywood stars walked away from fame and made remarkable comebacks years later on screen.
story: Actor Jonathan Bennett tells Fox News Digital he’s excited about his ‘Mean Girls’ co-star Lindsay Lohan’s return to acting and discusses co-hosting ChristmasCon with Lacey Chabert.
Rick Moranis is stepping back into the spotlight after decades away from Hollywood, joining a growing list of stars who left fame behind and later returned.
The 73-year-old actor is taking on his first live-action part in nearly 30 years after walking away from the entertainment industry at the height of his career after a family tragedy.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet in "Spaceballs: The New One," the long-awaited sequel to Mel Brooks' 1987 cult classic science-fiction comedy movie, "Spaceballs."
'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME

Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan disappeared from Hollywood before making triumphant returns years later. (David Becker/Getty Images for CinemaCon; Dave Benett/WireImage; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images)

In July, Moranis made a rare public appearance to promote the sequel at San Diego Comic-Con, where he received a standing ovation when he appeared on stage wearing his character's signature massive black helmet. Moranis participated in a panel discussion alongside co-stars Daphne Zuniga, Josh Gad, Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman, as well as director Josh Greenbaum and screenwriters Benji Samit and Dan Hernandez.
Zuniga is reprising her role as Princess Vespa, while other original stars who returned for the sequel include George Wyner as Colonel Sandurz, Bill Pullman as Lone Starr and Brooks as Yogurt.
During the panel, Moranis revealed what finally brought him back in front of the camera after his decades-long hiatus.
Moranis made a surprise appearance at the "Spaceballs: The New One" panel at Comic-Con International: San Diego in July. (Variety via Getty Images)

"This came along right at the right time, and I started talking to these folks and hearing who was going to be in it," Moranis said, via People. "I spoke to Josh Greenbaum, and I heard that Bill Pullman was coming back, and that Lewis was going to be in it too. And it just felt like this is it. It’s time and — yes. I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made."

Moranis became one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in a string of hit movies, including "Spaceballs," "Ghostbusters," "Little Shop of Horrors," "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," "Parenthood," "My Blue Heaven" and "The Flintstones."

However, after his wife, costume designer Ann Belsky, died in 1991 after a battle with breast cancer, Moranis stepped away from show business to focus on raising their two children, daughter Rachel and son Mitchell. He last appeared on-screen in 1997's "Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves," the third installment in the "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" movie series.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet. (Alamy)
During a 2015 interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Moranis reflected on his decision to prioritize his family over his career.

"I was working with really interesting people, wonderful people," he said. "I went from that to being at home with a couple of little kids, which is a very different lifestyle. But it was important to me. I have absolutely no regrets whatsoever. My life is wonderful."
Moranis also clarified that he had not officially retired from acting, telling the outlet, "I took a break, which turned into a longer break."

"But I’m interested in anything that I would find interesting," he continued. "I still get the occasional query about a film or television role and as soon as one comes along that piques my interest, I'll probably do it.
MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE
"I’m happy with the things I said yes to, and I’m very happy with the many things I’ve said no to," Moranis added. "Yes, I am picky, and I’ll continue to be picky. Picky has worked for me."
One of Rick Moranis' final on-screen roles was in "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," in 1989. (AJ Pics/Alamy Stock Photo)

Though Moranis left live-action films behind for many years, he continued working occasionally as a voice actor. He first dipped his toe back into the movie business in 2001, voicing two characters in "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer & the Island of Misfit Toys." Some of his other voice-acting gigs include "Brother Bear," "The Animated Adventures of Bob & Doug McKenzie" and the voice of Dark Helmet in "The Goldbergs."

During his appearance at Comic-Con, Moranis once again set the record straight regarding the perception that he had retired as he revealed that he and Brooks had long discussed making a follow-up to "Spaceballs."
"Actually, I started talking to Mel about the sequel in 1989," he said. "We kept talking about it.
"I really wasn’t retired; I was just negotiating."
STOCKARD CHANNING HITS FIRST RED CARPET IN 2 YEARS AFTER SAYING SHE'S A 'RECLUSE'

While Moranis’ return has drawn renewed attention due to his decades-long absence, other stars have also taken long breaks from Hollywood before making high-profile comebacks. Here's a look at several celebrities who stepped away from the spotlight for years before finding their way back to the screen.
Cameron Diaz
Cameron Diaz returned to Hollywood after stepping away from acting in 2014. (Getty Images)
Cameron Diaz was one of Hollywood’s most bankable stars when she quietly stepped away from acting in 2014.

Diaz made her breakthrough in 1994's "The Mask" and went on to star in a series of hit films, including "There’s Something About Mary," "My Best Friend's Wedding," "Charlie's Angels," "My Sister's Keeper," "Shrek" and "The Other Woman," among others.
After starring in 2014's "Annie," Diaz walked away from show business to focus on building a life with husband Benji Madden.

"It felt like the right thing for me to reclaim my own life, and I just really didn't care about anything else," the actress said during a 2025 appearance at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, according to E! News.

"Nobody's opinion, nobody's success, no one's offer, no one's anything could change my mind about my decision of taking care of myself and building the life that I really wanted to have. I think it really comes to what are you passionate about? For me, it was to build my family."
During her break, Diaz welcomed daughter Raddix, 6, and son Cardinal, 2, with Madden and launched her Avaline wine brand. The couple's third child, son Nautus, was born in May.

After a decade away from movies, Diaz returned to the screen in Netflix’s 2025 action comedy "Back in Action," starring opposite Jamie Foxx. She has since lined up other projects, including Netflix’s "Bad Day," Apple TV+’s "Outcome" and "Shrek 5," in which she will reprise her voice role as Princess Fiona.
Lindsay Lohan
Lindsay Lohan mounted a comeback years after fleeing Hollywood for Dubai. (Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Images)
Lindsay Lohan’s comeback followed years of intense public scrutiny and a long stretch away from major studio films.
Lohan became one of Hollywood’s biggest young stars after breaking out in "The Parent Trap" and later leading hits including "Freaky Friday," "Mean Girls" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded."

However, Lohan's promising career was derailed by multiple box-office flops and a string of highly-publicized legal problems and substance abuse issues. After years of tabloid attention and personal struggles, Lohan left the United States in 2014 and eventually relocated full-time to Dubai, spending much of the next decade outside the Hollywood spotlight. She told Emirates Woman in 2018 that moving to Dubai afforded her "a fresh start."

Lohan began rebuilding her acting career with Netflix’s 2022 holiday movie "Falling for Christmas," followed by more streaming projects and a major return to one of her signature roles in "Freakier Friday."

During a 2025 interview with The Sunday Times, Lohan said she stepped away because she had lost her excitement for making movies and wanted "a more private life, a real life," before returning once she felt "that itch again."
Lohan will next be seen in Hulu’s "Count My Lies," a limited series in which she stars opposite Shailene Woodley and Kit Harington.
Ke Huy Quan
Ke Huy Quan's comeback culminated in a Best Supporting Actor Oscar win. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Image)
Ke Huy Quan’s Hollywood disappearance ended with one of the industry’s most celebrated comeback stories.

Quan became a child star after playing Short Round opposite Harrison Ford in 1984’s "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom" and Data in 1985’s "The Goonies." However, Ke only landed a few minor TV and film roles after his early fame and found himself being offered stereotypical parts geared toward Asians.

During a 2023 interview with People, Quan said he made the "very difficult decision" to walk away from acting in the early 2000s. He then spent years working behind the camera as a stunt coordinator and assistant director.
However, he recalled that, after seeing 2018’s "Crazy Rich Asians," he was inspired to revisit his first love.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"I was happy working behind the camera, but I had serious FOMO (fear of missing out)," Ke told the outlet. "I wanted to be up there with my fellow Asian actors."

After roughly two decades away from acting, Quan returned in 2022’s "Everything Everywhere All at Once," a role that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor. In his emotional Oscars speech, Quan reflected on his unlikely journey, saying, "Dreams are something you have to believe in. I almost gave up on mine."
Daniel Day-Lewis
Daniel Day-Lewis returned to Hollywood to team up with his son Ronan for 2025's "Anemone." (Jason Merritt/WireImage)
Daniel Day-Lewis has stepped away from Hollywood more than once, but his latest return marked the end of what many believed was a permanent retirement.

Known for his intensely selective approach to roles, Day-Lewis has previously taken long breaks throughout his career. After starring in 1997’s "The Boxer," Day-Lewis retreated from acting and spent several years in Italy learning shoemaking before returning in Martin Scorsese’s 2002 film, "Gangs of New York."

The three-time Oscar winner announced he was retiring from acting after starring in 2017’s "Phantom Thread." At the time, his representative said, "Daniel Day-Lewis will no longer be working as an actor. He is immensely grateful to all of his collaborators and audiences over the many years. This is a private decision and neither he nor his representatives will make any further comment on this subject."
Eight years later, his son, Ronan Day-Lewis, persuaded him to co-write and star in the 2025 drama "Anemone."
Day-Lewis later pushed back on the idea that he ever meant to permanently retire.

In a 2025 Rolling Stone interview, Day-Lewis said he "never intended to retire, really" and called his earlier retirement announcement "grandiose gibberish." He explained that he still loved the work but struggled with the lifestyle around filmmaking and felt "hollowed out" after "Phantom Thread."

He said returning for "Anemone" was largely about working with Ronan, who directed the film. Day-Lewis said that collaboration brought the spark back, saying, "Working with Ro, that furnace just lit up."
Renée Zellweger
Renee Zellweger took a six-year break from acting. (Getty Images)
Renée Zellweger stepped away from Hollywood after years of working at a relentless pace.

Zellweger became one of the most prominent actresses of the late 1990s and 2000s with roles in the hit movies "Jerry Maguire," "Bridget Jones’s Diary," "Chicago," "Cold Mountain" and "Cinderella Man." But after 2010’s "My Own Love Song," Zellweger took a six-year break from acting.
During a 2025 interview with British Vogue, Zellweger explained why she decided to pause her career.

"I was sick of the sound of my own voice. When I was working, I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, listen to you. Are you sad again, Renée? Oh, is this your mad voice?’ It was a regurgitation of the same emotional experiences," she said.
Zellweger told the outlet that her hiatus from acting enabled her to pursue other projects and embrace a healthier lifestyle.

"I wrote music and studied international law," she said. "I built a house, rescued a pair of older doggies, created a partnership that led to a production company, advocated for and fundraised with a sick friend and spent a lot of time with family and godchildren and driving across the country with the dogs. I got healthy."

Zellweger returned in 2016 with the hit sequel "Bridget Jones’s Baby." She went on to earn some of the strongest reviews of her career for playing Judy Garland in 2019’s "Judy," and her performance earned her the Academy Award for best actress. Zellweger previously won the best supporting actress Oscar for her performance in "Cold Mountain."
Macaulay Culkin
Macaulay Culkin stepped away from acting as a teenager after childhood fame. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic)
Macaulay Culkin walked away from Hollywood after becoming one of the most famous child stars in the world.

Culkin shot to superstardom as Kevin McCallister in 1990’s "Home Alone" and its 1992 sequel, "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." He went on to star in hit films, including "My Girl," "The Good Son" and "Richie Rich."

After filming "Richie Rich," Culkin stepped away from acting, later explaining that he wanted to attend school, date and spend time with people his own age.

He returned nine years later with "Party Monster" and has continued accepting occasional projects on his own terms, including roles in "Saved!," "American Horror Story: Double Feature" and "The Righteous Gemstones."
Pamela Anderson
Pamela Anderson embraced a quieter lifestyle before her career reinvention. (Getty Images)
Pamela Anderson’s return to the spotlight has become one of Hollywood’s more unexpected late-career reinventions.

Anderson became a global sex symbol in the 1990s through "Baywatch," Playboy and years of tabloid attention that often overshadowed her acting ambitions. After decades of being defined by her image and personal life, she retreated to Vancouver Island, embraced a quieter lifestyle and began reassessing the public persona that had followed her for much of her career.

Her comeback began with a wave of projects that allowed her to reclaim her own story, including the 2023 Netflix documentary "Pamela, a Love Story" and her memoir, "Love, Pamela."
She made her Broadway debut in "Chicago" in 2022 and earned some of the strongest reviews of her career for "The Last Showgirl," along with Golden Globe and SAG nominations.

title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
summary: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
story: Jon Bon Jovi and Jay-Z said their hellos on the field ahead of the 2026 Super Bowl.
Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon from President Donald Trump.

Jones, an executive with Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now Trump has given him a completely clean slate.

The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar."
JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION
Trump pardoned 30 individuals Sept. 3, including Jay-Z's friend and business associate, Emory Jones. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images; Kevork S. Djansezian/Getty Images)

"Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. "I am deeply grateful to President @realdonaldtrump for granting clemency and pardons to 30 deserving individuals whose cases we carefully reviewed and brought forward — and to the White House Counsel team, led by Will Scharf, for the hard work behind these decisions.

"Among them is Emory Jones, who served nearly 16 years in federal prison and came home determined to build a different life. Today he is an entrepreneur and creative leader whose journey reminds us how much people can grow — and how much good they can still do."
TODD CHRISLEY RECALLS EMOTIONAL PHONE CALL WITH DAUGHTER SAVANNAH AFTER CONTROVERSIAL TRUMP PARDON
In 1999, Jones pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to distribute cocaine. The following year, he was sentenced to 188 months, nearly 16 years, in prison, with five years supervised release.
Jones was originally sentenced to 188 months in prison before his sentence was reduced to 151 months. (Getty Images for Fanatics)
Jones' legal team submitted a request for a reduction of his sentence in 2009, and, as part of their request, it submitted a series of letters from people familiar with Jones, including Jay-Z.

In a letter to the judge, Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, wrote that he'd be offering Jones an executive assistant job with Roc Apparel Group upon his release, with a starting salary of $50,000.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Jay-Z, photographed with wife Beyoncé, wrote a letter to the judge in 2009 in attempt to get Jones' sentence reduced. (Mike Coppola/Getty Images)

"As you might expect, this position needs to be filled as soon as possible," he wrote. "It is my strong desire to have Mr. Jones fill this position. I have known Mr. Jones for 15 years. I believe his attributes, including intelligence, interpersonal skills and solid work ethic will be a significant asset for my organization."

In another letter, Jones wrote about his conviction, saying, "Of all the excuses that I could have attributed my demise to, I chose not to use a single one. Excuses are tools of the incompetent and only build monuments to nothingness."

He also included mention of his support system, including Jay-Z, writing, "When a person or people make sacrifices and devote themselves to supporting you through the adversity of incarceration, you owe them.
"Nothing monetary because you can't put a price on love and support. However, you do owe them the privilege and opportunity to see you do something extremely positive with your life."

Jones still works with Jay-Z with his Roc Nation brand. (Getty Images)
Jones was resentenced to 151 months, still with five years supervised release, shaving 37 months off of his original sentence.

Today, he's the head of lifestyle at Roc Nation, and he has an executive role in fashion brand Paper Planes, which he and Jay-Z founded in 2014.

title: Joe Biden shares health update after prostate cancer diagnosis while issuing warning to others
summary: Joe Biden revealed his radiation treatment from last fall "worked as intended" as he urged men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors.
story: Jill Biden admits former President Joe Biden experienced a decline in mental acuity, "slowing down" and "stuttering more" during his term due to exhaustion, despite her urging him to seek re-election. Rep. Claudia Tenney comments on the situation, suggesting it's an opportunity for Jill Biden to gain power, highlighting the former First Lady's own upcoming book.

Former President Joe Biden shared an update on his battle with prostate cancer Tuesday, revealing that radiation treatment he underwent last fall "worked as intended" while urging American men not to delay conversations with their doctors about cancer screening.
Biden, 83, issued the update in a lengthy social media post marking Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, saying the occasion was more personal for him following his diagnosis last year.
"The radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended, and I continue to do the things I care about, like finishing my memoir," Biden wrote.
JILL BIDEN SAYS FORMER PRESIDENT WILL LIVE WITH STAGE 4 CANCER 'FOR THE REST OF HIS LIFE,' HAS SLOWED DOWN
President Joe Biden speaks at the White House in Washington, D.C. (Reuters)
He also thanked the doctors, nurses and other medical professionals who have treated him, saying their "skill, dedication, and compassion mean so much."
Biden used much of the message to urge men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors, pointing to the dramatically higher survival rate when the disease is detected early.
CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’

Joe Biden continues radiation therapy for Stage 4 prostate cancer that has metastasized to bone, with aides saying the 83-year-old former president remains active and engaged. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images)
"Talk to your doctors. Ask the hard questions. Do it for yourself, and do it for the people who love you," Biden wrote.

Biden said men at average risk should begin discussing prostate cancer screening with their doctors around age 50, while Black men and those with a family history should begin those conversations earlier.
SIMPLE SITTING CHANGE LINKED TO LOWER RISK OF CANCER DEATH, STUDY FINDS

The American Cancer Society recommends discussing screening at age 50 for average-risk men, age 45 for Black men and certain men with a family history, and age 40 for some men at even higher risk. (iStock)
The American Cancer Society recommends discussing screening at age 50 for average-risk men, age 45 for Black men and certain men with a family history, and age 40 for some men at even higher risk.
Biden’s office announced in May 2025 that the former president had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had metastasized to his bones.
JOE BIDEN'S CANCER HAS SPREAD FURTHER, LEAVING HIM IN 'VERY PAINFUL' CONDITION, HUNTER REVEALS
Former President Joe Biden shared this picture of him and Jill Biden after it was announced he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. (X/JoeBiden)

The diagnosis came after Biden experienced increasing urinary symptoms and doctors discovered a prostate nodule. His office said at the time that the cancer had a Gleason score of 9, Grade Group 5, but was hormone-sensitive, allowing for effective management.
Biden later underwent radiation therapy and completed that course of treatment last fall.
CANCER SURVIVORS SAW MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS IN SLEEP AND WELL-BEING WITH ONE WEEKLY PRACTICE
Biden closed Tuesday's message by thanking those who have continued to pray for him and his family. (Grant Baldwin/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Biden’s office for additional comment on his current health, treatment and prognosis.
Biden closed Tuesday's message by thanking those who have continued to pray for him and his family.

"It’s my hope and prayer that by sharing our experience and being part of this important conversation, we can help save lives," he wrote. "And no matter what, keep the faith. God bless you."Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and Robert McGreevy contributed to this reporting.

title: Drug developed for lung disease may slow biological aging in surprising ‘bonus’
summary: Rentosertib, an AI-discovered drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, made patients appear three to four years biologically younger in a clinical trial.
story: A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, first author Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD, founder and co-CEO of Insilico Medicine, told Fox News Digital.
A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, researchers say.
In a small clinical study, patients who took rentosertib – developed by Insilico Medicine in Massachusetts – showed changes in blood proteins that made them appear biologically younger.
Several tests estimated that after treatment, the patients were biologically about three to four years younger.
EATING COMMON DAIRY FOOD EVERY DAY MAY SLOW BIOLOGICAL AGING, STUDY SUGGESTS

"There is a promising trend in age reversal in addition to treating the disease, and it came as a bonus for disease treatment," first author Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD, founder and co-CEO of Insilico Medicine, told Fox News Digital.
A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, researchers say. (iStock)
"It basically means that you are predicted to be younger using a validated set of aging clocks. We don’t know what that means yet."
The results were published in Nature Biotechnology and presented Monday at the Nature conference at Sorbonne University in Paris.
ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION
The researchers caution, however, that this does not yet prove the drug can actually reverse aging or help people live longer.
"It’s early days," Zhavoronkov noted. "The drug is still investigational."
What is rentosertib?

Rentosertib is an experimental drug, discovered with the help of artificial intelligence, that is being developed to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a serious disease that causes scarring in the lungs.
In an unexpected outcome, the drug was found to change patterns of proteins in the blood in ways that made patients appear an average of three to four years younger, in one case up to six years.

Rentosertib is an experimental drug, discovered with the help of artificial intelligence, that is being developed to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a serious disease that causes scarring in the lungs. (iStock)
Six different aging tests showed the same general pattern, with patients who took rentosertib "scoring" biologically younger than those who received a placebo.
The strongest effect was seen after four weeks in patients taking 30 mg of the drug twice a day.
LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS

When researchers compared the results with data from more than 55,000 people in the UK Biobank, they found that the drug changed several blood proteins in the opposite direction from what is normally seen with aging.
The researchers also found signs that the drug may affect aging at the cellular level, as it changed processes involved in how cells function and respond to damage.
"Everybody agrees that living longer should be a fundamental human right for everyone."
Zhavoronkov said the company's approach uses AI to search for what he calls "molecular criminals" — biological targets that may contribute to both aging and disease.

The study – which was published in Nature Biotechnology – involved researchers from Insilico Medicine as well as Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, the Broad Institute, RWTH Aachen University, Peking University and Westlake University.
Study limitations
Zhavoronkov stressed that the findings are preliminary. "This is a pilot," he said. "It is early [and] exploratory."
The study had some limitations, including the small sample size – just 42 patients were analyzed over a 12-week period.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The participants all had IPF, which can change many of the same proteins researchers use to measure biological aging. This means it’s possible that the improvements in the participants’ lung disease was related to the changes in blood proteins.

Larger and longer trials – including healthy older adults and populations without IPF – are needed to determine whether the drug truly has anti-aging effects and whether they could lead to better health. (iStock)
The findings don’t prove that the drug actually slows aging, keeps people healthier longer or extends their lives, the researchers acknowledged.
The results were based only on changes in proteins in their blood, and do not yet support the use of rentosertib as an anti-aging treatment.
Risks and side effects
The risks and side effects associated with rentosertib were found to be "manageable," according to Dr. Carol Ann Satler, senior vice president of clinical development for Insilico Medicine.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
The most common potential side effects included mild diarrhea, slightly lower potassium levels in the blood and temporary increases in liver enzymes.
The drug was found to change patterns of proteins in the blood in ways that made patients appear an average of three to four years younger, in one case up to six years. (Insilico Medicine)
"Once you stop the drug, essentially, they return to normal," Satler told Fox News Digital.
In the next trial, the doctor said, "We'll be looking to adjust the doses of the drug based on the side effect profile so that people can stay on it longer."
Looking ahead
Rentosertib has now progressed into a year-long phase 3 study of more than 300 patients in China, according to Insilico.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Larger and longer trials – including healthy older adults and populations without IPF – are needed to determine whether the drug truly has anti-aging effects and whether they could lead to better health.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
While more research lies ahead, Zhavoronkov said the findings have given him more confidence to continue pursuing drugs that could target both age-related diseases and aging itself.
"Everybody agrees that living longer should be a fundamental human right for everyone," he said.

title: 105-year-old credits ‘the good Lord’ for her long life: ‘Every day is a blessing’
summary: Blynda Vidock of Baytown, Texas, still lives independently at 105 and credits faith, athletics and eating well for her remarkable longevity.
story: Dr. Annu Navani, chief medical officer at Le Reve Wellness, revelas why people should focus on adding healthy years to life — not chasing immortality.
A Texas woman who just turned 105 attributes her long life to "the good Lord."
While Blynda Vidock's faith may have played an important role in her longevity, the Baytown resident has also followed many of the habits that experts say can contribute to a longer, healthier life.

"The good Lord put me here for so many years, and it’s His life through me," she told FOX 26 Houston at her recent birthday celebration. "But I’ve always been very athletic, played tennis, swam all my life and ate good food."
GEORGIA WOMAN CELEBRATES 112TH BIRTHDAY, REVEALS HER SECRET TO A LONG LIFE
Vidock joked that she preaches to her children, grandchildren and "great-grands" to eat healthier, but said, "They still eat junk food!"
"We live faster nowadays," she said. "We used to have time to sit down and have a meal together."
Blynda Vidock celebrated more than a century of life with loved ones, joking at her birthday gathering that she had been made "queen for a day." (FOX 26 Houston KRIV)

Vidock was born in 1921 and grew up in West Palm Beach, Florida. While working for $15 a week at a bank in West Palm Beach, she crossed paths with big-name movie stars Clark Gable and Fred Astaire, and also recalled encountering a young John F. Kennedy.
She met Coast Guardsman Charles "Chuck" Vidock while volunteering with the USO during World War II. The two married and moved to Texas in 1946 and spent decades traveling the world together.
LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS
Vidock is "completely sharp, independent and full of stories from a century of living," according to the report.
A video from her birthday party shows the centenarian walking around and chatting animatedly with the many friends and family members who gathered to honor her.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It’s wonderful to have you people here, and I don’t know if I’m supposed to dance or sing or get up on the table," she said. "I think I've been made queen for a day, and I've got my 15 minutes of fame, so you better enjoy it because it won't come again."
Every morning when she wakes up, Vidock said she wonders, "‘This is another day, Lord, why am I here?’" adding, "Every day is a blessing!"
Blynda Vidock celebrated her 105th birthday surrounded by friends and family in Texas. (FOX 26 Houston KRIV)
She said "the saddest part about getting old" is watching people lose their mental sharpness and credits "the good Lord" with allowing her to keep hers.
Vidock said a few simple habits have helped her live so long.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Living like you know you’re supposed to live, being kind to people, and everything in moderation helped, and I got blessed with good genes, but then I took care of my body," she said.
Expert tips to improve healthspan

Dr. Annu Navani, chief medical officer at Le Reve Wellness in San Jose, California, recently told Fox News Digital that longevity medicine is more about adding life to years than adding years to life.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Rather than splurging on costly biohacks, procedures or supplements, Navani recommends focusing on simple daily practices that can enhance quality of life.
Getting high-quality sleep — about seven hours a night for the average person — is necessary for people to perform optimally and has been linked to a healthier lifespan, the expert said.
Regular exercise can support physical and mental health as people age, and may also help with stress management, experts say. (iStock)

Managing stress is another key factor in healthy aging, according to Navani. Regular physical activity and social interaction — two other factors linked to longevity — can also help people keep stress in check, as can regular meditation.

Eating a nutritious diet that includes a variety of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, protein and dairy, while limiting added sugars and ultraprocessed foods, is another important component of healthy aging.

Longevity experts David Cravit and Larry Wolf, authors of "The SuperAging Workbook," previously told Fox News Digital that maintaining a positive attitude is the No. 1 factor linked to living a longer life.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"People with a positive attitude outlive people with a negative attitude because it reduces stress, which, in turn, reduces inflammation, and inflammation is the cause of most age-related diseases," Cravit said.
The authors also recommended setting and working toward new goals, building strong relationships and maintaining a sense of independence as people age.
Melissa Rudy and Angelica Stabile of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.
