title: Judge orders Alex Murdaugh murder retrial moved to nearby county
summary: Alex Murdaugh's double murder retrial moves to Sumter County after a judge ruled Colleton County's jury pool was too compromised for a fair trial.
story: During court testimony, witness Phil Barber refutes claims regarding a lack of affordable lodging near the Charleston County Courthouse. Barber explains that nine budget hotels in Mount Pleasant are only a 15-minute drive from the judicial facility. He also addresses parking accessibility and notes that weekend hotel price increases would not impact weekday court proceedings.
A South Carolina judge on Tuesday granted a request by Alex Murdaugh that the double-murder retrial for the disgraced attorney be relocated to a new venue.
Judge Debra McCaslin ruled that the trial will take place in Sumter County. Defense lawyers argued that Colleton County's jury pool was tainted by the highly covered original trial.

In her order, McCaslin wrote that Murdaugh can receive a fair trial in Sumter County, adding that it offers adequate security measures, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities to conduct proceedings.
ALEX MURDAUGH'S 'CHARLESTON OR BUST' PRAYER SHOT DOWN BY PROSECUTORS IN FIGHT OVER 'HOLY CITY' RETRIAL

Alex Murdaugh attends a judicial hearing on Monday, June 29, 2026, at the Marc H. Westbrook Judicial Center in Lexington, South Carolina. Murdaugh will be retried in the June 7, 2021, shooting deaths of his wife and son, after his original conviction was overturned due to jury tampering. (Tracy Glantz/The State via Pool)

"The judge considered several factors including the financial impact on Colleton County, the convenience of witnesses, courthouse security, transportation and security of Murdaugh, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities," the order states.
Murdaugh's attorneys had suggested Charleston or Richland County courthouses for the venue transfer before McCaslin made her ruling.
ALEX MURDAUGH RETURNS TO COURT AS DEFENSE ARGUES FOR RETRIAL MOVE AFTER CLERK SCANDAL POISONED JURY POOL
Fox News Digital has reached out to Murdaugh's attorneys and prosecutors.

Murdaugh was granted a new trial after the South Carolina Supreme Court determined his right to a fair proceeding was violated when it found that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced jurors during his 2023 murder trial.
ALEX MURDAUGH WINS NEW TRIAL AFTER COURT CLERK ALLEGEDLY TOLD JURORS NOT TO BE 'FOOLED' BY DEFENSE

Alex Murdaugh arrives for a judicial hearing on June 29, 2026, at the Marc H. Westbrook Judicial Center in Lexington, South Carolina. A judge o Tuesday ordered his retrial be moved to Sumter County. Murdaugh will be retried for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife and son, after his original conviction was overturned due to jury tampering. (Tracy Glantz/The State via Pool)
As a result, the court unanimously overturned his 2023 convictions and two life sentences.
Murdaugh is charged with murder and weapons offenses for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife, Maggie, and 22-year-old son, Paul, at their family estate.

At his 2023 trial, Murdaugh admitted to misleading investigators about his location shortly before his wife and son were shot, but he has consistently denied killing either of them.

title: Lindsay Clancy juror admitted 'reasonable doubt' but still refused insanity verdict, foreperson says
summary: Three Lindsay Clancy jurors say a lone holdout admitted having reasonable doubt but still refused to deliver a not guilty by insanity verdict.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports on the mistrial declared in the Lindsay Clancy murder case after a Plymouth, Mass., jury deadlocked following about 40 hours of deliberation over six and a half days.

Three people who served on the jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are speaking publicly for the first time after last week's mistrial, saying a lone holdout prevented the panel from reaching a unanimous verdict.
The jurors, including the foreperson, said one juror acknowledged having reasonable doubt but still refused to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, according to interviews with NBC10 Boston.
The mistrial came after days of deliberations in the closely watched case against Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children in January 2023.

Clancy admitted to the killings but pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, arguing she was suffering from severe mental illness at the time. Prosecutors maintained she was criminally responsible for the deaths.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL
Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)
"He admitted he had reasonable doubt and I started filling out the forms, I was so excited," the foreperson told NBC10 Boston.
But the foreperson said the juror then added, "But I'm still not going to say that she's not guilty by reason of insanity."

The foreperson also told the station she wrote the note to the judge raising concerns that one juror had expressed reasonable doubt but would not agree to a verdict. The three jurors said they became frustrated with the holdout during deliberations, claiming he refused to consider the views of the rest of the panel.
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Lindsay Clancy sits at the defense table during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., Wednesday, August 5, 2026. (David L. Ryan/Pool)
NBC10 Boston reported it attempted to contact the juror identified by the others as the holdout but had not received a response.
Lindsay Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, speaks outside the courthouse after the third day of deliberations in her murder trial on Aug. 31, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A judge declared a mistrial last week after jurors informed the court they were hopelessly deadlocked following several days of deliberations.
It remains unclear whether prosecutors will seek to retry the case.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Virginia county to pay up to $2K to families with primary wage earner detained by ICE
summary: Arlington County approved $50,000 to support immigrant families whose primary wage earner has been detained amid Trump administration enforcement efforts.
story: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents arrest more than 1,300 illegal immigrants in a massive Washington, D.C. area sweep known as Operation Safe Community. 'Fox & Friends' co-hosts break down the arrests of MS-13 gang members and a suspect tied to student fentanyl overdoses. The operation highlights growing concerns over border security and local community safety.
Leaders in one Virginia county approved a program last week to set aside $50,000 to support families in which the primary wage earner has been detained by federal immigration authorities.

In a special Sept. 2 meeting, the Arlington County Board voted 4-0 to appropriate the funds, which will be distributed by Arlington Thrive, which describes itself as a "key component of the social safety net" in partnership with the county government.

Under the program, eligible families will receive up to $2,000 for those who have lost the primary wage earner. Arlington Thrive aims to assist between 25 to 30 families, according to the board's agenda.
HOW GUARANTEED INCOME ADVOCATES STRIVE TO TURN CASH ASSISTANCE INTO POLICY AFTER COVID-RELIEF FUNDS DRIED UP

Federal immigration authorities make an arrest in Arlington, Va., in February. Arlington County leaders recently voted to set aside $50,000 to give families up to $2,000 if the primary wage earner was detained by immigration authorities. (ICE)
"We stand with our immigrant families, and we will not stop doing so," Board Chair Matt de Ferranti said. "We are valuing the families of those that have been displaced and removed."
The move was in response to the Trump administration's illegal immigration enforcement efforts in the Washington, D.C., area in recent months.

"Ensuring that we take care of our community and our residents and our people does mean making sure that we have emergency assistance available for what is probably one of the most challenging situations that you could possibly face," Board Vice Chair Maureen Coffey said. "I'm very proud of us for doing this."
SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW
Arlington County Board of Supervisors, from left, Julius D. "JD" Spain Sr., Susan Cunningham, Takis Karantonis, Board Chair Matt de Ferranti and Vice Chair Maureen Coffey. (Arlington County)
The funds will be distributed to families in the form of debit cards and checks.
Elizabeth Matlock, a staff member in the county manager’s office who is coordinating the effort, said the organization is ready to begin issuing funds.
"Thrive is eager to get started with this project," she said.
The vote came as officers with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) quietly made more than 1,300 arrests of illegal immigrants over 14 days in the Washington, D.C., suburbs last month.

title: Mom ‘very invested’ in Lindsay Clancy case hires Casey Anthony attorney after allegedly killing son: docs
summary: Corie Walsh allegedly texted friends about the Lindsay Clancy murder trial just hours before her 2-year-old son Barrett was found dead in Frankfort.
story: Andrea Lyon said Corie Walsh’s defense will challenge the first-degree murder charges after a judge denied her request for release to a locked hospital setting.

A Frankfort, Illinois, mother accused of killing her 2-year-old son had been discussing the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial with friends just hours before the boy was found dead, court documents allege, and has hired one of Casey Anthony's former attorneys to defend her.

Corie A. Walsh, 38, later told officers she killed her son because she believed he was the "devil" and the "anti-Christ," a petition seeking to deny her pretrial release obtained by Fox 32 in Chicago states.

Walsh has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her son, Barrett Walsh. The filing mentions her interest in the Clancy case but does not allege that it was connected to Barrett’s death.
ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY
Walsh’s attorney, Andrea Lyon, said she was "psychotic" and rejected any connection between her client’s interest in the Clancy case and the alleged killing.

Corie A. Walsh, 38, in a booking photo provided by law enforcement. Prosecutors are asking a judge to deny her pretrial release following the death of her 2-year-old son. (Will County Detention Facility)
"They are not correlated at all. It’s just accidental," Lyon said, calling speculation that Walsh’s actions were a copycat crime "baseless and cruel."
Court documents show Frankfort police officers were called to a home in the 22700 block of Brook Stone Court just after 4 p.m. Sept. 1 for a report of an injured child.
Upon arrival, officers found a neighbor performing CPR on Barrett after she reportedly discovered the toddler hanging from a basement rafter with his feet off the ground.
SUBURBAN ILLINOIS BOY DIES IN SUSPECTED DOMESTIC HOMICIDE AS NEIGHBORS FEAR ANOTHER LINDSAY CLANCY CASE

The neighbor brought Barrett down, laid him on the floor and attempted CPR while calling 911, later telling police the boy was cold and had no pulse. Barrett was pronounced dead at the scene, and a preliminary autopsy determined he died of asphyxia caused by strangulation, according to the filing.

Walsh’s three other children were unharmed, including an infant who was in the house at the time and two school-aged children who returned home around the time Barrett was found. Her husband was traveling out of state when the incident occurred and flew home that evening.
Corie Walsh, right, poses with her husband and children inside a church. Walsh faces three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her 2-year-old son, Barrett. (Facebook/Corie Walsh)
While officers were at the house, they were directed to an upstairs master bathroom where Walsh was reportedly trying to harm herself.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN

The petition states Walsh was lying fully dressed in a bathtub surrounded by bloody water while a neighbor held a towel against her left inner thigh. The neighbor told investigators she had disarmed Walsh of a knife and thrown it into a sink.
Police recovered the knife into evidence while documenting cuts on Walsh’s wrists and thighs, court documents state.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Corie Walsh, top left, pictured with her husband and children wearing matching holiday pajamas on a couch. (Facebook/Corie Walsh)

The neighbor told investigators that Walsh asked why she had taken the knife from her because she was trying to kill herself. Walsh then said "Bear" was in the basement – referencing a known nickname for Barrett, the petition notes.
LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY
While hospitalized, Walsh made additional statements to investigators describing how she killed the toddler, which prosecutors noted were consistent with the physical evidence.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Witnesses told investigators Walsh had recently become "very invested" in the Clancy murder trial, which involved a Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children.
Police tape surrounds the Frankfort, Illinois, home where a 2-year-old boy died. (FOX 32 Chicago)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Walsh allegedly discussed the Clancy case in a group text message with friends as recently as 12:30 p.m. Sept. 1 – roughly three and a half hours before Barrett was found. Her cellphone was recovered from the bathroom, and forensic analysis of the device was ongoing as of Sept. 3.
SEND US A TIP
Prosecutors are asking a judge to deny Walsh pretrial release, arguing that she poses a real and present threat to her husband and her three surviving children.

Walsh faces three counts of first-degree murder, with prosecutors outlining different legal theories regarding her intent. Because Barrett was 2 years old, a conviction carries a mandatory sentence of 60 to 100 years in prison without the possibility of early release.
Walsh remains hospitalized at Silver Cross Hospital and is expected to be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility once medically released.
ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY
Walsh’s defense team includes attorney Lyon, who previously represented Anthony. In 2011, Anthony was acquitted in the death of her 2-year-old daughter, Caylee, whose death remains unsolved.
A jury found Anthony guilty of lying to law enforcement but not guilty of first-degree murder, aggravated manslaughter or aggravated child abuse.
The Will County State’s Attorney’s Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

At a detention hearing Tuesday, a judge denied Walsh’s request for pretrial release to a locked hospital setting. Lyon said the defense was disappointed but would continue investigating the case while Walsh recovers from her wounds.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Lyon said the defense will argue that Walsh was psychotic and that the charges do not amount to first-degree murder.
"She was psychotic. And this is not a first-degree murder," she told reporters.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
The defense may seek pretrial release again, Lyon said.

The case remains pending in Will County Circuit Court.

title: United flight attendant makes quick save, catching baby that was about to fall from 'exhausted' mom's lap

story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A flight attendant aboard a United Airlines flight sprang into action when an exhausted mother dozed off and her baby began slipping from her lap — catching the child before offering to hold the baby so the weary mom could get some much-needed rest.

Passenger John Frehse shared the touching encounter on Instagram, praising flight attendant Monique Harris for her quick response aboard United flight 3486 from Newark, New Jersey, to Grand Rapids, Michigan.
"United should be very proud," Frehse wrote, adding that the new mother had fallen asleep when her baby was "about to fall out of her lap."

Passenger John Frehse shared the touching encounter between flight attendant Monique Harris and family on Instagram. (Instagram/ woodylovestravel)

Frehse tagged United CEO Scott Kirby in the post and said he has flown more than 2 million miles with the airline.
"She is an A+ employee," he wrote. "Take note!!!"
RETIRED POLICE CHIEF HELPS SUBDUE PASSENGER AFTER ALLEGED MIDAIR OUTBURST OVER ALCOHOL CUTOFF
Flight attendant Monique Harris was praised for her quick response aboard United flight 3486 from Newark, New Jersey, to Grand Rapids, Michigan. (Facebook/Monique Unique Harris)
Harris responded to the praise in the comments, saying she was moved by the attention the moment had received.
"I’m in tears," she wrote, adding, "I never do anything for recognition."
Harris said she "had no idea that being my normal natural self would grow into such a priceless moment," and thanked Frehse and others for the comments.
Republic Airways, which operates flights for United and other airlines, praised Harris in an email to Fox News Digital.

United Airlines planes are seen at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) in Newark, New Jersey, Nov. 3, 2025. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

title: Victims identified in fatal Amazon cargo jet crash at Miami airport
summary: Five victims were identified after Amazon Air Flight 7598 overran the Miami International Airport runway, crashing into vehicles beyond the pavement.
story: Former NTSB investigator Dr. Alan Diehl joins ‘Fox News Live’ to analyze possible factors behind an Amazon cargo plane’s deadly runway overrun at Miami International Airport.
Authorities in Miami identified the five people killed when an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, crashing into vehicles and catching on fire.
Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz released the names of the victims in a news conference on Tuesday.
They were identified as: Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, 53; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and 47-year-old Javierkys Reyes Quevedo.

title: Smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch to retire amid allegations of far-left woke messaging at museums
summary: Lonnie Bunch III announced his retirement from the Smithsonian Institution amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over museum leadership.
story: Laura Ingraham exposes the left-wing curators behind radical exhibits at the Smithsonian. Historian Dr. Jody Edward Ginn joins 'The Ingraham Angle' to discuss the bias and exclusion of conservative perspectives in national museums.

The head of the Smithsonian Institution announced his retirement Tuesday, stepping down amid an escalating clash with the Trump administration over the leadership and direction of the nation’s museums.

Lonnie Bunch III, who has led the Smithsonian since 2019 and was the founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, said he will leave the post by the end of the year.

"It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian," Bunch said in a press release. "I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together."
SMITHSONIAN SHOWDOWN INTENSIFIES AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ISSUES A STARK NEW WARNING
Lonnie Bunch III speaks during the Smithsonian Latino Museum Reception on June 16, 2022, in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for Smithsonian Latino Museum)
"I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward," he added.

Bunch’s departure comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of the Smithsonian, accusing its leadership of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history and raising concerns about potential violations of federal nondiscrimination law.

In a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior, the administration said the Smithsonian leadership’s "institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law," including allegedly creating a hostile work environment and allocating opportunities, funding and other benefits based on race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics.
The Smithsonian, the nation's largest museum and research complex, is at the center of a White House campaign to overhaul its presentation of American history. (J. David Ake/Getty Images)
The letter did not include specific evidence of illegal activity, and the Department of the Interior did not provide further information when previously reached for comment by Fox News Digital.

The administration warned that federal agencies could withdraw certain forms of support if its concerns are not addressed, saying an "appropriate response" from the Smithsonian "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is being called out for being 'ideologically captured' and presenting woke revisionist history on the weekend of America's 250th birthday. (Kevin Carter/Getty)
The pressure follows a 2025 executive order directing officials to seek the removal of what the administration called "improper ideology" from the Smithsonian.
SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

Bunch became the Smithsonian’s 14th secretary in June 2019, making him the first African American and first historian to hold the position. He previously led the creation of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, serving as its founding director from 2005 through its opening in 2016.
Bunch first joined the Smithsonian in 1978 and has spent nearly four decades at the institution, apart from a period when he served as president of the Chicago Historical Society.
The Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025. (Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian, praised Bunch’s tenure and said the institution would work with him to ensure a smooth transition.

title: Bryan Kohberger's bid to oust judge and undo guilty plea moves forward with new court date set
summary: Bryan Kohberger's new lawyers challenge Judge Steven Hippler's impartiality as the convicted Idaho murders killer fights to undo his guilty plea.
story: Legal maneuvers escalate in the Idaho student murders case as Bryan Kohberger attempts to disqualify Judge Steven Hippler. Fox News legal analyst Gregg Jarrett breaks down the defense's strategy.

Convicted Idaho student murderer Bryan Kohberger will return to court on Oct. 15 for a hearing on his motion to remove Judge Steven Hippler from his case as he seeks to undo his guilty plea through a process known as post-conviction relief.

Kohberger, 31, filed a handwritten petition in July, telling the court he had ineffective counsel, that his guilty plea was "not knowingly or voluntarily entered because it was induced by unkept promises" and that it was "not voluntarily entered because of threats asserted by petitioner's (Kohberger's) legal counsel."
The court appointed attorney Greg Rauch, of Moscow, Idaho, and private defense lawyer Jason Goldman, of New York, later joined Kohberger's new legal team.
BRYAN KOHBERGER APPOINTED NEW LAWYER AFTER IDAHO MURDERS CASE COSTS TAXPAYERS OVER $8 MILLION

Bryan Kohberger appears at the Ada County Courthouse for his sentencing hearing on July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho. Kohberger pleaded guilty in exchange for being spared the death penalty for the stabbing of four University of Idaho students nearly three years ago. (Kyle Green-Pool/Getty Images)
His new lawyers are expected to file an amended petition by Nov. 13 — four years to the day after the murders.

"We think the [amended petition] and evidentiary hearing will naturally address some of the outstanding and unanswered questions," Goldman told Fox News Digital last week. "That said, the main priority right now is to scrutinize the constitutional issues surrounding Bryan's plea."
BRYAN KOHBERGER’S 2027 HEARING IS NOT GUARANTEED AS IDAHO SEEKS QUICK DISMISSAL

Judge Steven Hippler of Idaho's 4th Judicial District in Ada County rejected the latest attempt by Bryan Kohberger's defense to drop the death penalty as a possible sentence if a jury convicts him of killing four University of Idaho students in 2022. (Katherine Jones/Idaho Statesman/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Kohberger pleaded guilty on July 2, 2025, to four counts of first-degree murder and a burglary charge for the stabbing deaths of 21-year-olds Madison Mogen and Kaylee Goncalves as well as 20-year-olds Xana Kernodle and Ethan Chapin.

On July 23, 2025, Hippler sentenced him to four consecutive terms of life in prison without the possibility of parole, plus another 10 years, as part of a plea deal in which Kohberger avoided the death penalty.
KOHBERGER DEFENSE EXPERT WANTS HIS LAWYERS UNDER OATH AFTER KILLER CITES FINDINGS IN BID TO UNDO GUILTY PLEA

Madison Mogen, top left, smiles on the shoulders of her best friend, Kaylee Goncalves, as they pose with Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle, and two other housemates in Goncalves' final Instagram post, shared the day before the four students were stabbed to death. (@kayleegoncalves/Instagram)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Rauch filed a 22-page motion to have the judge disqualified on Aug. 27, questioning Hippler's impartiality after he declined to give Kohberger's former defense team more time when they said they were not finished with discovery as the expected trial date approached last year.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Kohberger pleaded guilty weeks before it would have taken place. Rauch also took issue with some of the language Hippler used to describe his client at sentencing: "someone in whom the Court could identify nothing remaining that was 'good or intrinsically human.'"

Judge Steven Hippler speaks at the sentencing hearing of Bryan Kohberger at the Ada County Courthouse, Wednesday, July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho, for brutally stabbing four University of Idaho students to death nearly three years ago. (Kyle Green/AP Photo, Pool)

In a separate order last week, Hippler gave Kohberger's lawyers until Sept. 10 to explain why the court should seal a supplemental filing attached to their motion to disqualify him from the case.

They've also been ordered to share the confidential filing with the Latah County Prosecutor's office. It has not been made public and will remain sealed at least until the deadline — likely longer after a justification is given.

title: Third Burning Man festivalgoer dies during final days of annual Nevada desert gathering
summary: A third Burning Man festivalgoer died while being transported to a Reno-area hospital, following two earlier deaths at Black Rock City during this year's gathering.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A third Burning Man festivalgoer has died after being transported to a hospital, authorities said, marking the latest death connected to the Nevada desert gathering after two men died at the festival within roughly 48 hours.

Pershing County Sheriff Jerry Allen told Fox News Digital in an email that his office had received information about a third participant who died while being transported from the festival to a Reno-area hospital.

Allen said he did not have additional information about the circumstances of the death, because it occurred outside his jurisdiction. He referred questions to the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office and Washoe County Medical Examiner’s Office. Fox News Digital has reached out to both for comment.
TWO MEN DIE WITHIN 24 HOURS AT BURNING MAN AS TENS OF THOUSANDS GATHER IN THE NEVADA DESERT
Burning Man attendees sample the art at Black Rock City during a dust storm on Sept. 2, 2026. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Authorities are also awaiting autopsy and toxicology results for the two men who died at Burning Man earlier in the festival.
Allen said his office typically sees about one death each year at the festival.

The first death was reported Thursday at Rampart, the temporary hospital at Burning Man, according to a Pershing County Sheriff’s Office news release. Festival organizers described the man as in his mid-50s.

Deputies found Sampson Tshombe dead at the hospital after he was found on a street at the festival, the sheriff’s office said. Emergency personnel performed CPR for several minutes before a doctor pronounced him dead.
Burning Man attendees watch as the Man structure burns as part of the annual celebration at Black Rock City, Nevada, on Sept. 5, 2026. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Investigators found no external signs of foul play. Tshombe was taken to the Washoe County Medical Examiner’s Office for an autopsy and toxicology screening because authorities did not have his medical history.
BURNING MAN MURDER MYSTERY DEEPENS AS NEW DETAILS EMERGE 1 YEAR AFTER DESERT FESTIVAL KILLING
On Saturday, deputies were again called to Black Rock City, the temporary city built each year for Burning Man, after festival organizers said a 60-year-old man died.
Craigh Mann was found dead in a trailer he shared with his significant other at about 3:17 p.m., according to the sheriff’s office. Investigators found no outward signs of foul play.

Mann was also taken to the Washoe County Medical Examiner’s Office for an autopsy and toxicology screening. The sheriff’s office said investigators did not have his medical history or other information that could explain his death.
The autopsy and toxicology results for both men are expected in six to eight weeks. The sheriff’s office said it would not release further information until it receives the results.

A Vantor satellite image shows the center of the Burning Man festival site in Black Rock City, Nev., on Aug. 31, 2026, with its distinctive circular layout and numerous temporary structures. (DigitalGlobe/Getty Images)
Burning Man organizers previously said their "thoughts and deepest condolences" were with Mann’s family, friends, campmates and others affected by his death.

"The safety and well-being of our community and staff remain our highest priority," organizers said after the first death, adding that support resources were available around the clock in Black Rock City.

The annual Burning Man festival began Aug. 30 in Nevada’s Black Rock Desert and concluded Monday. The gathering can draw as many as 80,000 people, known as "burners," and is best known for the burning of a large wooden effigy.

title: Lindsay Clancy attorney Kevin Reddington signals he's open to a deal, hopes DA will 'revisit' case
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney says he hopes prosecutors will "revisit" the case and signals openness to a plea deal after the murder mistrial.
story: Criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno weighs in on the Lindsay Clancy murder case following a mistrial. They discuss the potential for a plea deal on 'Fox & Friends Weekend'. They debate whether a second trial is likely or if a plea bargain will resolve the charges after the deaths of her three children.
Lindsay Clancy's attorney signaled Tuesday he would be open to a plea deal, saying he hopes the district attorney will "revisit" the case now that her murder trial has ended in a mistrial.

Kevin Reddington's comments come after Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Friday in Clancy's murder case after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict, ending in an alleged 11-1 divide.
Reddington argued that the one holdout juror acknowledged doubt, but was refusing to properly apply the judge's instructions on reasonable doubt.
Clancy, 36, faced three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children — Cora, Dawson and Callan, all under age 6 — who were found strangled at the family's home in January 2023.
PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL

Lindsay Clancy and Kevin Reddington listen to Judge Sullivan ask the jury to continue deliberations during Clancy's murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)
In an interview on "Good Morning America" on Tuesday, Reddington said he hopes the two sides can "work something out" when asked about a possible plea agreement.

"I‘m willing to listen to Tim. I‘ve known Tim for 30 years. He‘s a very hard charging prosecutor," Reddington said, referring to Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz. "I hope, however, after sitting through this trial and seeing the evidence that was presented from the government as well as from the defense, that he would revisit that issue and hopefully would be able to work something out that would be acceptable to both sides."
Reddington previously said that prosecutors weren't open to a plea deal while talking to reporters on Sept. 2. He later said "bring it" when asked about the possibility of a retrial.
"There's no plea bargaining, there's nothing Cruz wants, his triple homicide convictions, consecutive life sentences," Reddington said.
LINDSAY CLANCY JURY RECAP: DAY 5 ENDS WITH NO VERDICT AFTER RARE INSTRUCTION
Lindsay Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, speaks outside the courthouse after the third day of deliberations in her murder trial on Aug. 31, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
Reddington also appealed to President Donald Trump for a potential pardon. However, Trump has no authority to issue a pardon since Clancy's murder trial is being handled in state court, not federal.
"Mr. President, I would hope that you would consider this young lady, the type of person she is, what she‘s been through, and consider a pardon," Reddington said.
Reddington also softened his criticism of the lone holdout juror, whom he had previously accused of having an "agenda" and of having "robbed" the other jurors of their time.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

"I at the end of the case made statements to the effect that I was upset," he said. "I would defend that individual‘s right to be a holdout for forever. That‘s part of our judicial system. And I respect that. And I would certainly defend his right to do that."
SEND US A TIP

"What I was upset about was, after that lengthy trial and the work that everyone put into this case, including these jurors that spent literally almost two months away from their home, their job, their family, where a gentleman had an opinion, not that he was sticking like the movie '12 Angry Men,' but in fact he had agreed, according to the note from the forelady, that he had doubt, but he would not apply the law of reasonable doubt as presented by the judge. That's not right. And that's why I was upset," Reddington explained.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
WATCH: Patrick Clancy declines to answer questions after mistrial

In a statement to Fox News Digital on Tuesday, Patrick Clancy's attorney, Howard Cooper, said his client and his family have been the target of a "relentless, escalating and destructive defamation campaign" and warned that those behind it could face legal consequences.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Patrick Clancy leaves his apartment building in East Midtown in New York City, NY, Thursday, September 3, 2026. (Elder Ordonez/InStar for Fox News Digital)

"Over the past months, Patrick Clancy and his family have been subjected to a relentless, escalating and destructive defamation campaign. This campaign of misinformation has been launched and promoted by minor celebrities, so-called influencers and outright conspiracy theorists who appear intent on boosting their own social media profiles and potential profit by publishing what they know to be outright falsehoods that Patrick was somehow involved in the death of his young children and other vile claims," Cooper said.

Patrick Clancy and Rachel Danis hold hands as they walk through East Midtown in New York City, NY, Wednesday, September 2, 2026. (Elder Ordonez/InStar for Fox News Digital)

"Enough is enough — this spread of blatant and baseless falsehoods must stop. Those responsible should understand that there will be consequences, and every appropriate measure will be pursued to hold them accountable, including legally.  Law enforcement has been notified," Patrick Clancy's attorney added.

title: 4 Florida family members found dead after small plane goes down off the Bahamas
summary: U.S. Coast Guard joined the search for a plane carrying four Florida family members that authorities believe "crash-landed" near Andros Island in the Bahamas.
story: A plane carrying pilot Mario Lamar, 80, his wife Lili, 79, and two of their grandchildren, Sofia Sosa, 28, and Christian Sosa, 22, disappeared on Labor Day after departing Great Harbour Cay for Opa-locka, Florida. (Credit: Silvia Larrieu)
Four Florida family members have been found deceased after a plane they were traveling on went down off the coast of the Bahamas, a family member said Tuesday.
The U.S. Coast Guard had joined the search for the aircraft that authorities in the Bahamas believe "crash-landed" in the ocean after departing from Great Harbour Cay on Monday.

Pilot Mario Lamar, 80, his wife Lili, 79, and two of their grandchildren, Sofia Sosa, 28, and Christian Sosa, 22, were identified by family as those on board the PA-34 Piper five-seater aircraft that was heading to Opa-locka, Florida.

"It is with profound sadness that we confirm all four of our family members have been found deceased. The search and recovery mission was conducted alongside family members and civilians who answered our call for help. Our relatives ultimately located our loved ones and had to bring them aboard their own vessels," Silvia Larrieu, the niece of Mario and Lamar, said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

"We are now in communication and working with the U.S. Coast Guard to bring our loved ones home safely and with dignity. We are deeply grateful to everyone who supported us, searched alongside us, and kept our family in their prayers. We respectfully ask for privacy as we mourn this unimaginable loss," she added.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY

Pilot Mario Lamar, 80, his wife Lili Lamar, 79, and two of their grandchildren, 22-year-old Christian Sosa and 28-year-old Sofia Sosa, were identified by a family member as those onboard the plane. (Courtesy Silvia Larrieu)
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Royal Bahamas Police Force for comment.

Larrieu told the Miami Herald that the family was coming home to Florida after visiting a vacation property in Great Harbour Cay over Labor Day weekend and that "they’ve spent their whole life going there." Data from the website FlightAware showed the plane descended from 10,000 feet to 3,700 feet in about three minutes before vanishing from radar.
Great Harbour Cay in the Bahamas is seen from an airplane during a flight from Spain to the Caribbean. (NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Larrieu also said to the newspaper that Mario Lamar had years of experience as a pilot and always kept the aircraft in "pristine" shape.

U.S. Coast Guard Southeast said Monday it was assisting authorities in the Bahamas "following a report of a downed aircraft with four souls on board approx 15 mi off Andros Island," with a Coast Guard HC-144 Ocean Sentry airplane joining the search.
The Royal Bahamas Police Force said it received a report around 2:20 p.m. on Monday "that an aircraft may have gone down in the waters off Red Bays."
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY ONBOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE

A U.S. Coast Guard HC-144 Ocean Sentry medium-range surveillance plane from Air Station Cape Cod flies over the Atlantic Ocean in Newport, R.I., on April 4, 2026. One of these planes has joined the search for the missing aircraft off the coast of the Bahamas. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

It added that air traffic control "confirmed that a PA-34 Piper five-seater aircraft, bearing tail number N212ML, departed Great Harbour Cay at approximately 11:12 a.m., en route to Opa-locka, Florida."
"Air traffic control subsequently lost contact with the aircraft approximately 13 miles west of Andros Island," the Royal Bahamas Police Force said.
A civilian boat that was used in the search for the missing Florida family, according to Silvia Larrieu. (Courtesy Silvia Larrieu)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The Bahamas Air Sea Rescue Association (BASRA) advised that the United States Coast Guard had attempted to search the area for the missing aircraft," police also said. "However, due to inclement weather, the search was postponed until conditions became favorable."
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Massive fire engulfs apartment complex under construction, forces evacuations in South Bend
summary: A massive construction fire engulfed the Stadium Flats apartments in South Bend, Indiana, forcing emergency evacuation of neighboring residents.
story: The fire erupted just after midnight at the Stadium Flats apartment development in South Bend, Indiana, near the training facility for the South Bend Cubs, the city's minor league baseball team. (Credit: @goonie52832 via Storyful)

A massive fire early Tuesday morning tore through an apartment complex under construction in South Bend, Indiana, forcing residents of a neighboring building to evacuate, according to local officials.
The South Bend Fire Department said the fire began just after midnight at the Stadium Flats apartments near S. Lafayette & W. South Street.
Fire crews arrived to a scene of towering flames and billowing smoke after receiving reports that the blaze had engulfed both the building under construction and a crane.
CRANE ARM COLLAPSES INTO MIAMI CONDO ROOFTOP POOL AREA AS WORKERS CLING TO DANGLING STRUCTURE

A massive fire engulfs the Stadium Flats apartment complex in South Bend, Indiana, on Sept. 8, 2026. The building was under construction and would have added dozens of affordable housing units to the city. (South Bend Fire Department)
Despite the fire producing "a significant amount of embers and debris," firefighters were able to keep it from spreading to the neighboring Diamond View Apartments.

Residents of the Diamond View Apartments were evacuated during the fire, with officials saying the heat damaged several windows on the building's top floor. The building has 60 units of affordable housing, according to a report last year in the South Bend Tribune.
Crews from the South Bend Fire Department arrived to the scene shortly after midnight on Sept. 8, 2026. (South Bend Fire Department)
MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION
The Stadium Flats building was set to introduce 92 additional affordable units to downtown South Bend. Before the fire, construction was expected to be completed by spring 2027.

Both buildings are near the training facility for the South Bend Cubs, the city's minor league baseball team. Firefighters were able to stop the blaze from spreading to the 17,000-square-foot complex, which is right next to the baseball stadium.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation, officials said. No injuries or fatalities were reported. (South Bend Fire Department)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Officials said the cause of the fire remains under investigation. No injuries or deaths were reported.
The fire occurred a little over two miles from the University of Notre Dame's campus.

title: Texas education board approves controversial curriculum changes tying 'radical Islam' to 9/11 attacks
summary: The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to controversial social studies changes impacting how students learn about Islam and Christianity.
story: Rep. Mike Lawler joins 'Saturday in America' to react to reports that a local administration is building a network of social media influencers to promote its agenda. Lawler discusses the impact of these policies on New York business owners and outlines his bipartisan legislation to mandate 9/11 historical curriculum in classrooms nationwide.

The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to changes to the state's high school social studies curriculum, a controversial move that will impact how students are taught about Islam and Christianity.

The amended social studies curriculum, which covers U.S. history, government and world geography, comes after dozens of people gave public testimony, with most expressing their opposition to the finalized version.
The board approved language asserting that "radical Islam" motivated the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks rather than taking a more narrow focus on the terrorist groups involved in the attack.

The material also requires students to study early Islam through Prophet Muhammad's "brutal military campaigns against Jewish and Christian tribes," the "normalization of slavery" and the taking of female captives as "harem slaves."
NBA CHAMPION JOSH HART CELEBRATES TEXAS BOARD OF EDUCATION'S VOTE TO MAKE BIBLE PASSAGES REQUIRED READING
The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to changes to the state's high school social studies curriculum. (iStock)
Several Democratic State Board of Education members pushed back against the wording, but the Republican-majority board still approved that section and the other changes on Friday.
Muslim groups and students, as well as multiple curriculum experts, also spoke out against the new changes.

"I feel attacked, as if my religion doesn’t belong," Habiiba Quresh, a 15-year-old Muslim student, told the board, according to The Texas Tribune. "I shouldn't have to defend my religion in the middle of history class because of one sentence someone on this board wrote."
At least three of the board-appointed curriculum experts also warned against the new language.
TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA'

The board approved language asserting that "radical Islam" motivated the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks rather than taking a more narrow focus on the terrorist groups involved in the attack. (Antonio Perez/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Andrea Hutchison, a social studies curriculum coordinator for Prosper ISD, argued the material did not "hold up to close historical scrutiny," according to the outlet. Robert Koons, a philosophy professor at UT-Austin, said most nonreligious scholars find the source of the claims "not very reliable," adding that he would warn against including material that is "not based on well-established secular sources."

The Texas chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations said the board’s decision to "single out and denigrate Islam, minimize the brutal realities of slavery and segregation, and entirely erase Palestinian history is an affront to our system of education and the First Amendment."

"No credible scholar of history validates the bigoted caricatures of Islam this curriculum teaches," CAIR Texas and CAIR Action Texas said in a joint statement. "Even the board’s own appointed experts warned it doesn’t hold up to historical scrutiny, yet the board voted against removing it. Texas students of every background deserve an education that tells the truth about their history and their neighbors’ history, not propaganda that teaches them to see each other as threats or erases them from the story altogether."
Muslim groups and students, as well as multiple curriculum experts, spoke out against the new changes. (Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images)

State Board of Education Chair Aaron Kinsey pushed back on criticism of the revised standards, saying opponents had "sensationalize[d] all these topics and [made] them seem more divisive than they actually are." He added that board members "worked through, democratically, how to make those choices on behalf of our constituents" and said he believed they "did an exceptional job overall."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
But Republican school board member Julie Pickren boasted about the material's final approval, according to Fox 7.

"This social studies law that got us here, I've been working on for over 10 years with the House and the Senate, the Texas House and Texas Senate ... and so this is such a huge accomplishment; this vote kind of bookends 12 years of life's work," Pickren said.
The approved curriculum is expected to be phased into classrooms during the 2030-31 school year.

title: Climber dies in fatal fall on Colorado 14er south of Aspen
summary: A 21-member rescue team was dispatched to the remote mountain after nearby hikers witnessed the climber fall and officials determined the injuries were not survivable.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Officials in Colorado said a climber suffered a fatal fall Sunday after scaling a towering peak south of Aspen.
The tragic incident occurred on Castle Peak, which reaches a steep elevation of 14,272 feet in the Elk Mountains, according to Mountain Rescue Aspen.
Responders said rescue team members reached the climber by 4 p.m. after the Gunnison County Sheriff's Office was notified of a fallen climber.
However, officials "determined the individual had sustained injuries that were not survivable."
NORTH CAROLINA CLIMBER AIRLIFTED AFTER PLUNGING 20 FEET DOWN GORGE, SUSTAINING SERIOUS INJURIES
Responders reached the climber by 4 p.m. but determined the injuries could not be survived. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
The fall was apparently witnessed by nearby hikers, including Rebecca Rees, who recounted the incident in a statement posted to Facebook.
"Unfortunately, we witnessed the event. It has been an extremely sad and terrible afternoon for all involved. He did not survive," she said.
Rees said a bystander, identified as Robert, even scrambled toward the climber immediately after the fall, putting himself at risk in case there was still a chance of survival.
She added that the victim ultimately "wasn’t alone" in his final moments.
NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS
Nearby hikers reportedly witnessed the fall at Castle Peak, south of Aspen. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
Rees said the rescue crew responded at a commendable speed. Despite the remote location, helicopter and ground teams reportedly reached nearly 13,000 feet in under two hours on a holiday weekend.
According to Mountain Rescue Aspen, officials used off-highway vehicles and helicopters to reach the remote area.
After a helicopter located the fallen climber, it returned to Aspen to pick up additional rescue personnel before taking them to the high-elevation area near the peak.
MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE
Officials said the climber was recovered from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
A total of 21 rescue members were sent into the field, and officials safely recovered and evacuated the deceased climber from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m.
Rees said the responders showed extraordinary compassion throughout the recovery effort.
The rescue operation unfolded at elevations approaching 13,000 feet. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

"The response of search and rescue, the sheriff, and the coroner all made us feel like every single person matters. This young man had a story and we all care," she said.

title: US forces sink narco-refueling station linked to Ecuadorian cartel in Pacific: SOUTHCOM
summary: U.S. forces sank a Los Choneros refueling vessel in the Eastern Pacific after SOUTHCOM said it supported at-sea drug trafficking operations.
story: The vessel was involved with Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian organized crime syndicate, U.S. Southern Command said (Credit: X @Southcom).
U.S. forces on Monday sank a floating refueling vessel used by an Ecuadorian organized crime ring, officials said.

Forces with Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTFWH) interdicted the refueling vessel used for "at-sea drug trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said.
"JTF-WHEM continues to conduct precise and professional operations to dismantle the logistical networks fueling narco-trafficking in the Western Hemisphere," a SOUTHCOM post on X states.
The vessel was involved with the Los Choneros narco-terrorist organization, SOUTHCOM said. The people aboard were removed and will be handed over to Ecuadorian authorities.
NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING
U.S. Forces on Monday sank a refueling vessel used by Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian organized crime ring, in the Eastern Pacific Ocean. (U.S. Southern Command)
Once the boat was cleared, U.S. forces sank it.
JTFWH was activated by SOUTHCOM in August to counter threats, strengthen regional security, and respond to crises in the Western Hemisphere.
The Trump administration has prioritized targeting suspected drug-smuggling vessels bound for the United States.
US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK
U.S. forces have launched dozens of strikes targeting such boats under the administration's anti-drug campaign.

Last week, the cartel was designated by the State Department as a foreign terrorist organization. Its members have attacked and threatened public officials and their families, security personnel, judges, prosecutors, and journalists in Ecuador, the agency said.

"Their ultimate goal is to control drug trafficking routes through Ecuador by terrorizing and inflicting brutal violence on the Ecuadorian people," said State Department deputy spokesperson Thomas Pigott.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In July, U.S. and Ecuadorian authorities cooperated to extradite Los Choneros leader Fito Macias, who was the first Ecuadorian citizen extradited from Ecuador to face justice in the U.S.

title: Jimmy John's employee accused of opening fire on car, shooting 14-year-old girl in leg: police
summary: Police say that a dispute at a St. Louis Jimmy John's escalated into gunfire, leaving a 14-year-old girl wounded and an employee facing felony charges.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A dispute that began at a Jimmy John's restaurant in St. Louis ended with a 14-year-old girl shot in the leg and a restaurant employee facing charges for allegedly opening fire on a vehicle carrying the teen, according to police and court records.

The teenage girl was struck shortly before 6 p.m. Saturday near the intersection of Vandeventer and Laclede avenues and was taken to a local hospital, where she was listed in stable condition, the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said in a statement on X.
Court documents identified the alleged shooter as 27-year-old Adam White, whom police say was an employee at the Jimmy John's where the confrontation began.
MISSOURI ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER HIDDEN VIDEO FOUND ON WIFE'S PHONE, INVESTIGATORS SAY
Police said the shooting stemmed from a dispute involving the teenage girl's mother and "several individuals" associated with the Jimmy John's in the 3800 block of Laclede. (Google Maps)
White is charged with first-degree assault, armed criminal action, unlawful use of a weapon, first-degree child endangerment, among other felony offenses.
In their statement, police said the shooting stemmed from a dispute involving the teenage girl's mother and "several individuals" associated with the Jimmy John's in the 3800 block of Laclede.

"A preliminary investigation indicates the shooting followed a disagreement involving the girl’s mother and several individuals associated with the Jimmy John’s in the 3800 block of Laclede. The mother’s connection to the restaurant remains under investigation," the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said.
According to investigators, the girl's mother's boyfriend later arrived at the restaurant with the 14-year-old. The confrontation escalated, and gunfire erupted.
GOP CANDIDATE GETS BUSTED ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO PLANT DRUGS ON HIS POLITICAL RIVAL
Court documents identified the alleged shooter as 27-year-old Adam White. (City of St. Louis)
Court documents allege that White got into a verbal argument with a former employee, which continued into the parking lot.
Police say the former employee, her boyfriend and her juvenile daughter then got into a vehicle.
As the vehicle drove away, White allegedly fired multiple rounds into its rear, striking the teenage girl in the left leg.
"As they drove off, the defendant fired multiple rounds into the rear of the vehicle. Victim 3, the juvenile, was struck by one of the bullets in her left leg," court documents state.
Investigators said they found ballistic damage to the trunk of the vehicle.
US MARSHALS SURVIVE DECK COLLAPSE WHILE SERVING WARRANT AT SEX OFFENDER'S HOME
According to court documents, White initially fled the scene but later returned and was taken into custody. (Karl Merton Ferron/The Baltimore Sun/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

According to court documents, White initially fled the scene but later returned and was taken into custody. After being advised of his Miranda rights, White allegedly admitted firing at the vehicle and told detectives he had left the gun at his home.
A judge ordered White held without bond pending trial.
Jimmy John's and the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: Prosecutors drop Khalid Sheikh Mohammed confession appeal to protect 2028 trial for alleged 9/11 mastermind
summary: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed's 2007 confession was thrown out over "severe coercion," but prosecutors won't appeal to protect the June 2028 trial date.
story: Former assistant U.S. attorney Andy McCarthy analyzes evidentiary obstacles in prosecuting 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, judicial rulings on mail-in ballots as North Carolina begins distribution and the prosecution's strategy following an 11-1 jury deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial.

Military prosecutors will move ahead with the trial against the mastermind of the Sept. 11 attacks without a key confession, a decision made to avoid further delays in the long-awaited proceedings scheduled for 2028.
The federal government has decided not to appeal a recent ruling by a military judge that threw out statements made by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed in 2007.
The decision means Mohammed's statements to the FBI cannot be used at trial.

"An appeal could jeopardize the hard-earned June 5, 2028, trial date," the prosecution team's liaison to victims wrote in a letter Friday — a week before the 25th anniversary of the attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people, sources familiar with the matter told The New York Post.
NEW EVIDENCE IN LOCKERBIE PAN AM FLIGHT 103 BOMBING CASE PUSHES FEDERAL JUDGE TO POSTPONE TRIAL
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks, has been held at Guantánamo Bay since 2003. (AP)

Appeals can take years to resolve, an outcome military prosecutors want to avoid given the series of delays that have prolonged the wait for victims' families to receive justice. Mohammed and his alleged co-conspirators — Walid bin Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi, and Ammar al-Baluchi — are scheduled to go on trial in June 2028.
Prosecutors initially planned to use a confession obtained from Mohammed at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, where he has been held for nearly two decades.
9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

Firefighter walks through the rubble of the World Trade Center after it was struck by a commercial airliner in a terrorist attack. A hijacked American Airlines Boeing 767, originating from Boston's Logan Airport, struck 1 World Trade Center (north tower) at 8:45 a.m. At 9:03 a.m., a United Airlines 767, also hijacked in Boston, crashed into 2 World Trade Center (south tower).The second tower came down 39 minutes after the first. (Todd Maisel/NY Daily News via Getty Images)
Lt. Col. Michael Schrama set the trial date last month before suppressing the confession. He cited "severe coercion" and noted that Mohammed did not have an opportunity to consult with an attorney.
Mohammed and two of his co-defendants had agreed to a plea deal with the Biden administration in 2024 that would have spared them the death penalty.

The deal was subsequently revoked following public outcry, resulting in further lengthy litigation.
Meanwhile, 9/11 families have asked the Trump administration to declassify documents on Saudi Arabia's alleged role in the attacks.

title: NTSB reveals if crew survived Amazon cargo jet disaster as it shares details about victims
summary: The NTSB said the crew survived after the Amazon cargo plane overran the runway, caught fire and collided with two vehicles carrying eight occupants.
story: NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said the Boeing 767 continued about 1,300 feet beyond the paved runway surface.
Federal regulators said the two crew members aboard the Amazon cargo jet that crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday survived the accident.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) provided the update during a Sunday press conference after officials said the cargo plane overran the runway and caught fire while landing. The crash killed five people and injured five others, authorities said Sunday.
The jet collided with two vehicles carrying at least eight occupants, according to NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy.

Seven of the victims were in a van that was struck and "torn apart" on airport grounds, Homendy said. The 2012 white Ford Econoline van was owned by Ocean Service Corporation, a contract cleaning company that provides services for airlines, she said.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED
NTSB investigators examine a wreckage field Monday after a Boeing 767 cargo plane overran the end of Runway 30 while landing Sunday at Miami International Airport. (@NTSB_Newsroom/X)
The NTSB said the aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE, that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue.
Homendy said investigators observed what appeared to be deployed airbags in the vehicles as they surveyed the crash site.
"You can see components from vehicles, both passenger vehicles and the aircraft itself," Homendy said.
The jet then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said.

An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 crashes off the runway and crushes a vehicle near the Miami International Airport in Miami on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026.  (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
In total, the jet reportedly traveled 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface.
Homendy said the wreckage was "extensive," noting that the crash damaged airport navigational aids and equipment, while fencing was ripped apart throughout the area.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Officials investigate a Prime Air cargo plane at Miami International Airport after it overran the runway at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida, on September 6, 2026. (CHANDAN KHANNA / AFP via Getty Images)
Officials said the Boeing 767 had completed two other flights before crashing in Miami, where its operator, 21 Air LLC, is based.
The aircraft traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico, before returning to Miami, Homendy said.
NTSB investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which they planned to examine.
Prime Air flight 7598 became disabled after overrunning Miami International Airport’s diagonal runway. (Google Maps)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Homendy described the crash site as "devastating," saying wreckage was scattered throughout the area.
"I would describe it in one word, devastating, utter devastation," she said.
"I mean, you can see on the paved surface, tire marks that continue through the grass. There's debris everywhere."
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Menendez brothers granted 2027 parole hearing a year earlier than expected
summary: Erik and Lyle Menendez will face a parole hearing in March 2027, moved up from 2028 reportedly under Proposition 9 provisions after their resentencing.
story: Former Sacramento DA Anne Marie Schubert is spearheading a lawsuit challenging new California Board of Parole Hearings guidelines that she warns will open a pathway to freedom for serial killers, mass shooters and more of the state's worst violent criminals.
Erik and Lyle Menendez have been granted a parole hearing for next year, a year earlier than previously expected.

The brothers, who were both convicted of the Aug. 20, 1989, shotgun slayings of their parents, Jose and Mary Louise "Kitty" Menendez, in their Beverly Hills home, are scheduled to have a parole suitability hearing in March 2027 instead of August 2028, Fox News confirms.

The change stems from two provisions included in Proposition 9, which allow a prison inmate's next parole hearing date to be moved up if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole, The Orange County Register reported.
CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM
Erik and Lyle Menendez will face a parole board hearing in March 2027, a year earlier than expected. (Getty Images)

"For almost 40 years, Erik and Lyle have worked to take responsibility for their actions, confront and heal from the unimaginable abuse and trauma they endured, grow as individuals, and dedicate themselves to serving others," a statement by family members reads.

"Through efforts such as helping to establish a hospice program and creating Green Space, they have sought to build an environment that reminds people serving life sentences that their lives still have meaning and that, regardless of their circumstances, they can choose each day to grow, heal, accept accountability, and contribute something of value to the world around them," they added.
NEW HAMPSHIRE RESENTENCING GIVES DARTMOUTH KILLER ROBERT TULLOCH A PAROLE PATH AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

Lyle, left, and Erik Menendez leave a courtroom in Santa Monica, Calif., Aug. 6, 1990, after a judge ruled that conversations between the brothers and their psychologist after their parents were slain were not privileged and could be used as evidence. (AP Photo/Nick Ut, File)

The brothers were handed life sentences without the possibility of parole for the murders, which drew widespread media attention. However, they were resentenced to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole.
The new sentencing came amid a push by supporters following a Netflix series on the case that resurrected calls for their freedom. They were denied parole last year.
NEVADA PAROLE BOARD REJECTS HENRY RUGGS III'S BID FOR EARLY RELEASE AFTER DEADLY 156 MPH DUI CRASH
Erik Menendez appears remotely for a 2025 parole hearing. (CDCR)
The brothers have said the murders were committed after years of sexual abuse by their father. However, prosecutors have contested the claims, arguing the pair killed their parents out of greed.

"Erik and Lyle were once sentenced to life without the possibility of parole," the family statement said. "We will always be profoundly grateful that they have been resentenced and that our family can now imagine a future in which they are once again part of our everyday lives… We are incredibly proud of the men they have become and deeply grateful to the Parole Board for recognizing their efforts and allowing them to advance their parole hearing."
A sketch depicts (l-r) Erik and Lyle Menendez as they appear remotely at superior court in Van Nuys, California, Friday, April 11, 2025. (Bill Robles)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lyle Menendez, 58, and Erik Menendez, 55, are both incarcerated in the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility in San Diego.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Supporters of Alabama school bus driver charged in deadly accident say she suffered from 'medical crisis'
summary: Theresa McCloud faces vehicular homicide charges after a fatal Auburn school bus crash, but supporters claim a sudden blood sugar drop caused the accident.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
An Alabama woman accused of causing a deadly crash while driving a school bus experienced a medical crisis during the accident, her supporters reportedly said.
Theresa McCloud, 75, faces charges of vehicular homicide and criminal negligence for the Nov. 18, 2025 crash in Auburn.
McCloud was driving a bus for Auburn City Schools when she struck a vehicle. Jennifer Leigh Cooper, 42, a well-known local bakery owner, was killed in the collision, AL.com reported.
HEART-STOPPING VIDEO SHOWS MIDDLE SCHOOLERS SAVING THEIR BUS AFTER DRIVER PASSES OUT AT THE WHEEL
Morning light is "crucial to regulate sleep, [boost] alertness and support mental health," according to a sleep expert. (iStock)

McCloud's supporters said she suffered a medical crisis during the fatal crash. However, a lawsuit filed by Cooper's husband against McCloud and the Auburn City Schools Board of Education alleges that McCloud had diabetes and had been prescribed opiates.

On the day of the accident, McCloud told her supervisors that she was not feeling well, the lawsuit states. Two days prior, she had visited a doctor who prescribed opiates to help with her symptoms. Those medications came with a warning label against driving while taking them, according to the suit.
"Theresa’s blood sugar suddenly dropped to 23 mg/dL while driving, causing confusion and loss of consciousness," stated a GoFundMe page that has since been removed.
OLDER ADULTS TAKING 5 OR MORE PRESCRIPTION DRUGS FACE HIGHER RISK OF DEATH, STUDY FINDS

A school bus takes students home in the small Tulare County town in 2023. Supporters of an Alabama school bus driver charged in the vehicle death of a woman said she suffered a medical crisis during the deadly accident. (Genaro Molina / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"Theresa had never experienced a low blood sugar episode before, and doctors confirmed that this was a medical crisis," the page continued. "Even so, Theresa is now facing the overwhelming challenge of defending against charges connected to that emergency. On September 4, 2026, Theresa turned herself in and began facing the legal process head-on."
While driving, McCloud lost control "based on either her known medical conditions, her use of opiates and/or a mix of both," the lawsuit alleges.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The suit further said that the opiates and her diabetes "severely impaired her ability to drive any vehicle and made her unable to perform her duties as a bus driver," according to the newspaper. McCloud's family reportedly disputes the allegations.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the school district.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Ritzy Miami steakhouse manager held on ICE detainer after mom found stabbed to death
summary: Surveillance video allegedly shows the Miami steakhouse manager blood-soaked in an elevator with a knife hours after returning home with his mother.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Miami steakhouse manager allegedly emerged from his luxury apartment covered in blood and clutching a knife before telling police he had acted in self-defense after his mother was found stabbed to death inside.
Stefano Eduardo Cremasco-Cicero, 36, told officers, "I was defending myself," after Miami police were called to the Brickell high-rise early Friday, according to an arrest report obtained by WPLG.
Cremasco-Cicero is charged with second-degree murder with a weapon, Miami-Dade County jail records show.
KARMELO ANTHONY STAYS SILENT AS ANALYSTS WARN DEFENSE FACES UPHILL BATTLE IN TRACK MEET STABBING TRIAL
Stefano Cremasco-Cicero is being held without bond on a second-degree murder charge and an ICE detainer. (Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation)
Officers were dispatched at about 4:47 a.m. for an "unknown request for police assistance," according to the outlet.
Officers found Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby with blood on his hands, clothing and shoes, the outlet reported.
He allegedly directed officers upstairs to the apartment.
Inside the apartment, police found his mother lying behind the front door with multiple apparent stab wounds, according to WPLG. Miami Fire Rescue pronounced her dead shortly after 5 a.m.
FLORIDA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING MOM AND BURNING BODY BECAUSE SHE ‘WANTED TO BE CREMATED’
Cremasco-Cicero was reportedly found in the lobby with blood on his hands, clothing and shoes. (WSVN)
Authorities have not publicly identified the woman or disclosed her age. Police said she was visiting from Mexico and staying with her son.
The unusual chain of events began when a food delivery driver arrived at the building and encountered Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby, according to the report.

He allegedly opened the door for the driver and asked her to call 911. Cremasco-Cicero ultimately placed the call himself but handed the phone to the woman so she could give the dispatcher the building information, WPLG reported.

The driver noticed blood on him as they waited for police, according to the outlet. When she tried to return his phone, he allegedly refused to take it, and she later handed it to responding officers.
THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?
Investigators then turned to surveillance video and building access records to piece together what happened in the hours before police arrived.
Police were called to a high-rise in the Brickell neighborhood of Miami early Friday. (WSVN)
Surveillance video showed Cremasco-Cicero and his mother returning to the building together at about 10:32 p.m. Thursday, according to WPLG. They were reportedly alone in the elevator.
COURTNEY CLENNEY'S DEFENSE INSPECTS KNIVES AT CENTER OF ONLYFANS MODEL'S MURDER CASE AHEAD OF TRIAL: REPORT

At about 4:26 a.m., surveillance video allegedly captured Cremasco-Cicero entering an elevator wearing a white shirt, khaki pants and white shoes that appeared to be covered in blood. Police said he was carrying a knife.
He allegedly dropped the knife after stepping out of the elevator, picked it back up and rode another elevator upstairs, according to the report.

Investigators said Cremasco-Cicero later reappeared in a different, long-sleeved blue shirt and walked out of the building while using his phone. He returned minutes later and sat on a couch in the lobby before flagging down the delivery driver, WPLG reported.
Cremasco-Cicero’s wife, who was in France at the time, told detectives that his mother had been staying with him at the time of the incident, according to local reports. (WSVN)
Police said Cremasco-Cicero had small cuts on his hands and blood residue on his body and clothing. Crime scene investigators photographed him and collected his clothes, according to the outlet.
5 REASONS MORE AMERICANS ARE CUTTING OFF THEIR OWN PARENTS, ACCORDING TO PSYCHOLOGIST

After obtaining a search warrant, homicide detectives allegedly recovered several kitchen knives with blood on them, blood-spattered shirts, broken glass and a broken wine bottle from the apartment, WPLG reported.

Cremasco-Cicero’s wife told detectives she was in France attending a wedding when the killing happened, according to the report. She said her husband and his mother had not been close since his parents divorced and that he had recently been under stress while preparing to open a restaurant in Coconut Grove.
Stefano Cremasco-Cicero is seen sitting for an interview with WSVN-TV about his restaurant in July. (WSVN)
The Miami Herald identified Cremasco-Cicero as the U.S. operating manager of the high-end 1986 Steakhouse in Miami.
The arrest report identified Cremasco-Cicero as a Miami resident through an investor visa, according to WPLG.

Miami-Dade Corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Cremasco-Cicero was booked Friday night and is being held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. The records list no bond, a domestic-violence designation and a hold for immigration authorities.
The jail record does not provide additional details about the immigration hold.
A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital that Cremasco-Cicero is an illegal immigrant.

"On August 5, 2026, ICE lodged a detainer for Stefano Eduardo Cremasco Cicero, a criminal illegal alien from Mexico, charged with homicide," the DHS spokesperson said. "We are calling on Florida to honor our detainer. His claims will be heard by an immigration judge and he will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law."
"Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, if you break the law, you will face the consequences," the spokesperson added. "Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the U.S."
