story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

Before polls close tonight in New Hampshire’s primaries, Bridget Bowman and Ben Kamisar preview the key races to watch. Plus, Natasha Korecki digs into how Republicans are reviving their anti-trans playbook ahead of November.
— Adam Wollner
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
New Hampshire primaries test Trump and the left

President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.
Here’s what to watch tonight:

Democratic Senate primary: Rep. Chris Pappas, who first won a battleground seat in 2018, is considered the front-runner for his party’s nomination in the race to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. He already appears to be gearing up for the general election, focusing his campaign on addressing high costs and political corruption, while launching an ad attacking a potential Republican opponent.

But Pappas is facing a challenge from the left from Karishma Manzur, a scientist and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who supports progressive policies like “Medicare for All.” Manzur has sharply criticized Pappas over support and funding for Israel, saying he is “enabling genocide.” (For more on this primary, check out the latest edition of Steve Kornacki’s “Data Dive” newsletter.)
Republican Senate primary: This contest includes multiple candidates, but the race is largely between two former senators: John Sununu and Scott Brown.

Sununu represented New Hampshire in the Senate from 2003 through 2008 after serving in the House. He lost his bid for re-election in 2008 to Shaheen, but Republicans believe his well-known family name could give him a boost: Sununu’s brother and father both served as governors. Sununu is backed by President Donald Trump, Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.
Brown held a Massachusetts seat for three years, previously ran for the New Hampshire Senate in 2014, and served as Trump’s ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during the president’s first term.

General election preview: Trump lost New Hampshire by just 3 points in 2024, giving Republicans hope about making this open-seat race competitive. The GOP has not won a Senate race there since 2010, but New Hampshire does have a Republican governor, Kelly Ayotte.
Read more →
🗺️ Senate landscape: Eight weeks from Election Day, there’s an increasing sense in both parties that the Senate is up for grabs this fall, even in red territory, Bridget reports.
Tune in to the Kornacki Cam at 7 p.m. ET to watch Steve break down tonight’s results.
Republicans return to a familiar playbook in Texas
The first ad from Elon Musk’s super PAC in Texas’ competitive Senate race has arrived. And it centers on a go-to topic for Republicans: transgender issues.

The Musk-funded America PAC just released an ad titled: “Non-binary.” It features Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico saying, “God is non-binary,” twice in 15 seconds. The spot also notes that Talarico did not support a bill to ban biological men from playing in women’s sports. As a bookend, Republican Ken Paxton’s campaign posted on social media this morning an AI-generated ad featuring similar messaging.

With this and other similar ads in races in red-leaning states, Republicans are demonstrating that in their high-stakes endeavor to retain Senate control, they believe their best bet is to return to the well.

Some political observers credited the ubiquitous ads President Donald Trump ran in the 2024 election — “Kamala is for they/them; President Trump is for you” — as an influential factor in tanking Kamala Harris’ campaign.
But will they work two years later?

Harris’ 2024 loss fueled intraparty soul-searching and feuds over whether it was an error to allow those attacks to go unanswered. Whether the Talarico campaign will directly respond to these anti-trans ads in the future remains unclear.
Talarico has called his past comments “cringey” but said Paxton, Texas’ attorney general, was clipping them to “distract from his career of corruption.”

Talarico has also criticized the media for focusing too heavily on trans athletes and not enough on affordability, and spent months saying that some politicians were attempting to pit rank-and-file voters against one another.

“What I would say is that the only minority destroying this country is the billionaires,” Talarico said in 2025. “Trans people are 1% of the population. Undocumented people are 1% of the population. Muslims are 1% of the population. We are all focused on the wrong 1%. Trans people aren’t taking away our healthcare. Undocumented people aren’t defunding our schools. Muslims aren’t cutting taxes for themselves and their rich friends. It’s the billionaires and their puppet politicians.”

The political climate in America has decidedly shifted since 2024. Democrats have demonstrated, including in Virginia and Nebraska, that anti-trans ads did little to move voters who cared more about cost of living issues.

Poll after poll shows that in the run-up to the midterms, voters are frustrated by the cost of groceries and gas. An unpopular war in Iran drags on. Trump’s popularity is in free fall. Scores of Latino voters, a sizable voting bloc in Texas, are angry over aggressive immigration tactics, while Trump has lost significant ground on support on the issue. In Texas specifically, fury over data center expansion is in full force. And Republicans locally are facing backlash over the administration’s border construction in Big Bend National Park.

That may be why, when asked today, Talarico’s campaign had nothing to say about the new anti-trans ads. Instead, it released an ad featuring an endorsement from the former Texas attorney general’s director of law enforcement, David Maxwell, who served as a whistleblower against Paxton in his impeachment trial.

Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said the hearing was “about how a brutal, repressive regime can buy influence, indeed even take over a cherished American institution to cleanse its public image.”

Entering its fifth season this year, LIV’s big ambitions and roster of big-name players took a hit, however, when Koepka and a second major champion, Patrick Reed, left the tour in January. (In the bankruptcy filing, Koepka is listed as a creditor, with a claim of $1.7 million.) Soon after, Koepka played in a PGA Tour event. The defections followed the PGA’s decision to offer a small number of players who had left for LIV a pathway to return to playing in PGA events.

Though LIV plans to re-emerge next year, it will need players to sign on and Rahm, a former Masters champion who is one of its biggest former names, was noncommittal this week when asked about his future.
“There’s a lot of things that could happen, and it’s one of those things where time’s gonna tell,” Rahm told the BBC.

title: Man pleads not guilty to misdemeanor charges in Ohio fair incident involving Amy Acton
summary: A man accused of knocking an elderly couple to the ground in an attempt to confront Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton on Sunday has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from the incident.
story: A man accused of knocking an elderly couple to the ground in an attempt to confront Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton on Sunday has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from the incident.

Patrick Havas, 38, on Tuesday appeared via video in a Mahoning County court hearing to face two charges of assault, one charge of disorderly conduct, and one charge of inducing panic. He entered a plea of not guilty to all charges.

Acton, a Democrat, was visiting the annual Canfield Fair in Canfield on Sunday afternoon when the incident occurred. Havas allegedly pushed his way through a crowd in an attempt to approach Acton, knocking two elderly individuals over in the process, according to an incident report obtained by NBC News on Tuesday.

Ohio state troopers working as Acton’s security detail grabbed Havas as he attempted to approach her, the report said. Law enforcement officials reported finding two handguns, a set of brass knuckles and a Taser on Havas after arresting him.
Havas never brandished a weapon during the incident, the incident report said.

A judge agreed to a $5,000 cash surety bond for Havas and  ordered him to surrender any weapons he owns as a condition of the bond. Havas was also instructed not to speak to the media and to have no contact with the elderly couple or Acton.
Havas’ attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment following Tuesday’s hearing.
Records show that Havas was arrested in 2008 on a charge of petty theft. He pleaded no contest and the charge was reduced to disorderly conduct.
Mahoning County Prosecutor Lynn Maro defended her office’s decision not to pursue felony charges against Havas. She noted that Havas never made physical contact with Acton or brandished a weapon.

Adults are allowed to possess a firearm without a permit under Ohio’s open-carry law, so long as they are not concealed under clothing. Maro told reporters that there were no charges that would fit “for simply possession of those weapons.”
“We’re not going to let emotions take over,” Maro said. “We’re going to follow the evidence. We’re going to follow the facts, and that’s how we’re going to prosecute.”

Acton’s campaign had asked for people to stop recording shortly before the incident, Maro said, but Havas was recording at the time. Havas consented to a “complete search” of his phone, according to Maro.
Prosecutors have video from his vantage point, which Maro said does not support a pursuit of felony charges.

“It shows him walking into the tent, recording, and moving forward, calling out her name ... Somebody in her security comes forward, and then his phone is either dropped or tousled, and that’s all we have,” Maro said.

On Monday, during a Labor Day parade in Cleveland, Acton described the incident as a “rough day,” according to NBC News affiliate WKYC. She expressed gratitude to those who helped the injured individuals and the state troopers who provided security.

“I am a fierce warrior in this fight,” Acton said. “That’s exactly why I’m running. I refuse to look the other way, like people didn’t look the other way when I was a struggling kid in Youngstown, Ohio. I won’t look the other way, and you are refusing to look the other way.”
Three witnesses to the incident told NBC News that they saw the suspect knock two older attendees to the ground. They also saw Acton, a physician, help care for them in the aftermath.
The individuals’ names were redacted from the incident report and NBC News was unable to reach them for comment on Tuesday. They were treated on scene and released, the report said.

Former Rep. John Boccieri, D-Ohio, said he was within an “arm’s length” of Acton and that Havas made it “within feet” of the gubernatorial candidate. He described the incident as “an aggressive move from a very large man.”
“He was yelling, ‘Dr. Acton! Dr. Acton!’” Boccieri said. “And when the State Highway Patrol and the security detail grabbed him, he said, ‘I was just trying to ask a question.”

title: U.S. strikes Iranian tankers after attempted attacks on Navy warship
summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.
story: The U.S. military sank five Iranian tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in response to attempted attacks by the IRGC on an American warship, according to U.S. Central Command.

“CENTCOM forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers, Sept. 8, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days,” U.S. Central Command said in a post on X. “The U.S. warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed.”
Four of the tankers were attacked in the Gulf of Oman and one was hit near Kharg Island, according to CENTCOM.
“American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable,” CENTCOM said in a statement.

A U.S. strike hit an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island, Iran’s main oil terminal, which has been repeatedly threatened by President Donald Trump, according to the semiofficial Tasnim news agency.    The U.S. military hit a second tanker near the port city of Jask, according to Iranian state TV.

The strikes on the Iranian tankers Tuesday come after the IRGC attempted to hit an American aircraft carrier and a destroyer over the weekend, resulting in a U.S. response in which the U.S. sank one tanker and permanently disabled two more.
Iran threatened to target oil tankers in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for the U.S. strikes on Tuesday.

“Following the actions of the American military in targeting several Iranian oil tankers, we warn all oil tanker crews in the areas around the ports of Kuwait and Bahrain, which are hosting these forces and are complicit in their actions, to immediately evacuate their vessels, whether they are at anchor or docked as they will be targeted,” the IRGC Navy said in a statement posted by the semi-official Fars news agency.

The Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the war, has become the key battleground in the conflict as both the U.S. and Iran have attacked tankers.

The Trump administration on Tuesday also imposed sanctions on additional elements of Iran’s aviation industry, targeting more than two dozen commercial and private airlines as well as foreign cargo service providers in its new push to isolate Tehran from its remaining trading partners.

A U.S. blockade of Iranian ports has squeezed the country’s economy by limiting its oil exports, while the American military has been helping a limited number of ships transit on a route through the Strait of Hormuz off Oman. Tehran wants ships to follow a route that it chooses through the strait, which was considered an international waterway before the war.

title: Lori Loughlin files for divorce from Mossimo Giannulli after nearly 30 years
summary: Actor Lori Loughlin has filed for divorce from husband Mossimo Giannulli after almost 30 years of marriage, court documents show.
story: Actor Lori Loughlin has filed for divorce from husband Mossimo Giannulli after almost 30 years of marriage, court documents show.
The filing last week by the “Full House” star comes about a year after the couple separated, with the separation date on the documents listed as Aug. 31, 2025.
Court documents show the reason for divorce is “irreconcilable differences” and indicate the couple has a prenuptial agreement. Details of the prenup were not available.
Loughlin and Giannulli married in 1997. They share two children — Olivia Jade Giannulli and Isabella Rose Giannulli.
Their marriage came under intense public scrutiny in recent years due to their joint involvement in the 2019 college admissions scandal.

The scam, investigated by the FBI under the code name “Varsity Blues,” focused on getting students admitted to elite universities as recruited athletes, regardless of their athletic abilities, and helping potential students cheat on their college exams.

Loughlin and Giannulli admitted to paying $500,000 to the scheme’s ringleaders, Rick Singer and Key Worldwide Foundation, to falsely designate their daughters as recruits to the University of Southern California crew team, even though neither girl was a rower.

Loughlin served two months in federal prison, and was also ordered to pay a fine of $150,000 and complete 100 hours of community service once she was released. Giannulli was sentenced to five months in prison, 250 hours of community service and a fine of $250,000.

Loughlin is best known for her role as Aunt Becky on the hit ABC sitcom “Full House” and its Netflix revival, “Fuller House.” She’s also appeared in multiple television movies and series, including recurring roles on “Summerland” and “When Calls the Heart.”
Giannulli is a designer who founded the fashion brand Mossimo in 1986.

title: Former Penn State coach Jerry Sandusky seeks new trial after victim recants
summary: Former Penn State football coach Jerry Sandusky is seeking a new trial in federal court after one of his accusers recanted.
story: Disgraced former Penn State football coach Jerry Sandusky appeared virtually in court on Tuesday and told a judge he understood his legal team’s move in seeking a new trial in federal court after one of his accusers recanted.

Tainted victim testimony led to Sandusky’s wrongful conviction for child sexual abuse, according to his lawyers, who believe their client’s best chances for freedom now come from moving the case from the Pennsylvania system to a U.S. courthouse.

But in moving this case to another court, Sandusky’s legal team surrenders its right to litigate in state court claims that Victim No. 10, identified in court papers as “R.R.,” was allegedly manipulated into misleading testimony.

Sandusky, 82, an inmate at State Correctional Institution (SCI) Laurel Highland serving a term of at least 30 years, was convicted after multiple people testified they were sexually abused by the former assistant coach as boys. Sandusky used his name in the community and his nonprofit, The Second Mile, to meet victims, prosecutors have said.
Judge Maureen Skerda asked Sandusky, who appeared via video feed from prison, if he understood his legal team’s actions and he confirmed that he did.
“I’m making this decision on advice of counsel,” Sandusky said, according to the Associated Press.

Skerda later ruled that “the Court being satisfied that Mr. Sandusky has been fully informed of his rights and understood Counsel’s action in withdrawing the claim concerning R.R.’s recantation, the Court hereby” dismisses the coach’s state court bid for post-conviction relief.
Arthur Hellman, an emeritus law professor at the University of Pittsburgh, said it’s rare for a convict’s attorney to bypass all available state court remedies.
A federal court might not even consider new evidence if that material hasn’t been first presented in state court, according to Hellman, whose expertise is in federal courts.

“It’s certainly extremely unusual,”  he said. “If he (Sandusky’s legal team) expects to present new evidence in a federal habeas proceeding that was not part of the state court record, he’s in for a very unpleasant surprise.”
The coach’s appellate attorneys claim that damaging testimony from several alleged victims have been subsequently shown to be problematic, particularly Victim 10, “R.R.”

That victim came forward with “new evidence” on June 30, 2025, that he had been “approached by state investigators who told me that my role was critical to stopping a predator,” according to Sandusky’s defense team.

Prosecutors told Victim 10 “other alleged victims were reluctant to come forward and repeatedly encouraged me to believe that Mr. Sandusky had molested me-despite my lack of clear or certain memory of any such conduct,” according to the recanting witness has said, Sandusky’s lawyers have said.

“I was told — both directly and indirectly — that trauma may have fragmented my memory, and that I could safely affirm details I did not fully recall. I was assured this was common and even expected,” according to a statement from R.R.

Sandusky’s attorney claimed that “R.R. maintained that his account changed over time as ‘the result of emotional strain, repeated exposure to leading questions, intense investigative pressure and psychological manipulation.’ ”
Outside court, Sandusky’s lawyer Jerry Russo told reporters that his client’s incarceration is an ongoing  “miscarriage of justice”
Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday, though, called Sandusky a “child predator” and dismissed the coach’s legal maneuvers.

“This was yet another attempt by a convicted child predator to avoid accountability and escape punishment for years of abuse he perpetrated under the veil of a child-empowerment program,” AG Sunday said in statement on Tuesday afternoon.
“I commend our litigation team for challenging this alleged recantation by one victim, and putting on record the voluminous evidence that debunks this highly-suspect claim by defense counsel.”
Sandusky was convicted on June 22, 2012, on 45 sex abuse-related counts and then sentenced to 30 to 60 years behind bars.
The scandal led to Penn State firing Sandusky’s boss, legendary coach Joe Paterno, for his alleged failure to take appropriate action against the longtime defensive coordinator.
A statue of Paterno, who led the Nittany Lions went 409-136-3 in 46 seasons on the Penn State sideline, was removed from the football stadium in the midst of the Sandusky reckoning.
But in the years since the scandal and Paterno’s death, the coach’s supporters have gained traction in re-evaluating his legacy.

The university recently opened the “Paterno Family Football Experience Room” inside Beaver Stadium, calling it a “permanent museum experience celebrating more than a century of Penn State Football history.”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at https://www.rainn.org/get-help.

title: Pamela Anderson says hepatitis C was ‘death sentence’ that ‘took everything I had in my bank’
summary: Pamela Anderson said her doctor told her she had 10 years to live when she was diagnosed in the late 1990s with hepatitis C. “It was a death sentence,” said Anderson.
story: Pamela Anderson said her doctor told her she had 10 years to live when she was diagnosed in the late 1990s with hepatitis C.
“It was a death sentence,” said Anderson.

But on Sunday, the actress whose breakout role on “Baywatch” turned her into an international star, was honored with amfAR’s Award of Courage at a gala in Venice, where she opened up about the diagnosis that upended her life. amfAR is a nonprofit organization dedicated to ending HIV/AIDS; hepatitis C is frequently a co-infection with AIDS.
At the time of her diagnosis, there was no cure for hepatitis C, which is a viral infection that causes liver inflammation and potential long-term damage.
“I’m sure that colored and corrupted my decisions,” Anderson, 59, said. “It was not fear of death, but fear of what might happen to my young children. It turned my life inside out.”
When Anderson publicly revealed in 2002 that she was infected with the virus, she said she contracted hepatitis C after sharing a tattoo needle with her then-husband, Mötley Crue drummer Tommy Lee.
“Tommy has the disease and never disclosed it to me during our marriage,” said Anderson, who at the time was in a custody battle with Lee over their two children.
Lee, however, has insisted repeatedly that he does not have hepatitis C.
Meanwhile, Anderson said in her speech on Sunday that she struggled with “shame and guilt.”

“It stays with me; it haunts me,” she said in her speech. “And just like the sexual abuse that I endured as a child, it felt like it was carved into my forehead: damaged goods. And I presented myself as such.”
Then, in 2011, a cure for the viral infection was found and four years later Anderson announced she was “hep C free.”

“I was lucky,” Anderson said in her speech before amfAR. “I was offered it in its early stages, and it took everything I had in my bank to pay for it. It wasn’t covered by insurance yet, and I felt tremendous guilt that others weren’t granted the same access.”
But Anderson said she has “finally come to terms” with the diagnosis.

In recent years, Anderson’s acting career has been revived, with roles in films like “The Last Showgirl,” “The Naked Gun,” “Rosebush Pruning” and “Place to Be,” which premieres Wednesday at the Venice Film Festival.

“My truth has come through my work, finding ways to express myself through the arts. It gave me the ammunition I needed, a fertile life to use and play in,” Anderson said. “I’m not a victim, I’m a victor. I am strong and capable, more now than I could ever dream of … I’m not the damsel in distress, no matter how easy that role is to play.”

title: 4 family members confirmed dead in Bahamas plane crash, relatives say
summary: The bodies of four family members were recovered after a small private aircraft crashed Monday about 15 miles off the coast of the largest Bahamian island, according to relatives.
story: The bodies of four family members were recovered after a small private aircraft crashed Monday about 15 miles off the coast of the largest Bahamian island, according to relatives.
The Miami-bound PA-34 Piper, a five-seat plane with four people aboard, took off from Great Harbour Cay around 11:15 a.m. Monday and crash-landed near Andros Island, Bahamas police previously said.

“It is with profound sadness that we confirm all four of our family members have been found deceased,” the family said in a statement Tuesday, noting that relatives “located our loved ones and had to bring them aboard their own vessels.”
“We are now in communication and working with the U.S. Coast Guard to bring our loved ones home safely and with dignity,” the statement continued.

The Royal Bahamas Police Force released a statement confirming “human remains were recovered and are now in police custody.” The remains were expected to be transferred to New Providence, the main commercial section of the small Caribbean nation.

The family previously said the plane was piloted by 80-year-old Mario Lamar and that his 79-year-old wife, Lili Lamar, and two of their grandchildren — 28-year-old Sofia Sosa and 22-year-old Christian Sosa — were also on board.

Silvia Larrieu, Lamar’s niece, told NBC News affiliate WTVJ in South Florida that her uncle had an apartment in the Bahamas and had spent “a wonderful long weekend together” with the grandchildren who were passengers on the plane and two other grandchildren.
She called Lamar “a lifelong, very experienced pilot” and said the family was “departing business as usual, like he’s done his entire life.”
FlightAware, a flight-tracking platform, showed the aircraft “flying into the edge of a storm” before it quickly reversed course, Larrieu told the station.
Larrieu’s cousin, the mother of the two adult grandchildren on board, called authorities when she didn’t hear from her kids after they were supposed to have landed.
Earlier Tuesday, the family pleaded for assistance in the search.

“We are heartbroken and desperate. As of this moment, we are not aware of authorities actively searching the waters for our remaining missing family members,” the family added. “We are begging for help.”
After the grim discoveries, the family members thanked “everyone who supported us, searched alongside us, and kept our family in their prayers.”

Mario Lamar was an attorney for over 50 years and had a law office in Miami, according to a state database. Guilaine Sosa, his daughter and the mother of his grandchildren who died, practiced with him at the firm, public records show.

Christian Sosa graduated with a marketing degree this year from Loyola Marymount University in Los Angeles and was a sports photographer who had recently done seasonal freelance work for the Los Angeles Rams, according to his LinkedIn profile.

“Getting to shoot in the NFL was surreal,” Sosa said in a post that also had a portrait of the team’s photography staff. “It’s the job my younger self dreamed about when I spent summers in Miami shooting training camps as a fan.”
He also maintained an Instagram account with landscape and nature shots from the Grand Canyon and other national parks.
Matt Stefl, one of Sosa’s professors at Loyola, praised the young man and told NBC News he was “absolutely gutted” by the news. “The world lost a good one,” he said.

Stefl visited the United Nations in May with Sosa and other students for a collegiate program where the group pitched a marketing campaign. The educator remained in touch with Sosa throughout the summer “about career prospects and life in general.”
“Christian was an amazing young man who lit up every room that he walked into,” Stefl said.

Sofia Sosa graduated from Florida International University with a master’s degree in physician assistant studies in December 2023, according to a school spokesperson. Her Facebook profile had her listed as a student at the FIU Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine in 2021.

Her page, which shows the nickname “Sofi,” had not been updated since 2023 but included photos of her throughout the years enjoying life from tropical settings. She also promoted a fundraiser for a childhood cancer charity.

title: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch is leaving amid tensions with Trump
summary: Bunch, the first Black person and first historian to lead the institution, said he has “mixed emotions” about departing.
story: Lonnie G. Bunch III will step down as head of the sprawling Smithsonian Institution by the end of the year, he said Tuesday.

He will depart at a vulnerable time for the institution, which includes dozens of museums, along with libraries, research centers and the National Zoo. While the Smithsonian has traditionally operated independently of the party in power, the Trump administration has repeatedly criticized how the institution portrays America’s past. Last week, the Interior Department threatened to cut off support, alleging that Smithsonian facilities present a “radical ideology” that weakens “shared American identity.”
Bunch, who has worked at the Smithsonian for 38 years, said in a statement that his retirement came “with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude.”

“I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been,” said Bunch, who became secretary in 2019. “There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together.”
A person familiar with the situation told NBC News there was no pressure from the regents — the board that leads the museums — for Bunch to resign.

Bunch, the first Black person and first historian to lead the institution, has said he would have retired a year ago but felt he had to stay to defend the institution from the White House attacks, the person said.
He told friends after he saw last week’s letter from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum that he believed now was the time to step down and assist in the transition to new leadership, the person said.
Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian, praised Bunch in a statement.

“From his days as a young curator at the National Air and Space and American History Museums through his tenure as the founding director of the African American History and Culture Museum and culminating in his distinguished service for the past seven years in the Smithsonian’s top job, Secretary Bunch has pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story,” Roberts said.

“The Regents, and the Smithsonian, have benefited greatly from his wisdom, vision and leadership. We look forward to working with him in the coming months to ensure a smooth transition for his successor.”

The person familiar with the situation said that the regents are forming a search committee and considering inside candidates to lead the Smithsonian during the transition and that Bunch told them he would stay on for three or four months to ease the changeover.

President Donald Trump took aim at the Smithsonian shortly after beginning his second term, issuing an executive order in March 2025 that directed Vice President JD Vance to eliminate “improper, divisive, or anti-American” ideology from the museum’s programs.

“Once widely respected as a symbol of American excellence and a global icon of cultural achievement, the Smithsonian Institution has, in recent years, come under the influence of a divisive, race-centered ideology,” the order said. “This shift has promoted narratives that portray American and Western values as inherently harmful and oppressive,” it alleged.
Because of his position as vice president, Vance is a member of the Smithsonian Board of Regents, whose other members include Roberts, members of Congress and members of the public.
In August last year, Trump wrote on social media that he’d also asked “my attorneys” to conduct a review of Smithsonian museums, because they’re focused too much on “how bad Slavery was.”

“The Smithsonian is OUT OF CONTROL, where everything discussed is how horrible our Country is, how bad Slavery was, and how unaccomplished the downtrodden have been — Nothing about Success, nothing about Brightness, nothing about the Future,” he wrote in the Truth Social post.
Vance criticized Bunch’s leadership at a regents meeting several months ago, two people who attended the meeting told NBC News.

The White House continued attacking the institution on Independence Day. As the country was celebrating its 250th anniversary, the White House Domestic Policy Council issued a report blasting Smithsonian leaders as radical activists who cannot be trusted.

“The Smithsonian Institution, and the National Museum of American History in particular, under its current leadership and current interpretive ideology, cannot be trusted to tell America’s story honestly and in a way that is inspiring, unifying, and worthy of our great republic,” the report said.
In an unrelated interview that aired the next day on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” Bunch said, “The notion of being a more perfect union, not the perfect union, is really what motivates me.”
“America’s greatest strength, it’s not running away from its history, but it’s understanding how that history shaped us and continues to shape us,” he said.
Megan Brand contributed reporting.

title: Authorities identify 5 victims killed when Amazon-branded cargo plane overran runway in Miami
summary: An airline cleaning company was mourning the loss of five employees who were identified as those killed Sunday when an Amazon-branded cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, striking the company’s van and a passenger SUV.
story: An airline cleaning company was mourning the loss of five employees who were identified as those killed Sunday when an Amazon-branded cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, striking the company’s van and a passenger SUV.

The deceased victims were Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, 53; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said at a news conference Tuesday. They were all in the van, owned by Professional Ocean Service Corp., a contract cleaning company for airline companies.

Five other people were injured and taken to the hospital, officials said. Eugenio Corredor, 79, and Ridoel Averhoff Diaz, 32, remain in critical condition, and Roosevelt Sebastian Perdomo Torres, 36, is stable.
The two pilots of the Boeing 767-300 aircraft, Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37, and Joseph Carol, 55, were treated and released.
The cleaning company said in a statement Tuesday that it was “heartbroken” by the deaths.

“Our employees are far more than the people who work beside us each day, they are family, and they are deeply loved,” the statement read. “Our hearts and prayers are with every employee and every family whose lives have been forever changed. We grieve with those who lost a loved one and pray for the healing and recovery of those who were injured.”
The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said that the National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation into the crash.

The aircraft was on its third trip that day when it overran the runway during a landing, NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said at a news conference Monday. Earlier Sunday, the plane traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, and then Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico.
It was returning from San Juan when it crashed.

Homendy said that upon landing back in Miami, the plane overran the runway and struck navigational aids and equipment before hitting the cleaning company’s Ford van, which was transporting the crew inside the airport.

The plane then careened through a perimeter fence and struck a Toyota SUV that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue outside the airport. The aircraft continued into the grass where it hit a fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed, Homendy said.
She described the scene as “devastating” and said the van had been “torn apart.”
Cellphone video obtained by NBC South Florida showed someone jumping out of the plane after the crash. A photo sent to NBC News showed a crew member being taken away on a gurney at the airport.
An Amazon spokesperson had previously said that the flight was operated by 21 Air.
Keith Winters, 21 Air’s CEO, said in a message on its website that it is cooperating with federal investigators and offered condolences to the victims’ families.
Homendy said it was too early to release much information about the factors that contributed to the crash, but said the plane’s flight data and cockpit voice recorder have been recovered.

One of Leon’s neighbors said he was very kind and would help her by taking her to appointments. A family member said Leon and his co-workers were at the end of their shift when the crash happened. The family member said Leon’s son was devastated.

title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”
story: LONDON — Flights departing from at least two major British airports have been grounded following a “technical issue,” officials said Tuesday.

London’s Heathrow Airport said in a statement Tuesday that it was working with Britain’s National Air Traffic Service to resolve the issue, advising passengers to check with their airlines for more information regarding their flights.
“Arriving flights are not currently impacted,” Heathrow said, although it advised passengers to check flight times.

London Gatwick Airport also said on X that it had been affected, and further north, Manchester Airport took to social media to warn that the issue “may result in delays.” Edinburgh Airport in Scotland issued a similar warning.
After earlier blaming a “technical issue,” the National Air Traffic Service said in an update on X that its engineers had “implemented a fix, and our flight system is starting to recover.”
Apologizing to passengers for the disruptions, it said flights were “departing and airspace is open, but recovery will take some time.”
Heidi Alexander, Britain’s transport minister, also took to social media to apologize. “I know this will be frustrating for passengers and I’m sorry,” she wrote on X.
With 84.5 million passengers last year, Heathrow ranked seventh in the table of the world’s busiest airports, according to data published by Airports Council International.
Airline Ryanair said in a statement that 65,000 of its passengers were disrupted and 50 scheduled flights were canceled because of the disruption.
British Airways canceled 96 flights, easyJet 92, and KLM 20, according to the aviation tracking site FlightRadar24.
Travel from Heathrow was severely disrupted in March last year when a massive fire at an electricity substation caused a predawn power outage at the global transport hub.
The closure affected more than 1,300 flights and 200,000 passengers.

After investigating 600 items of evidence related to the substation, the National Energy System Operator ruled out suspicious activity in a report saying a preventable moisture fault caused the fire, leaving almost 70,000 homes without power.

title: Does it feel like your hair is always greasy? Here’s why it could be happening
summary: Causes of greasy hair include genetics, hormonal imbalances and lifestyle. Browse the best ways to treat oily hair from brands like Garnier, Ouai, Batiste and more.
story: If your hair always seems to look and feel greasy no matter how much you wash it, you’re not alone. It’s a common struggle with plenty of potential culprits, including your hair and scalp type, hormones and genetics. “Oily hair is often misunderstood as a hygiene issue, when it’s really about scalp biology,” says board-certified trichologist Aga Tompkins. “Oil itself isn’t bad, it’s actually essential for a healthy scalp.”

To learn more, I spoke to three trichologists and dermatologists about common causes, treatments and misconceptions around greasy hair (more on these below). How I picked the best greasy hair treatments
To choose the best products that’ll help keep your hair less oily (and potentially reduce the time between washes), the trichologists I spoke to recommend considering the following factors:

Ingredients: Look for a shampoo that has niacinamide and tea tree oil to regulate sebum, as well as beta hydroxy acids (like salicylic acid) or alpha hydroxy acids (glycolic and lactic acid) to gently exfoliate your scalp, regulate oil and keep follicles clear without triggering rebound oil production, says Tompkins. Surfactants like sulfates might be good for those with oily hair because they grab onto and whisk away dirt and oil, experts say. However, they do strip your scalp of natural oils and can cause dryness and irritation, so use in moderation, Product type: Those with oily hair should use an exfoliating, scalp-balancing shampoo and a lightweight, volume-enhancing conditioner. (Only apply the conditioner to your ends to avoid weighing down your hair.) What causes greasy hair?

The most common cause is overactive sebaceous glands on the scalp, which produce excess oil (called sebum) to protect your hair and skin, according to the experts I spoke to. What triggers overactive sebaceous glands? Genetics can play a major role: Some people have a skin condition called seborrhea dermatitis, which means they are predisposed to higher oil production than others, says Tompkins. Hormonal fluctuations, stress and lifestyle habits (like frequent touching or brushing your hair) can also have a part in how fast oil spreads from your scalp down the hair shaft, says Sara Hallajian, a trichologist and founder of Ame Salon in Santa Monica, California.

If you notice that your hair gets greasier more quickly than others, your hair type may be the culprit. “Those with fine hair tend to show oil more quickly because there’s less surface area and cuticle layer to absorb it,” says Hallajian.
Can over-washing make greasy hair worse?

Yes, if you use harsh or stripping formulas. “The issue isn’t washing itself, but the ingredients,” says Tompkins. When you over-wash, you strip your scalp of its natural oils, and the scalp may respond by producing more oil to protect itself, she says. Harsh ingredients include drying alcohols (like isopropyl alcohol, which is common in many hair care products) and parabens (preservatives that can throw off your scalp’s oil production). Frequent washing with gentle products, on the other hand, helps regulate oil rather than stimulate excess production, says Tompkins.
How do you treat and prevent greasy hair?

The goal is to not over-cleanse and instead use products that gently remove buildup, says Tompkins. “Treating oily hair is less about ‘drying it out’ and more about balancing and regulating scalp function,” says Hallajian. In addition to ingredients that reduce oil production like niacinamide, glycolic acid and lactic acid, consider the following expert-recommended tips:

Avoid heavy conditioners or oils. Using styling products that are too heavy for your hair type and texture will make your hair look more oily. That includes conditioning hair masks, which can weigh down your hair.Use a clarifying shampoo once a week to remove buildup. Clarifying shampoos have heavier surfactants (cleansing agents that create a lather), which help remove oils from the scalp that normal shampoos aren’t strong enough to remove, experts say. But keep in mind that overusing a clarifying shampoo can strip too much oil from your hair and leave it dry and brittle.Focus on proper nutrition and control your stress. These are major factors that can throw off your scalp health, says Hallajian.

Focus on proper nutrition and control your stress. These are major factors that can throw off your scalp health, says Hallajian.
Frequently asked questions

There’s no universal schedule when it comes to how often you should wash your hair, experts say. “Some people may need to cleanse daily, while others do well every other day,” says Tompkins. The frequency depends on your scalp type, lifestyle and the products you use. For example, if you go to the gym and sweat everyday, you may need to wash more frequently (like every other day).
However, when you use a shampoo that’s made for oily scalps, you can wash more frequently (like every day) without disrupting your scalp’s balance.

You won’t be able to train your sebaceous glands to produce less oil, especially if the cause is hormonally or genetically driven. “Skipping washes alone rarely fixes oiliness and often makes it worse,” says Hallajian.

The root cause for greasy hair is similar for both men and women, but hormones can influence oil production differently. “Androgens, like testosterone, stimulate sebaceous glands, which is why men may experience oilier scalps overall,” says Hallajian. “Women often notice changes tied to menstrual cycles, pregnancy, postpartum shifts or perimenopause.”

If your oily hair is paired with itching, redness, flaking, scalp odor, inflammation or hair shedding, it may be a sign of an underlying condition like seborrheic dermatitis, hormonal imbalance, metabolic or inflammatory issues, says Hallajian. In those cases, you should see a professional for a scalp evaluation and/or medical referral.

title: What Happened in the Elizabeth Holmes Doc, According to Someone Who Saw It
summary: Here’s what the Elizabeth Holmes documentary was like according to a person who was at a screening at Sundance.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
A surprise documentary about Theranos founder and convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes has created instant buzz after a screening at a film festival and the release of a trailer that has gone viral.

Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was in attendance at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado when the documentary “You Can See Everything” was screened on Sept. 7. The film was directed by absurdist comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim and produced jaw-dropping reactions from those in the crowd.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” Keegan told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.

Holmes was the founder and CEO of the tech startup Theranos, which promised to revolutionize blood testing. She was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab following reports that the technology did not work and could deliver faulty results.

The new documentary, which will be released in October, features footage of Holmes and partner Billy Evans with their two children at a rental home in San Diego before Holmes entered federal prison in 2023. She is scheduled to be released in 2031.
“I think part of the film is exploring this question of Elizabeth Holmes’s perception of reality and about things that she’s done,” Keegan said.
A trailer released by the studio A24 on Sept. 7 shows a wide-eyed Holmes awkwardly only inches away from Fielder’s face as she speaks to him in one scene.

“I’m not that person,” Holmes says in the clip. “I can promise you that. I don’t have anything to deceive you on. Of course, I’m not deceiving you. I’m engaging with you as a human being. Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that.”
“OK. All right. OK, good chat,” Fielder replies.
The two then stare at each other for an uncomfortable duration.
“You’re being real right now?” Fielder asks.
“I’m always being real,” Holmes replies.
Keegan described a “strange feeling” produced by the interactions between Fielder and Holmes in the film.
“Fielder is very much a character in the film, and in some ways, it’s him trying to understand whether he believes Elizabeth Holmes or not,” Keegan said.

“I’m struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced,” Fielder said during the post-screening Q&A, according to Keegan. “I don’t know why they want me there. I’m a weird guy. I don’t get it. That messed with my head.”

The conversations between Holmes and “The Rehearsal” star are reportedly not the only surreal moments in the documentary. The film also includes an A-list Hollywood actress reenacting Fielder’s conversations with Holmes from prison. Fielder asked the attendees at the screening not to reveal the actress’s identity, according to Keegan.
NBC News reached out to Holmes for comment, but did not hear back. Holmes shared the movie trailer on her X account on Sept. 6 and wrote, “I’m always being real.”

“You Can See Everything” is the latest screen adaptation of the saga involving Holmes. HBO released the documentary “The Inventor” about Holmes in 2019, and then Amanda Seyfried played her in the 2022 Hulu series “The Dropout.”

title: Would Sheinelle Ever Join ‘RHONY’? Jenna Gets Answers About that Rumor
summary: Jenna Bush Hager asked Sheinelle Jones if she would consider joining the cast of Bravo’s “The Real Housewives of New York City.”
story: Sheinelle Jones beams into living rooms every day from New York City on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, so would she consider adding another iconic New York show to her resume?
On the Sept. 8 episode of the show, Sheinelle and Jenna chatted with the “RHONY” cast, and Jenna mentioned there had a been a rumor that Sheinelle would be one of the housewives on the program.
“By a show of hands, who thinks she should join next season?” Jenna asked, as the entire cast cheered and raised their hands.
“It’s like being in an encouraging classroom,” Sheinelle said.
Jenna then Sheinelle outright: “Would you ever do it?”
“We’re going to keep the suspense,” she said coyly.
“That’s a maybe,” Jenna said.
“There you go,” Sheinelle said.
“You’d be filming all day long,” Jenna said, while Sheinelle asked the cast if cameras were around them 24/7.
“She’s getting some fact finding info,” Jenna said, prompting Sheinelle to laugh.

Sheinelle may not be part of the “Real Housewives” universe, but fans can still check out the 16th season of “RHONY,” which premieres Sept. 8 at 8 p.m. ET on Bravo and streams the next day on Peacock.

The new season will see Season 15 returnees Sai De Silva, Erin Lichy and Jessel Taank joined by Hailey Glassman, Erika Hammond and Daisy Toye. Rounding out the cast is Carole Radziwill, back full-time on the reality show for the first time since 2018’s Season 10.
Radziwill has said her return to the franchise is an “opportunity” after her name appeared in files related the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.

“I mean, I felt like this isn’t something I shy away from,” Radziwill said at a press event Sept. 1. “Me and many, many, many, many more people found their names in these files. And it’s not something I shy away from because I think, really, it’s important to talk about it. It’s important to be transparent. Obviously, I didn’t know anything, as no one, you know, 20 years ago would have known anything.”

title: Sandra Bullock Pries Hoda Kotb for More Details About Her ‘Connection’ With Man on Plane
summary: Sandra Bullock asked Hoda Kotb for more information about he man she met on a plane, sparking talk about a possible love connection.
story: Sandra Bullock turned the tables on Hoda Kotb in order to try and get some intel on her love life.

Hoda sat down with Bullock and Nicole Kidman to discuss their upcoming movie, “Practical Magic 2,” but the “Speed” star wanted to find out more about the mystery man Hoda met on a plane and discussed when she visited TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Aug. 21.
Bullock said she saw the segment in which Hoda opened up about the encounter.
“A question was posed to you about a flight that you took, and there was a little conversation and a little sparklet? What happened?” Bullock asked.
“So I was on a plane and I sat next to some guy, and he’s super whatever,” Hoda said.
“Handsome? Super handsome?” Bullock fired back.
Hoda confirmed she and the man swapped phone numbers before they went their separate ways.

“I didn’t know if it was a connection like just a bond for a second, or was it something — I don’t know. I still don’t know,” she said, while Bullock looked at the camera and mouthed the words, “Call her,” promoting Hoda to laugh.
“This is my favorite interview ever,” Hoda howled, as Bullock mouthed “soft skin” while caressing her arm.
“This is intense,” Kidman joked.
“Did you say ‘soft skin’? You are so weird,” Hoda told Bullock.
“Well, that’s important. If you look at someone and you go, ‘Am I going to enjoy touching their very soft skin?’ You will enjoy it,” Bullock replied.

While chatting with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones last month, Hoda divulged details of what seemed like a meet cute with the mystery man, saying their chat on the plane was “firing on all cylinders.” After the flight, the pair bumped into each other again in Cannes while her company Joy 101 was there, and they said hello to each other. They would later text, but Hoda wasn’t sure where things stood. She did confirm the man was single.
“Look. There are connections,” she said. “I don’t know what it is.”

title: Sandra Bullock Shares How Her Kids Appear in ‘Practical Magic 2’ — and Their Reactions to Surprise Cameo
summary: Sandra Bullock’s two teen children had no idea they are in the upcoming “Practical Magic 2” until she gave them a sweet surprise.
story: Sandra Bullock’s two teen children had no idea they are in the upcoming “Practical Magic 2” until she gave them a sweet surprise.

Bullock adopted son Louis, now 16, in 2010 and daughter Laila, now 13, in 2015. She told Hoda Kotb that “Practical Magic 2” was the first movie set the teens were old enough to remember being on, and the first film in which they actually made the final cut.

Bullock, 62, spoke alongside co-star Nicole Kidman on the Sept. 8 episode of Hoda’s “Making Space” podcast about how her kids were involved in the highly anticipated sequel to the 1998 cult hit, which hits theaters Sept. 10.
She said her kids had several questions about life on set, from “Where are you going?” to “Can we watch?” and finally, “Can we be in it?”
But “every time I put them in the background before, it’s gotten cut,” Bullock said. “Sorry. Show business.”
Things were different with “Practical Magic 2,” though, and Bullock said she put their voices, “their essences,” in the film.

Using “little recordings from when they were babies and then all the way up,” Bullock was finally able to put her kids into one of her films. The teenagers didn’t find out until the film’s premiere in Los Angeles on Aug. 31.
“Last night when it came up, they’re all like, ‘That’s me?’ And they got to see themselves as babies and little toddlers. And yeah, it was very sweet,” she said.
“So they didn’t get cut out,” Bullock added with a laugh. “They’re kinda in it.”
Kidman, 59, is also a parent of teenagers, in addition to two adult children she has with ex-husband Tom Cruise. She shares Sunday Rose, 18, and Faith Margaret, 15, with ex-husband Keith Urban.
Her children were also on the set of “Practical Magic 2.”

“They’ve been on sets pretty much their whole lives,” Kidman told Hoda. “So it was more like they were in London in the summer, and it was just beautiful for them. And my niece was there, and so for us it was just a family kind of affair. And they would come and go and watch things, and both of them have seen this movie now. They hadn’t seen the original.”
She said her teens have since watched the original film in which Bullock and Kidman play the Owens sisters, who are the descendants of witches and learn the use of practical magic while growing up.
The two Oscar winners also tried to prepare Hoda, whose daughters are 9 and 7, for what it will be like when she becomes the mom of teenagers.

“I think it’s a joy,” Kidman said. “I mean, is it hard? Aspects of it can be challenging. But at the same time, is it extraordinary to accompany these people on their journey, on the beginning of their journey, and just say, ‘I’m here. I’m your guide. I’m hopefully your home, your safe place, and the world is your oyster?’”
Bullock described how she approaches parenting differently. While she is white, both of her children are Black.

“I mean, we’re different this, you know?” she said while gesturing to her skin. “I’m uber paranoid, and they will tell you. They’re like, ‘Mom, it’s going to be fine.’ I’m like, ‘It’s not fine. It’s not fine outside.’ The energy that is floating around our country and our world.

“Again, the color of their skin. They’re my babies, they’re my life, but no one knows that when they leave my house,” she continued. “So that is always in the forefront of my mind. But I’m now learning to trust them. Where they are now is extraordinary.”

title: From ‘Traitors’ to Red Carpet Debut, Phaedra Parks and CT Tamburello’s Relationship Timeline
summary: Fans shipped Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame and “Real Housewives” alum Phaedra Parks when they appeared on “The Traitors.” Now the pair admitted that they are dating.
story: Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame may have won Season 2 of Peacock’s “The Traitors” competition show, but he also began a connection that blossomed long after leaving the Scottish castle: he is in a relationship with fellow contestant Phaedra Parks, a mortician and “Real Housewives” alum.
Yes, that’s right — the chemistry that fans of the show spotted on screen eventually led to a relationship off-screen.
Could “faithful” fans have possibly willed this relationship into existence? We’ll never know ... but we can hope!
So, how did these “traitors” become “faithful” to each other? Here’s a timeline of key moments in Parks and Tamburello’s relationship.
Fall 2023: Parks and Tamburello Meet While Filming ‘The Traitors’
Tamburello, 46, and Parks, 52, film Season 2 of “The Traitors” on location in Scotland.
The second season of the show featured familiar faces — and notable rivals — from popular reality TV programs.

Tamburello made his way to the cast via MTV. He first appeared on “The Real World: Paris” then went on to find success on “The Challenge.” Per People, he has won “The Challenge” five times (plus two spinoff seasons) and competed in 19 seasons.
His “Challenge” rival, Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio, also competed in this season of “The Traitors.”

The witty and outspoken Parks starred on “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” from 2010 to 2017, as well as in 2025 and 2026. She now dabbles in several projects, and on her Instagram page, she describes herself as an “attorney to the stars,” mommy, mortician, model, actress and author.
On both shows, she sparred for screen time with fellow Atlanta “Housewives” star Shereé Whitfield.
Early 2024: ‘The Traitors’ Premieres — and Fans Watch Their Connection Unfold
Episodes of Season 2 of “The Traitors” aired from January to March 2024.
The vibes between the two were noticeable.

Tamburello may have a tough Boston accent, but he seemed to turn into a softie around Parks. And while Parks could eviscerate an opponent in 30 seconds or less, she seemed surprisingly sweet on Tamburello, calling him her “Castle Daddy.”

Tamburello ultimately helped remove Parks from the castle, but as he voted for her as a Traitor, he smiled and said, “I think you came on here to be the opposite of who you are in real life. And I think you’ve been the best Traitor we’ve seen yet.”
March 2024: These Fan Favorites Comment on Their Chemistry During Press Tour
In an interview that spring, Vulture flat out told Parks, “So the internet wants you and CT to be boyfriend and girlfriend.”
Parks replied, “Oh, god.”

She went on to say, “CT is a great guy, and we definitely had a wonderful connection. He’s a sweetheart. He’s a really good guy, and he’s attractive and all those good things. He’s a gentleman. There was never anything romantic between us at all. It was just a sweet, pure friendship.”
Tamburello shared similar sentiments in an interview with Entertainment Weekly in March 2024.

“No, nothing real happened, I’ll be honest with you,” he said in the interview. “It was fun. I loved her because she’s a cornball. She was great. I would say there was a sense of sincerity, for sure. But it was also playing a game, you know?”
August 2026: Parks Admits She Might Have More Than a Friendship With Tamburello
During a Sept. 4 appearance on “Jeff Lewis Live,” Parks said that she would be attending the Emmys with a date that was “not” platonic.
Admittedly wanting to make a splash with their relationship, Parks withholds details but shared that something has been brewing with a mysterious “CT” for a while.
A caller piped up to “connect the dots” for everyone.

“They were on ‘The Traitors’ together. She called him her ‘castle daddy’ on the show,” said a caller identified only as Megan. “So I know you want to wait to disclose it to the world, but please don’t plead the fifth. Let us know if it’s that CT.”
“Ummmm ... I think so,” Parks replied hesitantly.
Lewis confirmed that he could see Tamburello outside the studio, and that the “CT” Parks mentioned was definitely her “Traitors” competitor.
September 2026: Tamburello and Parks Hard Launch Relationship on the Red Carpet
Phaedra Parks doesn’t do anything halfway, and the hard launch of her relationship with Tamburello is no exception.
The pair stunned on the red carpet at the first night of the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on Sept. 5.

Along with photos from the evening, Parks posted this comment on her Instagram page on Sept. 6: “Some came for the awards. I came with the prize. Thank you to the real trophy for making a beautiful night even better.”
Fellow “Traitors” contestant and occasional “Challenge” rival Devenanzio used the same comment and hilariously paired it on Instagram with photos of him and Tamburello from the same event.
Parks posted a response: “We are a thropple.”

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Teases James and Oliver Phelps As New Castle Keepers
summary: A first look at James and Oliver Phelps, known as Fred and George Weasley in “Harry Potter” films, as Alan Cumming’s castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood.”
story: “The Traitors” is gearing up for its first season filled with “every day Americans” — and it appears host Alan Cumming is getting help from some famous twins.
TODAY has an exclusive first look at the new castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood,” James and Oliver Phelps.

Best known for playing Fred and George Weasley in the “Harry Potter” films, the actors will keep an eye on Cumming’s castle as he welcomes the new recruits and puts them through the ultimate game of deceit.
The clip, shared Sept. 7, begins with a glimpse at the reality show’s famous Scottish castle before a phone rings and one of the Phelps brothers answers.
“Keeper, is the castle set?” Cumming is heard asking, with one brother replying, “It is, Alan” while the other also makes an appearance and adds, “Oh, it is Alan.”
The brothers then raise the castle flag as Cumming says, “Let the games begin.”

While the U.S. version of “The Traitors” has only featured celebrities over its four seasons, “New Blood” will welcome 22 civilians into the Scottish Highlands castle. The cast along with their mischievous portraits were revealed on Aug. 12.

Once there, the game is the same with the contestants either chosen as a Traitor or Faithful. Determined to win the $250,000 prize, the Faithfuls will then seek out the Traitors and attempt to not get eliminated (aka “murdered”), while the Traitors try to deceit the Faithfuls and not get banished from the castle. As for James and Oliver Phelps, the actors will be on hand to help the competition be as treacherous as ever.
“The Traitors: New Blood” premieres Sept. 17 on NBC at 8 p.m. with back-to-back episodes. They will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
New episodes will air every Thursday at the same time on the network.
(Peacock and NBC are owned by NBCUniversal, TODAY’s parent company).

title: Oasis Frontmen and Brothers Liam Gallagher and Noel Gallagher Reunite on Red Carpet Following Feud
summary: The Gallagher brothers, Liam and Noel, made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.”
story: British band members and brothers Noel Gallagher, 59, and Liam Gallagher, 53, are responsible for megahits like “Wonderwall,” “Champagne Supernova” and the titular “Don’t Look Back in Anger.” Despite their success, the band split more than a decade ago due to the all-too-frequent feuds.

The Gallagher brothers made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger,” a new documentary about the behind-the-scenes drama surrounding their highly anticipated 41-date reunion tour in 2025.
The documentary opens in theaters on Sept. 11.
Could the tour have brought the brothers closer together? Perhaps. They certainly seemed at ease on the Venice red carpet, smiling, hugging, pulling faces and even holding hands in a victory pose.
Noel Gallagher even got playful and stuck his tongue out at the photographers during the red carpet.
Oasis had been broken up since August 2009 following a reported brawl between the two. Noel Gallagher then announced he was quitting the band after a show at a festival in Paris.
While the two had pursued their own solo careers, they announced their reunion tour in August 2024.
This is not the first time post-breakup that the brothers seem to have found a new rhythm together.
Last August, Noel Gallagher told the British radio show talkSPORT that his brother Liam Gallagher has been “amazing” and “smashing it.”
That was quite a turnaround for the brothers, who frequently sparred on social media and in interviews over the years.
“I guess when it’s all said and done, we’ll sit and reflect on it, but it’s great being back in a band with Liam,” Noel Gallagher said in the interview. “I forgot how funny he was.”
He continued, “Liam’s smashing it, and I’m proud of him.”

Noel Gallagher, who had been working as a solo artist alongside his band the High Flying Birds following Oasis’ breakup, added about his brother, “I’ve got to say, I kind of look at him and think, ‘Good for you, mate.’ He’s been amazing.”

title: Behind Raygun’s ‘Cringe’ Olympic Breakdancing Routine Is An Oddly Sweet Love Story
summary: Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, becoming the center of ridicule. But husband Samuel Free stuck by her side.
story: When Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, she became the focus of memes, ridicule and a deluge of parodies.
But one person wasn’t laughing. In fact, unlike pretty much all of social media at the time, he found her moves rather breathtaking.

Samuel Free, Gunn’s husband and coach, is among the key figures featured in the new Netflix documentary “Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly,” which chronicles the events around the viral routine that set social media aflame.

The documentary, which was released Sept. 1, includes voices from other dancers who were less-than-impressed by Gunn’s breakdancing skills. But Free stands fiercely by Gunn’s moves, which included some, uh, odd choices like the sprinkler and a pose meant to mimic a kangaroo. He goes so far as to say that he was captivated by her routine.
“I was struck by the beauty of her performance,” Free says in the documentary of her Olympics appearance.
Free’s comments in the documentary have prompted social media users to describe the two as a match made in heaven, with some even hoping to find the same level of devotion in a partner.
“May all of us have partners as supportive as Raygun‘s husband was at the Olympics,” one social media user wrote on Threads.

Raygun went viral after her two performances in Paris did not earn a single point from the judges across four rounds. There, she lost by a combined 36-0 to two competitors. And her moves elicited everything from memes to Halloween costumes.
How Did Raygun Meet Her Husband, Samuel Free?
Raygun’s connection to the sport actually goes back to Free, who is responsible for introducing her to breakdancing, the documentary shows.
Free, a breakdancer himself, once competed under the name Sammy Sex. He says in the doc that he became drawn to the art form at an early age when he watched the 1984 film “Breakin.’”
“They’re doing big moves,” Free says. “I didn’t even know people could do this!”

He says he kept up with breakdancing through the years, which ended up being a “sticking point” in many of his romantic relationships throughout his 20s — that is, until he met Gunn while working at a call center.
“I have a life-changing moment,” Free recalls of meeting Gunn. “I remember walking past this girl in the break room.”

The two ended up hitting it off, according to the film. Gunn, who was in college at the time, says that Free “opened up my world.” For Gunn, one particularly pivotal moment was when he took her to a breaking battle, she says.
“Walking into this space felt like I walked into a movie,” Gunn says in the documentary.
It was after that battle, during which she was inspired by one of the women dancers, that she decided that she wanted to pursue breakdancing. And right by her side was Free.

“Sammy was my cheer squad, my fan, my biggest supporter,” Gunn, a university lecturer whose research revolved around breaking as well, says in the film. “He’s special ... makes you feel like you can do things when you’re around him.”
Free, who eventually started to coach her, says that they began “building a life together.” And in 2018, the two got married.
“Our wedding was so beautiful,” Gunn says over footage from their big day, which appeared to include quite a bit of craziness on the dance floor. “We were just so happy.”
How Did Free Help His Wife Prepare For The Olympics?
The two speak in the film about their experience preparing for the Olympics after Gunn had qualified to represent Oceania. They say that Gunn hit the gym and Free pushed her to train hard.
“I was like, ‘As your husband, I am in awe of how hard you’re working. Props to you. As your coach, you need to work harder. This is not clean,’” Free recounts.

In the lead-up to Paris, the couple says that they realized it was unlikely she’d best any of the other competitors. So instead of focusing on power moves — like windmills and headspins, for example — they decided to take a different approach. Free suggested they shift the routine into an ode to Australia, helping her incorporate moves reminiscent of swimming and the now-infamous kangaroo freeze, they recount.
While in Paris, some others were weary of what Gunn had planned to do, Free was stoked.
“This is Rachael’s moment. It’s her saying, ‘I’m doing me,’” Free says.
What Did Raygun’s Husband Think Of The Aftermath Of The Performance?

The aftermath of Gunn’s performance was pretty ugly, the documentary shows. And Free says that the onslaught of memes, trolling and bullying from the internet was a “massive trauma.” At the time conspiracies spread that Free was on the committee that had chosen Gunn to represent their country in the Olympics — something that’s been shot down by organizers, other competitors and the couple themselves. Still, the two spent a few months in the Netherlands in an attempt to lie low and recover from the incident.
It’s been a while since the 2024 Paris games, and Gunn admits that she was “cringe.”
“I brought shame and embarrassment on the country,” she says.
However, she underscores that she’s still dancing and that “Paris hasn’t defeated me.” As for Free, he’s still standing right by her side.
He says that his wife’s “performance connected with people, whether that’s genuine excitement and entertainment or outrage.”
“It generated discourse and got the entire world talking,” he says.

title: After ‘Ted Lasso’ Feature, Negro Leagues Baseball Museum ‘Can Hardly Handle’ Surge In Visitors, Its President Says
summary: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And it’s been flooded with visitors ever since.
story: Kansas City, Missouri’s Negro Leagues Baseball Museum is now dealing with a good problem to have.

The historical institution, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And since, the museum’s president Bob Kendrick tells TODAY.com, the establishment has been flooded with visitors. Sales, Kendrick says, are up around 50% to 60% compared to where they were last year at this time.

“I’ll tell you — it has superseded anything that I could have ever even remotely imagined,” Kendrick says of the outpouring of interest in the museum from the show. “I honestly did not know that it would have this kind of interest and immediate impact on the museum.”

While the show’s third season, which wrapped in May 2023, ended with star and co-creator Jason Sudeikis’ character Ted Lasso leaving his life in the UK for Kansas City, the new season is all about his hop back across the pond. This time, Ted is tasked with helping to lead AFC Richmond women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds, to success.

But the first episode of the new season doesn’t start in the UK. Ted, who’s now working in a grocery store and parenting his son, still needs some convincing to leave the stability behind for the coaching gig abroad. And several of his old friends, including Rebecca, Keeley and Higgins, show up in KC to do just that.

While there, Higgins, played by Jeremy Swift, attempts to hit up the American Jazz Museum — which is housed in the same building as the NLBM — but finds it unexpectedly closed for the day. So he ends up taking a tour of the baseball establishment and becomes wildly moved by the figures he’s introduced to. One of these impactful players is the legendary Satchel Paige, widely recognized as one of the best pitchers in the history of the game. Paige’s career in the Negro Leagues began the 1920s.

“Satchel was a showman. He had a wild throwing style and all these crazy names for his pitches. ‘The Hesitation.’ The Midnight Creeper.’ ‘The Dipsy-Do’,” an NLBM employee, played by actor Milan Carter, tells Higgins. “Many thought old Satch would be the first to break the major league color barrier. He wasn’t. But he finally got in at the age of 42. Oldest rookie in history, and he was still incredible.”
As the NLBM staff member says in the show, “the Negro Leagues were glorious.”

“They didn’t do it for fame or fortune. They did it ‘cause to not play would have been unacceptable,” the staff member says of the leagues, which were formed in 1920 as a response to a decades-long unwritten “gentleman’s agreement” between club owners that kept Black players out of all professional leagues with white players.

The visit leaves a huge impression on Higgins, who is seen later in the episode, decked out in a Kansas City Monarchs jersey. The Monarchs were one of the most successful teams in the Negro Leagues and boasted Paige as one of its alumni.
Kendrick tells TODAY.com that the episode’s representation of the museum was moving.

“The scene was so beautifully done,” Kendrick says. “The care, the concern, the understanding of the essence of what Negro Leagues history represented both on and off the field —you saw that in that scene.”
The only complaint he’s gotten?

“I got a lot of calls, people ask me why wasn’t I in it. Because they wanted me to be the guy that was talking about Satchel Paige,” he says, before laughing. “What I told him was, ‘Number one, you never play yourself. You go find somebody who’s younger and better looking for you.’”
Kendrick explains that the NLBM scenes were filmed about a year ago. Back then, he says he had no idea what would happen after the episode aired.

“Perhaps I was a little bit naive on just how big this show really is,” he says. “It has just absolutely captivated the hearts and the imaginations of ‘Lasso’ fans around the world, and it obviously has exposed Negro League’s history and this museum to millions of people around the globe.”
Kendrick, who met Sudeikis years ago at a holiday ceremony, says that the “Ted Lasso” creator has visited the museum and been a fan for some time.

“There are many great attractions here in Kansas City, and for Jason to write us into this this love letter to Kansas City speaks volumes about what this museum meant to him,” he says. “I was here on the set when they were shooting it, so I had seen it already. I saw it in real time, but when I saw it in the show, it was very emotional for me.”

Now that Paige has even more fans, Kendrick says that there’s a plethora of Negro Leagues stars that people can look into, like the great Martín Dihigo, perhaps the most versatile player in baseball history. Dihigo, whose nickname is “El Maestro,” hailed from Cuba and began playing professionally in 1922.

“He was essentially Shohei Ohtani before we ever knew who Shohei Ohtani was. Martín Dihigo played all nine positions and played all nine of them well,” Kendrick says, referencing the current Los Angeles Dodgers two-way phenom.

He added that Dihigo is among the only baseball players “in the history of our sport to be enshrined into five different countries’ baseball halls of fame. He’s in the Mexican, Cuban, Venezuelan, Dominican, and in Cooperstown.”

As more people continue to be introduced to the museum through “Ted Lasso,” Kendrick says that the institution’s existing plans to expand and move out of their current space has become even more important.

“A new, much larger, expansive Negro Leagues baseball museum is looming on the horizon,” he says. “I need more space now to handle all these people and to expand on the stories that we have and to tell new stories.”

title: Patriots Cheerleaders Join Savannah Bananas’ ‘Dad Bod Cheer Squad’ For Epic Routine
summary: During a recent Savannah Bananas baseball game, the team’s official “Dad Bod Cheer Squad” known as the Man-Nanas, joined forces with the New England Patriots cheerleaders at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts for a routine that’s been scoring big with fans.
story: It’s the collab we never knew we needed.
