During a recent Savannah Bananas baseball game, the team’s official “Dad Bod Cheer Squad” known as the Man-Nanas, joined forces with the New England Patriots cheerleaders at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts for a routine that’s been scoring big with fans.
The grand slam of a number has gone viral with nearly four million views on Instagram alone as of Sept. 6, since it was posted just over a day prior. And after seeing it, you’ll understand why.
The video begins with the Patriots cheerleaders, performing to a mashup of several songs including Destiny’s Child’s “Lose My Breath, Missy Elliott’s “Lose Control” and Beyoncé’s “Formation.”
Pretty soon, the Man-Nanas join the fun. And together, the parties crush the routine as the stadium explodes into cheers.
It’s pretty difficult to decide who does it better. As the caption says, it’s “safe to say @the_man_nanas gave the @patriotscheerleaders a run for their money 😉”
The performance was part of the Savannah Bananas’ two-night series against the Loco Beach Coconuts at Gillette Stadium on Aug. 28 and 29.

The team, which has amassed a following for their viral dance numbers and unique spin on the sport, which they call “Banana Ball,”  also invited several others for memorable performances during the series including country star Keith Urban. According to the team’s social media accounts, the event was popular, selling out both nights with 130,000 fans.

title: Bindi Irwin Posts Sweet Video of Dad Steve Irwin Reflecting on Her Birth, 20 Years After His Death
summary: Bindi Irwin, daughter of Australian wildlife conservationist and television personality Steve Irwin, honored her father on the recent 20th anniversary of his death.
story: Bindi Irwin, daughter of Australian wildlife conservationist and television personality Steve Irwin, honored her father on the recent 20th anniversary of his death.
Bindi Irwin shared an emotional Instagram post Sept. 4 in remembrance of her father, who died in 2006 after a stingray pierced his heart with a poisonous barb.

The post not only included some moving words about the beloved Steve Irwin’s impact on her life and the greater movement around conservation but also a heartbreakingly beautiful video of the “Crocodile Hunter,” reflecting on her birth — something he called “the most incredible wildlife encounter of my life.”
Bindi Irwin, who’s now a zookeeper and conservationist herself, wrote in the caption that “20 years ago, today, the world lost the most passionate and dedicated wildlife conservationist.”

“Our family lost our superhero. My mum lost the love of her life; my brother and I lost the greatest dad. Grief never truly leaves us; we walk alongside it every day,” Bindi Irwin wrote of her father, who died at age 44. “Where there is enormous grief, there is even greater love. In the last 20 years, I have watched the world mourn my dad with our family.
She added that she had “always thought that my dad’s legacy is wildlife conservation.”
“It turns out, his legacy is love,” Bindi Irwin wrote. “For our planet and for each other.”

In the video, Steve Irwin takes viewers through the story of Bindi Irwin’s birth in July 1998. He explains that the obstetrician, “an absolute legend of a man,” encouraged him to help with the delivery. After a bit of teamwork, Steve Irwin recalls, his daughter was born.
“I swear she’s fitted right in here in the palms of my hands,” Steve Irwin says in the video. “I was flabbergasted.”

He also explains that his daughter’s name comes from that of his favorite crocodile Bindi. His wife Terri Irwin added the middle name Sue after the couple’s dog Sui, who often made appearances on television alongside Steve Irwin.

“So Bindi Sue Irwin.  ... It was a combination of adrenaline and just emotion,” he says in the video. “It was like a euphoric feeling. I was in total utopia. We both were. To bring this little person into the world. For me to deliver my daughter was a very special moment. I can’t dwell on it too long because I start to cry. It was so special.”
Steve Irwin adds that after he cut the umbilical cord, he couldn’t help but pick up his baby girl and show her off to everyone in the hospital.

“I’ve grabbed that little thing, that little baby, and we’re in the maternity ward of a very special hospital where a lot of women have given birth,” he recalls. “And I ran around the hospital, ‘Look at this! Look at this!’”
The nurses and other mothers in the ward were already well acquainted with the concept of a newborn, he adds.
“And they’re like, “Yes, we’ve got our own,’” he remembers them saying. “’Yeah, but you haven’t got one like this one! Look at this little beauty! Look at this little beauty!”
He says he is “the proudest father on the face of the earth, no doubt.”

Steve Irwin passed away when Bindi Irwin was 8 years old. Her brother, Robert Irwin, was almost three years old. His death occurred during the filming of documentary “Ocean’s Deadliest,” which was released in 2007.
Bindi Irwin wrote in her post that her 5-year-old daughter, Grace Warrior Irwin Powell, watches Steve Irwin’s documentaries every morning.

“She feels utterly loved by her ‘grandpa crocodile’ without ever having met him. My dad left a lasting impact so poignant that it will ripple out for generations to come,” she wrote. “I believe with my whole heart that his love will live on forever. In all of us. In every kindness we show to the Earth. And that is a life and legacy worth celebrating.”
Bindi Irwin concluded the emotional post with a message to her late father.

“Dad, I love you with my whole heart. Thank you for being our guardian angel,” Bindi Irwin wrote. “And most of all, thank you for watching over my daughter now, too. She loves you so much. We all do.”

Other members of the Irwin family have paid tribute to Steve Irwin, including his wife Terri Irwin. The couple, who met in 1991, married the following year, according to the family’s website. In lieu of a honeymoon, they embarked on a crocodile rescue mission.
Terri Irwin wrote in an Instagram post Sept. 4 that “grief still walks with me like my shadow.”

“With the passing of time I have gained more perspective and understanding. We were together as a family, on our crocodile research expedition, for what was to be our final six weeks together,” Terri Irwin wrote. “Ours was to be a long and sweet goodbye. Steve spent time with Bindi and Robert building swings and climbing trees. We all slowed down. Time slowed down.”
She concluded her post, calling on fans to treasure their loved ones.
“I believe that all of us, every one of us, gets to say goodbye,” Terri Irwin wrote. “We just may not know that we’re saying it. Hold every moment dear with the ones you love. Until we meet again.❤️”

title: How Megan Moroney’s First Heartbreak Kickstarted Her Music Career
summary: Megan Moroney’s rise in the country music scene was fueled by teenage heartbreak and a trip to Guitar Center, she tells Willie Geist.
story: Megan Moroney’s rise in the country music scene was fueled by teenage heartbreak and a trip to Guitar Center.

The 28-year-old, behind hits like “Bless Your Heart” and “I’m Not Pretty,” has built a brand on vulnerable lyrics and all-things pink, leading to her current world tour. In between one of her “Cloud 9 Tour” stops in New York City, Moroney spoke to Willie Geist about the start of her success on TODAY’s Sunday Sitdown.
During their chat, the singer revealed that she inherited her music genes from her dad, who taught her to play guitar and also worked a second job as a musician.
Moroney, who grew up in Douglasville, Georgia, spoke to Willie about the pivotal moment in her childhood that prompted her to pick up a guitar.
“When I was, like, 16, I injured my knee in cheerleading. That’s why I have this gnarly scar right here,” she said, showing Willie the proof.
She continued, “I had nothing else to do but sit down and learn how to play guitar.”

She started learning how to play Deana Carter’s “Strawberry Wine.” But while she was trying to get a grasp of the instrument, she dealt with a second dose of bad luck — she experienced her first heartbreak.

“I got my first guitar, shortly after that, (I) got my heart broken for the first time. I wouldn’t stop crying, so my dad took me to Guitar Center,” she recalled. “And I remember there was a Memorial Day sale. But when I took the Taylor (guitar) down, my dad goes to pay for it. And (they’re) like, ‘Oh. This one’s not on sale.’”
Moroney was determined to get her hands on the instrument, so she had to work some magic.

“I remember looking at my dad. And I was like, ‘I’ve had my heart broken, once this week. I can handle it again, if you don’t want to get it for me.’ And that’s how I ended up with my first Taylor,” she shared and laughed.

That moment was the start of what has become a major country music career. Through her songs, Moroney’s fans are able to connect with her and relate to the relationship experiences she often reflects in her music.
Willie mentioned that Moroney refers to these intimate moments with her fans when she is on stage as “group therapy.”
Moroney said she uses that term because her shows feel as though she and her fans are together in a “collective effort,” to release their emotions.
“It’s very empowering to be in a room where everyone feels the same way, you know?” she pointed out. “It’s like, ‘Wow. This person got treated like s—, too.’ And we’re angry about it, together.”
Moroney also spoke about being an “overthinker,” a quality that she says has helped her develop her songwriting skills.
“That’s the best way that I’ve found to move on from things is when I take those emotions and I turn it into art. Now we all get to enjoy it,” she shared.
However, making music that reflects aspects of her personal life also brings interest and questions about her romances, especially around the subjects of her songs about love gone wrong, she said.
Moroney said she has become better at managing that side of stardom. But she added that she used to struggle with it.

“At that point, there were definitely nights where I would cry myself to sleep ‘cause I felt so misunderstood and I wanted to tell people everything,” she revealed when speaking about the early parts of her career.
It was challenging “trying to find the balance of not telling everyone my entire personal life, but also letting people know, like, ‘This is how I feel,’” Moroney said, laughing.
She mentioned her song “Who Hurt You?” from her third album “Cloud 9” as an example of a more private track.
“I purposely wrote it so that people wouldn’t ask me questions about it. If you listen to the song, (and) you still have questions, I got no answers for you,” she said.
Setting boundaries have come with age and a few years in the music industry, she said.
These days, she told Willie she has a newfound sense of confidence that is expressed in her newest album.

“I think it has a lot to do with me just getting a little bit older. I’m 28 now. So I trust myself a lot more. I think everyone can relate to when you grow up, you have a lot more experience and you trust that no matter what life throws at you, you’re gonna be OK,” she explained. “And being able to feel that way just kind of spilled into my writing, naturally, That’s where I’m at (in) life.”

title: Ariana Grande and Ricky Alvarez Are Back: Here’s Their Relationship Timeline
summary: Some Ariana Grande fans know Ricky Alvarez from when Grande was spotted alongside him licking a doughnut on a counter — a moment many online have referred to as “donutgate.”
story: Some Ariana Grande fans know Ricky Alvarez from when Grande was spotted alongside him licking a doughnut on a counter — a moment many online have referred to as “donutgate.” Other fans may know his name from his famous shoutout in her hit “Thank U, Next”: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh.”
Some may even recognize him from old concert videos, when he was a backup dancer on her first arena tour, “The Honeymoon Tour” in 2015, when their offstage public romance began.
Now, years later, Alvarez is once again the center of fandom conversations as Grande is seemingly back in a relationship with him, per recent buzzy Instagram posts and public sightings.
From backup dancer to boyfriend, breakup to rekindling, here’s a timeline of key moments in the relationship between Grande and Alvarez.
April 2014: Ricky Alvarez Becomes One of Ariana Grande’s Backup Dancers
Alvarez made his onstage debut with Grande while the pop star was in the middle of her own big moment: performing her hit song “Problem” for the first time live at the Radio Disney Music Awards.
At the time, Grande was rumored to be single, although she was spotted kissing former on-again-off-again beau Jai Brooks at the iHeart Radio Music Awards a month later.
February 2015: Ariana Grande Starts Her “Honeymoon Tour,” With Ricky Alvarez Backup Dancing
Grande kicked off her first arena tour with Alvarez as one of her male backup dancers.
June 2015: Relationship Rumors First Spark

Fans first started to speculate about a relationship between Grande and Alvarez after they shared an onstage kiss during New York City Pride, around a couple months after the singer reportedly split from rapper Big Sean.

In the months following the kiss, Grande proceeded to share romantic clips of the pair — including many of them goofing off together before and after shows, primarily on her now-defunct Snapchat account.
July 2015: The Famous “Donutgate” Unfolds
Alvarez was alongside the singer when she was captured on camera at Wolfee Donuts in California, licking a doughnut on the store’s counter and declaring “I hate America.”
In the same video, Grande is also captured kissing Alvarez — marking the couple’s first on-camera kiss following New York City Pride.
In an extended statement posted on X, Grande apologized to her fans and insisted, “I am EXTREMELY proud to be an American.”
She also said her comments were meant to be private, aimed at her friend who was purchasing the doughnuts, TODAY.com previously reported.
May 2016: Ariana Grande Releases “Dangerous Woman” Album, With Nods to Ricky Alvarez

When Grande released her third studio album “Dangerous Woman,” many fans speculated that some of the romance songs like “Moonlight,” “Knew Better/Forever Boy” and “Into You” were written about her then-beau.
In an interview with Billboard that same month, her longtime friend and co-writer Victoria Monet confirmed that “Moonlight” was based off a nickname Alvarez had given her.

“That’s what Ricky called her one night. I think it was after their first kiss,” Monet told the magazine. “He waited to kiss her for a long time, and she was really impressed. He’s such a gentleman, and the song is a great little bookmark of the start of their relationship.”
Grande’s comment to the publication was less detailed: “We’re happy. I’m a very happy girl. I have a healthy life right now, and I think that’s all anyone cares to know. The end.”
July 2016: Fans Speculate the Couple Split, Ariana Grande Posts Hinting Tweets
Grande first started to fuel breakup rumors when she took to then-Twitter to write “life is wild” and “change is f****** fantastic,” according to a fan account on Instagram.
The singer did not publicly confirm the breakup at the time.
November 2018: Ariana Grande Releases “Thank U, Next” With a Lyric for Ricky Alvarez, And He Reacts
Grande released her hit “Thank U, Next,” in which she name-dropped Alvarez alongside Big Sean, Pete Davidson and Mac Miller, her other former beaus.
“Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh,” she sang.
After the song came out, Alvarez posted an Instagram story reacting to his shoutout. In the clip, he zooms in on his face as Grande sings his name.
In a story posted right after, he wrote in part: “Nothing but gratitude ... those songs are fire tho... you’re welcome.”
January 2019: Ricky Alvarez Attended Ariana Grande’s “7 Rings” Release Party
Alvarez attended Grande’s party for the release of her hit single “7 Rings” and shared an Instagram photo from the festivities, posing with two photographers and directors from her team.
Grande commented “the best team see y’all on touuuur,” with two camera emojis.
February 2019: Ariana Grande Comments on Ricky Alvarez’ Reaction to “Thank U, Next” Feature
During her interview on the Zach Sang show, Grande responded to Alvarez’s initial reaction to her “Thank U, Next” lyric about him.

“Ricky loved it. He was proud. But Ricky was like, ‘Why did I get the worst line?’ And I was like, ‘What do you mean?’ He was like, ‘Everyone else’s line is so nice, and mine is like, ‘Man, f*** him, he’s trash,’” the singer recalled.
She continued: “I was like, ‘I could have said that, I could’ve said ‘Wrote some songs about Ricky,’ never mind he’s trash,’ But I didn’t. I said, ‘Now I listen and laugh.’”
March 2019: Ariana Grande Starts Her “Sweetener World Tour,” Ricky Alvarez Joins As A Photographer
Alvarez got back into professional work with Grande when she kicked off her “Sweetener World Tour.” He joined the crew as a photographer, per multiple fan reports.
April 2019: Ricky Alvarez Co-Directs Ariana Grande’s “Monopoly” Music Video, Photographs Her Coachella Performance

Alvarez took his camera work with Grande a step further when he collaborated with her longtime photographer and videographer Alfredo Flores to make a music video for “Monopoly,” her single with Victoria Monet.
After the video premiered, he took to Instagram to declare the song one of his “favorite slaps yet,” per his post’s caption.
Later that month, Alvarez photographed Grande’s headlining performances at Coachella.
He posted a photo he captured on Instagram from the first weekend, and the singer commented a praying emoji with a black heart.
June 2026: Ariana Grande Starts Changing “Thank U, Next” Lyrics About Ricky On Stage

Around seven years, several public relationships and one brief marriage later, Grande alluded to the pair’s potential rekindling — or at least friendship — when she first changed the lyric about him in “Thank U, Next” during her “Eternal Sunshine Tour” stop in Austin, Texas.
“Wrote some songs about Ricky / And they still kinda slap,” she sang.
Two nights later, she changed the lyrics again during her birthday show in the same city: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / I know he’s still got my back.”
Meanwhile, relationship rumors about the pair swirled as TMZ photographed the pair together multiple times throughout the summer.
At Grande’s Brooklyn, New York tour stop, she changed the lyrics again: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / We always find our way back.”
July 2026: Ricky Alvarez Includes Ariana Grande in an Instagram Post
Alvarez posted Grande on his Instagram for the first time in years when he included a visual from her “Eternal Sunshine Tour” in a photo carousel.
The singer commented a heart emoji on the post.
August 2026: Ariana Grande Posts Instagram Carousel Including Ricky Alvarez, Confirming Romantic Spark. Singer Reveals New Matching Tattoo
Grande practically confirmed the relationship rumors when she posted an Instagram carousel Aug. 12 that included two photos of the couple cozying up.
A few days after she shared the post online, Grande debuted a new tattoo across her upper chest at her tour stop in London: “I do love you.”
Alvarez also has the phrase tattooed in the same spot, but his appears in a different font.
Most recently during the final show of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour Sept. 1, she changed the “Thank U, Next” lyrics once again: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / I’m tryna make him my last.”
Although they continue to share their affection online and at Grande’s tour stops, neither of them have publicly commented on the current status of their relationship.

title: Julia Louis-Dreyfus Reveals She Had A Nursery Next To Dressing Room on ‘Seinfeld’
summary: Julia Louis-Dreyfus joined podcast “Friends Keep Secrets” and reflecting on having children while filming “Seinfeld.”
story: Julia Louis-Dreyfus was juggling a whole lot while filming hit sitcom “Seinfeld.”

The comedian, who played Elaine on the show, opened up about what it was like to have kids while filming the nine-season NBC hit during a recent episode of podcast “Friends Keep Secrets.” Louis-Dreyfus revealed that her children often came to work with her.
“I had a nursery,” Dreyfus, 65, told hosts Benny Blanco, Lil Dicky and his wife Kristin Batalucco during the Sept. 1 podcast episode. “I had a nursery right next to my dressing room.”
Louis-Dreyfus has two sons with husband Brad Hall. Her eldest, Henry Hall, was born in 1992 while her younger son, Charlie Hall, was born in 1997.

“Seinfeld,” which also starred Jerry Seinfeld, Michael Richards and Jason Alexander, aired from 1989 to 1998. Louis-Dreyfus said on the podcast that raising children at the height of the show’s fame was no walk in the park.
“It was really hard,” Louis-Dreyfus said. “I’m not even sure if it was the right thing to do.”
Though Louis-Dreyfus found parenthood challenging at the time, she said she enjoyed the experience immensely.
“I wish I had one more, actually!” she told the hosts.
During the podcast, Louis-Dreyfus also shared that there was  “tons” of friction on the set of the show.
“It’s hard to do anything really well, and it takes a lot of work, and you’re going to butt heads,” she said.

During its run, “Seinfeld” became a smash hit, winning 10 Emmy awards and three Golden Globes among many other awards. Louis-Dreyfus also earned an Emmy award for outstanding supporting actress in a comedy in 1996 and a Golden Globe in 1994 for best supporting actress while on the show.

While she enjoyed a great deal of success in her role as Elaine, Louis-Dreyfus has been open about how difficult it was to enter motherhood at the time. And yet, she once told television host and cook Ina Garten that the experience was “fabulous.”
“I was becoming very famous at at this time, it really kept all of that in perspective,” Louis-Dreyfus told Garten on an episode of show “Be My Guest.”
She also said that as time went on, the show didn’t do much to hide her pregnancies.
“The first go round, I stood behind things. I carried boxes,” she told Garten. “By the time I was pregnant the second time, nobody cared, and it was like it wasn’t happening.”

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Boys Show Off The Chinese Skills They Learned From Carl Schmidt
summary: While many of the guys in the latest season of “Love Island USA” have yet to master the language of love, they do seem to be picking up Chinese fairly quickly.
story: While many of the guys in the latest season of “Love Island USA” have yet to master the language of love, they do seem to be picking up lingo from another culture fairly quickly.

Thanks to some coaching from islander Carl Schmidt, who speaks Mandarin and is of Chinese descent, fellow Season 8 finalists Sincere Rhea, Zach Georgiou and Bryce Alakai recently revealed that they’ve learned a couple Chinese words. And in an interview with Glamour magazine, the boys showed off a bit of their skills.
In the video, shared Sept. 1, Sincere tells the outlet, “We can say some things in Mandarin,” before asking the crew to demonstrate.
“You guys ready?” he asks.
Zach cuts in, saying “Ni hao ma? Wo jiao Zach,” which translates to “How are you? My name is Zach.”
Bryce continues the convo, adding, “Wo jiao Bryce. Ni ne?” which roughly translates to “My name is Bryce, how about you?”
“Wo jiao Sincere,” Sincere adds.
“Ni men dou shi wode pengyou,” Carl says, which translates to “you are all my friends.”
“Feichang hao,” a few of them chime in, which means “very good!”
Not bad, boys.
As Carl tells the outlet in the video, “Mandarin’s really hard because it’s tonal.”
“You have to have the right pronunciation and the right tone,” Carl says, before adding that he also received some criticism for his Mandarin skills during the season.

Carl came into Season 8 during the second half of the show as a bombshell, quickly becoming close with fellow islander Aniya Harvey. As one of the few cast members of Asian descent in the show’s history, Carl wasn’t shy about introducing aspects of his culture to his connection. In an early interaction between the two, Carl taught Aniya some Mandarin. Though it appears that the guys of the villa also got a few language lessons from Carl, who also speaks some Japanese.

The video comes just after the Season 8 reunion aired on Aug. 31. Among the highlights was the reveal that Carl and Aniya, whose nonlinear relationship on the show eventually had a happy ending, had not yet defined their relationship but were still exploring their connection. Their moms, however, are besties.
“They’re out hanging out right now,” Aniya told host Andy Cohen. “They’re texting each other, calling each other.”

title: After Years Of Criticizing Marriage, Gloria Steinem Got Married. All About Her Husband David Bale
summary: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem, the journalist and activist, who died Sept. 2, was married to Bale for three years until his death in December 2003.
story: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem spoke out for decades against the pressures of marriage. But then she met someone.

While Steinem had long railed against the institution of marriage — once telling local Washington outlet the Spokesman-Review in 1973 that it was an “unconstitutional contract with one party having the financial responsibilities and the other charged with providing domestic and sexual services” — she eventually met entrepreneur David Bale. The journalist and activist, who died Sept. 2, was married to Bale for three years until his death in December 2003.
For Steinem, who got married at 66, the marriage was not a deviation from her feminist values, but rather a reflection of them. It was also a surprise, she said.

“Though I’ve worked many years to make marriage more equal, I never expected to take advantage of it myself,” Steinem said in a 2000 press release issued by political action committee Voters For Choice, which she co-founded. “I hope this proves what feminists have always said—that feminism is about the ability to choose what’s right at each time of our lives.”
As fans look back on the life and legacy of Gloria Steinem, here’s what we know about her marriage.

While she told Glamour earlier this year that she’s been in love “three or four times,” Steinem married just once. Steinem, largely seen as the face of the second-wave of feminism, met Bale in October 1999 in Los Angeles at a fundraiser for Voters For Choice.

The South Africa-born Bale, (actor Christian Bale’s father), had been a longtime environmentalist, entrepreneur and animal rights activist. He was also known for importing skateboards and jeans from Asia to England.
Bale’s marriage to Steinem was his third. And he had four children from his previous marriages.

According to the Washington Post, the two tied the knot in 2000. They had a small ceremony in Oklahoma at the home of Wilma Mankiller, the first woman elected Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation. In typical Steinem fashion, the event, which included elements from a Cherokee ceremony, was a unique one. She wore blue jeans, according to the Post. And the pair did away with terms “husband,” “wife” in the nuptials, choosing instead to use “partners,” according to ABC News.
At the time, the marriage prompted a range of reactions, including some backlash from individuals who had long known Steinem as someone who said, “you became a semi-nonperson when you got married.“

Steinem told ABC News’ Barbara Walters in an interview months later that marriage law had evolved quite a bit since she had first begun to fight for gender equality in the 1960s. And that was in part what sparked her decision to wed.

“If the marriage law was the same law that it was before the women’s movement thirty years ago. I wouldn’t have been able to do it,” she said. “You know, because I would have lost most of my civil rights. I would have lost my name, my credit rating, my legal domicile, the ability to start a business.”
David Bale did not appear to be threatened by Steinem’s fame and influence, once telling Walters, “I actually sometimes introduce myself as Mr. Steinem.”

Bale died from lymphoma at 62 in December 2003, just years after they wed. However he left a profound mark on Steinem’s life. She told the Guardian that though their time together was brief, Bale’s presence had “had a purpose.”

“His purpose in my life was, as my friends all said, to make me feel deeply, and to live in the present. Because I live in the future,” she told the outlet in a 2011 interview. “My purpose was to give him something that he hadn’t had. We discovered that he liked to travel with me, and after an event [a speech on campus], he would have 500 young women around him, all so relieved to see that you can be a feminist and have a relationship with a man — and he was so excited by it.”

When the two would walk around Steinem’s alma mater, Smith College, Steinem recalled to the Guardian that Bale would “walk round campus saying: ‘Which one of these young women is going to be president?’”
Then, Steinem said, she “ushered him out of life.”
“His kids were there, and they were wonderful, but a contemporary is a different thing,” she told the outlet. “In a way, he taught me about dying.”
While mourning Bale, Steinem and his family members decided against holding a funeral or memorial service.
“He disliked funerals and would never go to them,” Steinem told the Los Angeles Times. “He’d rather go out to nature and think about the person who had died.”
She spoke of her late husband with high praise, describing him as having “the greatest heart of anyone I’ve ever known,” according to the Hartford Courant.

title: Dolly Parton’s Sister Slams ‘AI And Endless Garbage’ Amid Grief: ‘Show More Compassion’
summary: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton has spoken out against some of the recent AI social media posts that have followed the country icon’s death.
story: Dolly Parton’s sister has spoken out against some of the recent social media posts that have followed the country icon’s passing, which she says have been difficult to tolerate.

Stella Parton, 77, slammed the “tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage” on social media in the wake of the death of her sister Dolly Parton. The “Jolene” singer died Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer, her estate said in a statement.

“Sadly, because of the way our lives have been lived in front of the public, we have no choice but to be subjected to incredible pressure and insensitivity from strangers,” Stella Parton, a country singer and songwriter herself, wrote in an Sept. 4 Instagram post. “There is a tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage being posted everyday and it’s been challenging to absorb and or ignore.”
Stella Parton condemned “those who are in the business of exploiting the loss and tragedies of others,” adding that those individuals will “move on to the next stampede of endless misinformation.”

Dolly Parton died “at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones,” her estate said. She was preceded in death by five of her 11 siblings, who were raised in the Appalachia region of rural Tennessee by parents Robert and Avie Lee Parton, according to the Country Music Hall of Fame. Stella Parton is among her six living brothers and sisters.
In her Instagram post, Stella Parton thanked those who showed the family “‘genuine’ support and love during this time of our family bereavement.”
“We will be okay in time but each of us will grieve in our own personal way,” Stella Parton wrote. “Every human being experiences pain and loss in life and my family is no different.”
She also wrote that her sister would be “surprised and delighted” by the love that her family has been shown amid their mourning.
Stella Parton additionally praised Dolly Parton’s openness and positive influence.

“Her heart was so big and tender toward anyone who felt, as she often felt as a child,” Stella Parton wrote of her sister. “The feeling of being told you were less than, undeserving or insignificant were deep wounds on all of us as children.”
Criticizing some of the negative comments that have arisen amid the family’s journey with grief, Stella Parton called on fans to “show more compassion and wisdom as we move forward in life.”
“Use my sister’s life as an example for tolerance and respect toward others,” she wrote. “It’s not about the most clever comments, fake AI garbage or snarky tweets.”
Stella Parton added: “At the end of the day or the end of a life, how will you feel about yourself?”
“It’s not about what other individuals you will never meet think of you!” she wrote.

Stella Parton is among the family members of many late celebrities who have spoken out against the use of AI-generated images in tributes. Robin Williams’ daughter Zelda Williams also slammed the creation of deepfakes of the actor’s likeness. Robin Williams died by suicide in 2014 at age 63 while suffering from Lewy body dementia.

“If you’re just trying to troll me, I’ve seen way worse, I’ll restrict and move on. But please, if you’ve got any decency, just stop doing this to him and to me, to everyone even, full stop,” Zelda Williams previously wrote in her Instagram stories.
While Stella Parton has been vocal about some of the negativity that has followed Dolly Parton’s passing, she has also taken to social media to remember the beautiful aspects of her sister’s life.

In an Aug. 27 social media post, Stella Parton called the “Islands In the Stream” singer “one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known,” adding, “What the world saw is exactly who she was.”
“Show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end,” she wrote.

title: Fans Impressed by Usher Wax Figure They Say Is ‘Too Spot On’
summary: Some celebrity wax figures go viral for being unrecognizable, but Usher’s replica is capturing fans’ attention for being “too spot on.” See his reaction to the wax figure.
story: Some celebrity wax figures go viral for being unrecognizable, but Usher’s replica is capturing fans’ attention for being “too spot on.”

Madame Tussauds’ Las Vegas location unveiled its newest wax figure to Usher in a video shared on Instagram Sept. 3. Usher’s wax figure shows him posing while in the middle of hitting one of his signature dance moves.
“Wow,” the R&B singer said in the clip the instant he walked into the museum and spotted the creation.
“Look at that guy! It looks more like me than me,” he marveled as he inspected all the intricate details.
He pointed out that the artists perfectly matched his eyes.

“I’m blown away,” he added before sharing that the wax figure is sporting the same outfit he wore during his 2021 Las Vegas residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace. The look featured glittery red roller skates, black gloves and a “U” chain. The replica even had in-ears, the audio device musicians use when they perform.
“I hope that my fans who did not get the chance to see that show have a little bit of a glimpse of the magic that was there for my very first Vegas residency,” he shared.
In the caption, the “U Remind Me” singer quipped that now his fans know where to find him.
“I’ve officially made it back to Vegas permanently!!” he joked.
He also further complimented the Madame Tussauds creation, adding, “The details are crazy.”
Fans in the comments agreed that the wax figure was impressive, labeling it one of the best they’ve ever seen.
“Now that actually looks like the actual person. Have that person do all of them for now on even statues,” one said.
Another wrote, “I’ve never seen a wax figure look this much like the person. The person that made this has to be a fan.”
Others chimed in and poked fun at the recent rumors that Usher was using an imposter to perform for him at some stops on his joint tour with Chris Brown.
“See? The fans swore up and down you had a double. Now look!” one commented and included a crying-laughing emoji.
“You said they can’t clone you, but they sure can wax you!!!!” an Instagram user wrote. “Still doesn’t compare to the original though.”
She continued, “I guess I gotta go to Vegas to get my picture, because that’s the only way I’m getting one with you.”
But one fan playfully said she was alarmed by just how good the wax figure looked.
“This one is TOO spot on. I’m scared lol,” she said.

Usher worked personally with a team of Studio Artists from Madame Tussauds to make sure they nailed the wax figure, the museum said in a press release. The team took hundreds of measurements and photographs of the Grammy winner to include all his features.
The museum also revealed that Usher donated his residency outfit to complete the look.
“Over the course of about nine months, 20 studio artists sculpted, painted and individually inserted each piece of hair to achieve the perfect likeness,” Madame Tussauds said.

title: Tina Knowles Shares a Rare Photo Taken Moments After Beyoncé Was Born 45 Years Ago
summary: Tina Knowles shares a photo from right after Beyonce’s birth on the singer’s 45th anniversary.
story: Forty-five years ago today, a queen was born: Queen Bey.
Beyoncé is celebrating her 45th birthday on Sept. 4, 2026, and her mother, Tina Knowles, shared a glimpse into the day a star was born with a rare photo.
The photo, posted on Instagram, shows a young Knowles in a hospital bed with an even younger Beyoncé in her arms.
The photo is signed “Baby Beyoncé” with the date “9/4/1981.”

“Reminiscing on this day 45 years ago. You took nine hours to come. And I am exhausted on this photo, but the happiest I’ve ever been in my life up to this point on this day,” Knowles wrote in the caption.
She goes on to describe what’s happening in the photo.
“We are making our first eye contact. The connection is so strong and so beautiful and so powerful. It’s never been broken and it never will,” she continued.
Knowles then paid tribute to her daughter, the “extraordinary human being” that she is.
“Out of all the beautiful things about you, the thing I love the most is your huge heart! It is the thing that I’m the most proud of. You are an extraordinary human being first.”

“And even through all the sometimes terrible noise you keep going and moving forward,” Knowles said, concluding her birthday message. “Creating, loving, lifting up others constantly making history, and using that genius mind, working your butt off, minding your own damn business, and living your life to the fullest. Happy Birthday I love you ❤️🙏🏾🌹”
Knowles spoke about the meaning behind her firstborn’s name during a podcast appearance in 2021.

“A lot of people don’t know that Beyoncé is my last name. It’s my maiden name,” Knowles said on the “In My Head With Heather Thomson. “My name was Celestine Beyoncé, which at that time was not a cool thing to have that weird name. I wanted my name to be Linda Smith because those were the cool names.”

Knowles has always been very outspoken in her support for her daughter, whether it’s re-creating one of the singer’s iconic “Renaissance Tour” looks or slamming critics. She’s also a cheerleader for her second daughter, Solange.
When Beyoncé made her first Met Gala appearance in a decade and shared the spotlight with her husband Jay-Z and their daughter Blue Ivy, Knowles told TODAY she got emotional.

“It was kind of reminiscent, because Beyoncé started, you know, her first red carpet at 15, and Blue is 14,” Knowles said May 5 on the 3rd hour of TODAY. “And so just seeing her out there looking confident and beautiful, it just brought tears to my eyes.”

title: Inside Gloria Steinem’s Feminist Paradise Home, To Be Preserved as a Political Organizing Space
summary: Gloria Steinem’s New York City brownstone has been famously known as a hub for feminist organizers and activists across a swath of movements, with a history of remarkable gatherings held between its elegantly decorated walls.
story: Gloria Steinem’s New York City brownstone has been famously known as a hub for feminist organizers and activists across a swath of movements, with a history of remarkable gatherings held between its elegantly decorated walls. As activists push to preserve the iconic home after Steinem’s death this week, many are curious about what’s inside.

Nonprofit Gloria’s Foundation has said that the three-story New York City home will stand as a permanent place for political gathering and organizing. Steinem, who died on Sept. 2, passed away in the residence, “surrounded by some of the many who loved her,” according to the Instagram post on her official page.

In an installment of Architectural Digest’s “Open Door” series, Steinem gave viewers a glimpse into the storied apartment that she considered her sanctuary. And it turns out, the home was a treasure trove of historic memorabilia.

“Home means safety, shelter, friends, sleep,” she told the outlet in the 2024 house tour. “Home — I don’t want to say it’s more important than love — but it’s more permanent. And I feel that especially now, because there are so many people in the world who have no home.”

Steinem’s 1880s brownstone sits in Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Her space is an amalgamation of several apartment units in the building. And over the years, Steinem told AD, the space hosted leaders and prominent artists from Wilma Mankiller, the first woman elected Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation, to novelist Alice Walker, the first African-American woman to win the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

The journalist and activist first rented the parlor floor with friend and artist Barbara Nessim in 1968, before expanding. During the house tour, Steinem showed viewers the space that she initially shared with Nessim. The two lived between two rooms and created additional sleep space by putting a bed onto a loft that they built. The loft is still there to this day.

“We built this balcony, which actually is the front porch of some unknown person in Connecticut, and was in a wrecking yard,” she recalled to AD. “So whoever got in first got the balcony, and whoever got in second got the couch in the other room.”

Steinem’s living room was the site of many iconic gatherings. That area, she showed the outlet, includes cozy plush sofas and walls covered in artwork. Among the pieces Steinem owns is a still-life painting by her mother in addition to a piece depicting Barack Obama’s inauguration.
She also pointed out a “Madonna I bought on a trip to Latin America, because she was the only Madonna of color,” she told the outlet.
While she only had a small kitchenette when she first moved in, Steinem revealed that she has since added a larger kitchen to the home — though she doesn’t necessarily use it.
“My idea of cooking is dialing,” she said, alluding to a habit of ordering takeout.

The feminist icon’s bedroom, once her shared workspace with Nessim, includes high ceilings, built-in bookcases and a library ladder. Nightstands flank Steinem’s bed. And one of the lamps, she shows in the video, is topped with tassels that have a unique story.

“Their origin was women who were working in a factory in Afghanistan, and their bosses made them cut their hair off because they thought it was a safety hazard to get their hair, you know, caught in the machinery,” Steinem said. “They meanwhile missed the whole feeling, as we can understand, of having hair that you could toss back, and so they created their own kind of headpiece with something they also could toss back.”
The guest room is just as vibrant, filled with books, artwork and its own bathroom. Steinem said that it was her way of providing lodging to movement workers when they needed it.

“I always wanted to have space for people who were visiting New York, so it allowed me to create what is often a guest room downstairs. Meanwhile, organizers, workers, political people, friends, whoever it is, need to pass through New York,” she said. “So it always seemed right to be able to contribute at least a guest room for one or two people with its own bath.”

There’s also an outdoor space, Steinem showed AD. The garden includes several highlights, such as a plaque dedicated to Mary Wollstonecraft, the 18th century English writer and philosopher whose work “A Vindication of the Rights of Woman” is largely considered a cornerstone of classic feminism.

“In my garden, I have a Mary Wollstonecraft plaque, which reminds me that various current living generations of women, who are trying to democratize a patriarchy, can identify with their courage when they had not even a separate legal identity from daughters or wives, could not vote,” Steinem said. “It’s definitely an inspiration.”
The Instagram post on Steinem’s official Instagram requests that, in lieu of sending flowers, fans can make donations to Gloria’s Foundation, which is spearheading the preservation of the home.

title: The Emmys Are in a Week. Here’s What to Absolutely Watch
summary: Here are the TV shows and performances to watch before the 2026 Emmys including The Pitt, Pluribus and Widow’s Bay.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, pop culture experts share their recommendations for what to watch ahead of the Emmys.
The Emmys are approaching fast, which means there are only a few more days to catch up on buzzy award shows.

The ceremony takes place on Monday, Sept. 14, on NBC. So, maybe not quite enough time to binge-watch entire series, but there’s definitely enough hours to at least get a taste of the performances that everyone will be talking about.
To narrow down what to watch, TODAY.com spoke to two pop culture experts to get their opinions:
Chris Witherspoon, founder of PopViewers and an entertainment contributor for NBC News and MSNBCKristen Maldonado, founder of the entertainment outlet Pop Culture Planet
Chris Witherspoon, founder of PopViewers and an entertainment contributor for NBC News and MSNBC
Kristen Maldonado, founder of the entertainment outlet Pop Culture Planet
Read on for their recommendations.
Front-Running Shows

Nominated for: 18 awards, including outstanding drama series; outstanding lead actress in a drama (Rhea Seehorn); outstanding supporting actor in a drama (Carlos-Manuel Vesga); and outstanding guest actress in a drama (Miriam Shor)
“Apple TV is really just nailing it lately,” Maldonado says, referring to “Pluribus” and another Emmys darling, “Widow’s Bay.”

Created by Vince Gilligan of “Breaking Bad” and “Better Call Saul,” this sci-fi series is about a woman (Rhea Seehorn) who ends up being one of the few of humanity not to be taken over by an alien virus that dissolves individuality.
“The most miserable woman on book in the world has to save everyone,” Maldonado says.

Nominated for: 19 awards, including outstanding comedy series; outstanding lead actor in a comedy (Matthew Rhys); outstanding supporting actor in a comedy (Stephen Root); and outstanding supporting actress in a comedy (Kate O’Flynn)

Created by Katie Dippold, a former “Parks and Recreation” writer, “Widow’s Bay” is set on a definitely haunted New England island, which the mayor (Matthew Rhys) is desperately trying to make palatable to tourists.
“What’s so great about ‘Widow’s Bay’ is that it’s equal parts funny and unsettling,” Maldonado says. “Katie Dippold managed to deliver something that we haven’t seen before.”

Nominated for: 25 awards, including outstanding drama series; outstanding lead actor in a drama series (Noah Wyle); outstanding supporting actress in a drama series (Sepideh Moafi, Katherine LaNasa, Taylor Dearden, Fiona Dourif); outstanding guest actress in a drama series (Brittany Allen, Tal Anderson, Tina Ivlev) and more
Witherspoon says all you need is to watch one episode of “The Pitt,” HBO’s ER-set medical drama, to get the appeal. “You’ll be like, ‘Oh my God! I see how powerful this show is,’” he says.
The show’s second season follows senior attending doctor Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch (Noah Wyle) on the last day before he heads out for a risky sabbatical.
Hidden Gems

Nominated for: Outstanding limited or anthology series; lead actress in an anthology series or movie (Sarah Snook); supporting actress in an anthology series or movie (Dakota Fanning); outstanding writing for a limited or anthology series (Meghan Gallagher)
The book “All Her Fault” was sparked by an incident from author Andrea Mara’s real life, which then became a Peacock miniseries. Sarah Snook plays a mom whose son disappears suddenly.
Witherspoon calls this a great show, and “one that you can rush through.”
Nominated for: Outstanding writing for a comedy series

The second season of “Jury Duty” followed the zany, “Truman Show”-esque premise of the first, but with a different setting. Instead of staging a fake jury duty, producers put the unsuspecting Anthony Norman at the center of a company retreat.
Must-See Performances

Maldonado and Witherspoon both said Noah Wyle is the one to watch in the outstanding lead actor in a drama category. He took away the award for “The Pitt’s” first season for his work as Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch, the beleaguered, wise and occasionally bereft ER doctor.
Witherspoon also notes that he’s the first lead actor nominee who is also up for best director and could make history if he wins.

“Wonder Man” is a spin on a typical superhero show. Yahya Abdul-Mateen plays a struggling actor who ends up developing unexpected powers. The show was not renewed for a second season, a decision Abdul-Mateen has criticized. He was nominated for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series.

“It’s one of those shows that I think people underestimated. You know, it’s not getting a second season, but his performance is such a standout. He brings this like comedy and charm that I think is really refreshing,” Maldonado says.
Nominated for: Outstanding lead actor in a comedy series
Matthew Rhys is nominated for two Emmys this year: One for his work in the anthology series “The Beast in Me” and another for Apple TV’s sleeper hit “Widow’s Bay.”
“We’ve not really seen him be a nominee since ‘The Americans.’ I feel like it could put Matthew back in the winner circle,” Witherspoon says.
Nominated for: Outstanding supporting actress in a comedy series
“She just is so funny, so uncomfortable, so vulnerable, but also so badass. She’s been the MVP of the season of the show,” Maldonado says.
If you’re going to watch one episode, check out the episode “Beach Reads,” centered on her character discovering a bewitching book.
Nominated for: Outstanding lead actress in a drama series
Rhea Seehorn gives “such an impressive performance” as Carol Sturka, one of the few people not impacted by an alien virus, Maldonado says.
Witherspoon says she goes through “the entire range of emotions” on the show. Plus, her winning an Emmy would be a full-circle moment after years of nominations but no wins for “Better Call Saul.”

“I love when I watch moments where somebody who’s been in the game for 30 years gets their flowers. She’s 54 years old. She is the front runner to win that category. I just feel like give Rhea all her things,” Witherspoon says.

title: See Kelly Clarkson’s First TODAY Interview After Winning ‘American Idol’ 24 Years Ago
summary: Take a look back at Kelly Clarkson’s visit with TODAY, two days after she won the first season of “American Idol” in 2002.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment aired Sept. 6, 2002 and features Kelly Clarkson, less than 48 hours after winning the first season of “American Idol.”

On Sept. 4, 2002, the world of music changed when Kelly Clarkson won the inaugural season of “American Idol.” Her charming, down-home personality and stunning vocal range won over viewers and judges alike, as Clarkson toppled Justin Guarini to win the show, which, like Clarkson herself, would go on to become a cultural institution.

Clarkson, of course, would transform from powerhouse singer to just plain powerhouse. She has scored a trio of No. 1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 and won three Grammy Awards, with 14 other nominations under her belt. She became a coach on “The Voice” and just wrapped up her seven-year run as host of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” which netted her multiple Daytime Emmy Awards for outstanding host and talk show.

All of those accomplishments and accolades were ahead of Clarkson, though, when she stopped by TODAY on Sept. 6, 2002, just two days after her “American Idol” win. It was a whirlwind time for her as the victory was quickly followed by a massive press tour.
“I just walked off a plane, so, yeah, I’m a little exhausted. But it’s cool. It’s cool. I love it,” the then-20-year-old told Katie Couric.
“I’ve done a little bit of everything,” she said about the previous 48 hours, alluding to all of the appearance she had made and noting how little she had slept.
Kelly Clarkson Understood the Impact of Her First Song
After she was announced as the winner, Clarkson sang “A Moment Like This,” which would become her first single — and first No. 1 hit. What was going through her mind as she sang?
“I was trying not to think of the words,” she said, laughing while Couric said the lyrics were “very relevant” to what Clarkson was experiencing at that point.
Kelly Clarkson Was in Awe That She Won
Clarkson was gobsmacked by the enormous odds she overcame to win the contest, even as she performed “A Moment Like This.”
“I guess I was thinking, there’s so many talented people out there, I can’t believe. Who would’ve thunk it, you know? Walking in, out of 10,000 people, I don’t know,” she said.
Kelly Clarkson Had Endured Plenty
Though only 20 at the time, Clarkson had already held many jobs while pursuing her dream as a singer.
“I’ve done everything,” she said, while first saying she had worked as a waitress before Couric asked her what else she had done.

“Oh, I’ve worked for the zoo,” she continued. “I’ve worked for bookstores. I’ve been a telemarketer. I’ve done door-to-door sales. You name it. You know, because I’m a performer. You never want that job. You know, you always want to do singing, so you’re never satisfied.”

title: U.S. strikes Iranian tankers after attempted attacks on Navy warship
summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.
story: The U.S. military sank five Iranian tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in response to attempted attacks by the IRGC on an American warship, according to U.S. Central Command.

“CENTCOM forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers, Sept. 8, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days,” U.S. Central Command said in a post on X. “The U.S. warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed.”
Four of the tankers were attacked in the Gulf of Oman and one was hit near Kharg Island, according to CENTCOM.
“American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable,” CENTCOM said in a statement.

A U.S. strike hit an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island, Iran’s main oil terminal, which has been repeatedly threatened by President Donald Trump, according to the semiofficial Tasnim news agency.    The U.S. military hit a second tanker near the port city of Jask, according to Iranian state TV.

The strikes on the Iranian tankers Tuesday come after the IRGC attempted to hit an American aircraft carrier and a destroyer over the weekend, resulting in a U.S. response in which the U.S. sank one tanker and permanently disabled two more.
Iran threatened to target oil tankers in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for the U.S. strikes on Tuesday.

“Following the actions of the American military in targeting several Iranian oil tankers, we warn all oil tanker crews in the areas around the ports of Kuwait and Bahrain, which are hosting these forces and are complicit in their actions, to immediately evacuate their vessels, whether they are at anchor or docked as they will be targeted,” the IRGC Navy said in a statement posted by the semi-official Fars news agency.

The Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the war, has become the key battleground in the conflict as both the U.S. and Iran have attacked tankers.

The Trump administration on Tuesday also imposed sanctions on additional elements of Iran’s aviation industry, targeting more than two dozen commercial and private airlines as well as foreign cargo service providers in its new push to isolate Tehran from its remaining trading partners.

A U.S. blockade of Iranian ports has squeezed the country’s economy by limiting its oil exports, while the American military has been helping a limited number of ships transit on a route through the Strait of Hormuz off Oman. Tehran wants ships to follow a route that it chooses through the strait, which was considered an international waterway before the war.

title: Iran increases gasoline price for its heaviest consumers as economy struggles
summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran early Tuesday introduced a higher price for its heaviest users of gasoline, state media reported, in the latest economic pinch caused by months of war.
story: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran early Tuesday introduced a higher price for its heaviest users of gasoline, state media reported, in the latest economic pinch caused by months of war. It’s the second such hike since December.
Such gas price increases can be sensitive and contribute to inflation. An increase in 2019 sparked nationwide protests and a crackdown that reportedly killed over 300 people.

Without specifically mentioning the war with the United States, the government’s announcement cited the “current situation,” adding that the extra money from the price increase will be given to households.

Under the new system, people buying more than their quota of 110 liters (29 gallons) of gasoline a month now must pay 100,000 rials (about 7 cents) per liter, or twice as much as they have been paying since December.

Iran still has some of the world’s lowest gasoline prices, but the price increase adds to daily pressures for many of the country’s more than 90 million people. Already, the currency has been dropping to record lows, and purchasing power has weakened. On Monday, the U.S. dollar was trading at 2.22 million rials.
Keramat Veis Karami, the CEO of the state oil distribution company, on Monday said the new gasoline rate would affect 15% of consumers, the official IRNA news agency reported.

The CEO said consumption reached a record high at 145 million liters (38 million gallons) per day in August, while domestic production capacity was 122 million liters per day. The rest of the supply is imported.
Raising prices can help calm high consumption, which experts have blamed on aging cars and spare parts in Iran as well as insufficient public transportation.

But experts also say increases in gasoline prices will lead to higher inflation in a country that’s already struggling with an annual inflation rate of about 67%, according to the country’s statistics center, a government agency.

Cheap gasoline has been viewed for generations as a birthright in Iran, sparking mass demonstrations as far back as 1964, when a price increase forced the shah to put military vehicles on the streets to replace those of striking taxi drivers.
Iranians react to the gas price hike
An hour after the new pricing went into practice, two of eight gas stations visited by The Associated Press were closed to regulate the price rate of the pumps.
The six others were active, and a dozen cars were in line in each.
Security was tight around the filling stations and both uniformed and plainclothes police were visible around.
In the queue, Asghar Rahimi, a 34-year-old Tehran resident, said the price increases will not stop.
“The tiny amount cannot help government to manage problems like poverty and unemployment,” Rahimi said. “This was the first step. In coming months, they need to raise it again.”
Another resident, Ali Salari, 55, feared the raise in price will affect prices of other goods, including bread and meat.
“It has been that way ever since government manipulated gas prices,” Salari said.
Tehran citizen Hamid Mirzei, 43, said food prices have kept rising and a grocery trip just for staples, like beans and lentils, can cost up to 100 million rials ($73).
“Life has become difficult for all of us. Even basic groceries are becoming unaffordable,” Mirzei said.
“If gasoline prices go up as well, things will only get much worse,” he added.

title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”
story: LONDON — Flights departing from at least two major British airports have been grounded following a “technical issue,” officials said Tuesday.

London’s Heathrow Airport said in a statement Tuesday that it was working with Britain’s National Air Traffic Service to resolve the issue, advising passengers to check with their airlines for more information regarding their flights.
“Arriving flights are not currently impacted,” Heathrow said, although it advised passengers to check flight times.

London Gatwick Airport also said on X that it had been affected, and further north, Manchester Airport took to social media to warn that the issue “may result in delays.” Edinburgh Airport in Scotland issued a similar warning.
After earlier blaming a “technical issue,” the National Air Traffic Service said in an update on X that its engineers had “implemented a fix, and our flight system is starting to recover.”
Apologizing to passengers for the disruptions, it said flights were “departing and airspace is open, but recovery will take some time.”
Heidi Alexander, Britain’s transport minister, also took to social media to apologize. “I know this will be frustrating for passengers and I’m sorry,” she wrote on X.
With 84.5 million passengers last year, Heathrow ranked seventh in the table of the world’s busiest airports, according to data published by Airports Council International.
Airline Ryanair said in a statement that 65,000 of its passengers were disrupted and 50 scheduled flights were canceled because of the disruption.
British Airways canceled 96 flights, easyJet 92, and KLM 20, according to the aviation tracking site FlightRadar24.
Travel from Heathrow was severely disrupted in March last year when a massive fire at an electricity substation caused a predawn power outage at the global transport hub.
The closure affected more than 1,300 flights and 200,000 passengers.

After investigating 600 items of evidence related to the substation, the National Energy System Operator ruled out suspicious activity in a report saying a preventable moisture fault caused the fire, leaving almost 70,000 homes without power.

title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan are “surprised” by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles that reiterated they will remain nonworking members of the royal family after their return to Britain, a spokesperson for the couple told NBC News on Tuesday.
story: LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, were “surprised” by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III that confirmed they remain nonworking members of the royal family after their return to Britain, a spokesperson for the couple told NBC News on Tuesday.
Buckingham Palace released the letter Monday, reiterating that Harry and Meghan remained nonworking royals as they have since they stepped down from royal duties in January 2020.
A palace source said the letter was issued to clarify the unchanged position of the couple for the British government and military amid questions over whether the public should fund their security.
It was put into the public domain because it likely would have leaked anyway and the palace wanted to avoid claims of secrecy around what it contained, the source said.
But a spokesman for Harry and Meghan told NBC News that they  were “surprised” by the letter and were not given an opportunity to contribute to its contents.

The contents of the letter were shared with the couple’s staff a few hours before it was released, according to a spokesperson for the Sussexes. A Buckingham Palace source confirmed to NBC News that the letter had been shared with Harry’s team Monday.

A spokesman for Harry and Meghan told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week, perhaps as early as Tuesday, to discuss whether to provide security for the couple now that they have moved back to the United Kingdom.
The Home Office, the government department responsible for the protection of public figures, declined to respond directly when asked by NBC News, citing security concerns.
A palace source said Monday that it was up to the security committee to decide whether to allocate security for the prince and his family.
The couple moved from California last month for an “extended” stay with their children Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

Their surprise return has reignited media coverage of royal tensions, which exploded into public view with the couple’s allegations of racism and bullying. They moved to Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara, and signed a number of commercial deals.
The move back to Britain has also raised a number of questions over security, after a protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the removal of their protection.

The long-running dispute stems from a decision by the Home Office in February 2020 that the couple would no longer automatically receive personal police security while in Britain. Harry argues that the government should provide security for him and his family due to his high-profile position, military service in Afghanistan and threats he has received.
The latest public tension follows Monday’s release of the letter signed by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior officer of the royal household.

It said: “It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family.”

It went on to say that their charitable work was “a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity” and “in short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”

It added: “This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected.”

title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan will not be working royals after U.K. return
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan will not be working members of Britain’s royal family now they have returned to the U.K., a letter sent on behalf of King Charles said.
story: LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, will remain nonworking members of Britain’s royal family after their return to the U.K., a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III said Monday.

The couple who last month moved from California back to Britain for an “extended” stay with their children Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, will still not be able to use the titles of His and Her Royal Highness, according to the letter signed by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior officer of the royal household.

“It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family,” the letter read.

“This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected,” it added.

A Buckingham Palace source confirmed to NBC News that the letter had been shared with Harry’s team on Monday. It was put into the public domain because it would likely have leaked anyway and they wanted to avoid claims of secrecy around what it contained, they said.
Add to Google
Add to Google
NBC News has reached out to the Sussexes for comment.
The letter from Lord Chamberlain went on to say that “their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used.”

It added that their charitable work was “a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity” and “in short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”
The letter was released “to help avoid doubt or confusion,” after “a number of requests for guidance.”
Harry and Meghan rattled the royal family when they opted to step down as working royals six years ago, eventually choosing a quieter life in Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara.

Relations with the royal family have been strained since then, worsened in part by explosive allegations of racism and bullying made by the couple in their Netflix documentary “Harry & Meghan” and in Harry’s memoir, “Spare.”

After few signs of a royal rapprochement, Britain was shocked last month when it emerged they were planning a return and reports in British media indicated that Archie and Lilibet had been enrolled in schools in the country.
A source close to the couple told NBC News at the time that they were moving back for an “extended period” of time.

The location of their new home has not been disclosed and questions remain over what security arrangements will be in place for the couple, after a protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the removal of their security protection.

Harry’s return to Britain also comes after he and several other claimants were ordered to pay a combined 34.5 million pounds ($46 million) to Associated Newspapers, the publisher of The Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday, after losing a High Court battle over alleged breaches of privacy.

It was one of several salvos between Harry and the British press, which went into overdrive after they announced their return, with front pages dominated by unconfirmed reports that Meghan could return to acting for the first time since she departed the television show “Suits” ahead of her 2018 wedding to Harry.

title: U.S. envoys ‘very encouraged’ after peace talks in Moscow and Kyiv
summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said talks were “substantive,” but neither gave details of any proposal to end the conflict.
story: President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had “very meaningful” talks with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday after holding similar discussions a day before with Russia’s Vladimir Putin aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.
Speaking with reporters following an initial round of talks with Zelenskyy on Sunday, Witkoff said the discussions had been “substantive” and “important.”
“We are very encouraged,” he added.
Kushner emphasized in separate comments that Trump was “very determined to see an end to this war.”
Neither gave details of the specifics of any proposal to end the conflict.
The pair arrived in Kyiv earlier Sunday by train following a flight from Moscow to the Polish border.

“Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive. We are interested in bringing the end of the war closer,” Zelenskyy said on social media ahead of the talks, adding that Ukraine’s “proposals are ready.”

Both Russia and Ukraine agreed to hold off on aerial attacks on each other’s capitals to enable the visits over the weekend, bringing a brief respite in the cities, though no broader ceasefire is in place.

A stream of past peace efforts have so far failed to deliver significant movement toward peace in a war that Trump once vowed to end on Day 1 of his presidency. Talks have been effectively paused in recent months due to the Iran war.

While there has been little recent movement on the front lines, the talks come ahead of what will likely be a difficult winter in Kyiv, which is facing a critical shortage of U.S.-made interceptor missiles able to repel Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure.

Sunday’s visit to Kyiv is believed to be the first to be made by Witkoff and Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, as part of the peace effort. Witkoff has visited Moscow several times, most recently holding talks with Putin at the Kremlin in January.

Witkoff on Saturday appeared to strike a particularly warm tone during the meeting with Putin. In video published by Russia’s state-owned news outlet RIA Novosti, he told the Russian leader that the delegation had been reflecting on how “when we retire, we’ll have all these incredible stories and incredible memories, and yours will be right at the top of it all.”

Putin did not publicly signal any movement from his previous steep demands, which seek major concessions from Ukraine. He praised Witkoff and Kushner in the video, telling them: “I would like to say that working with you is a comfortable experience for us, and we certainly place a high level of trust in you throughout this process.”
Following the meeting Sunday with Zelenskyy, Witkoff also offered praise to the Ukrainian leader, saying his hospitality was “unsurpassed.”
A White House official said “substantive plans for the next steps” in the effort to end the war were at the center of the talks.
In a statement, the official said those next steps would be announced in the coming weeks, with the U.S. delegates looking forward to “equally productive meetings” in Ukraine.
They added that officials from the National Security Council, the State Department and the Treasury Department joined the meeting on Saturday, which lasted more than three hours.

Putin aide Yury Ushakov told Russian state media on Sunday that the meeting, which included an “informal setting at the dining table,” was “substantive, constructive, extremely frank and trusting,” noting it was the eighth time the U.S. delegation has visited Russia and that Putin had extended his “best wishes” to Trump.
In a nightly address on Friday, Zelenskyy said Kyiv’s goal was to have the “most constructive, substantive visit and negotiations possible with the American side.”
“We need to look for real options for how to bring this war to an end,” he said, adding: “We’ll see what proposals Steve and Jared have, and what they are told about this in Moscow.”
Pope Leo XIV said in remarks following his weekly Sunday Angelus prayer that he hoped the talks would “bear concrete fruit and open space for diplomacy.”

“My heart goes out to the suffering people, who for years have lived in anguish and fear,” he said, renewing his “appeal to put an end to the violence, to stop the destruction and to open hearts to dialogue and peace.”
Ahead of the talks, Russia had ramped up its attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities with relentless bombardments, exploiting Ukraine’s shortage of air defense systems.

A Russian drone on Friday hit one of the most important government buildings in Kyiv, the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service, known as the SBU, one of the agencies involved in the execution of deep-strike operations inside Russia.
In a social media post Saturday, Zelenskyy said Russia had launched overnight strikes on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports, linking the attack to the U.S. visit.
“Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the U.S. side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” he said.
He said Kyiv had “taken note of this Russian move” and would “adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky.”

Speaking with reporters on Friday during an event in the Oval Office, Trump said Kushner and Witkoff had been doing a “great job” in their efforts on the peace process ahead of their visits to Moscow and Kyiv.
“We sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done,” he said. “And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it.”

title: U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets Navy warships, military says
summary: U.S. Central Command said no American personnel were harmed in the Iranian missile attacks.
story: U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy ships, the U.S. military said.
A U.S. aircraft carrier and guided missile destroyer evaded multiple attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, U.S. Central Command said in a statement. No American personnel were harmed.

CENTCOM said U.S. forces retaliated by permanently disabling two crude oil carriers, the M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask. Forces also destroyed a third vessel, the M/T Kylo near the Gulf of Oman.
The Kylo was not carrying oil at the time and its crew was directed to abandon the vessel before American forces struck it in multiple locations, CENTCOM said.

“If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, said in a statement. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”
Iran’s Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the U.S. strikes, calling them “illegal and aggressive” and accusing Washington of waging a naval blockade and economic war against Iran.

In a statement carried by Iranian state media IRIB, the ministry said the attacks violated the United Nations Charter and constituted a war crime and a threat to international peace and commercial shipping.

Iranian semiofficial news agency Fars reported that the IRGC attacked with ballistic missiles an aircraft carrier and a military destroyer that had been taking part in the naval blockade and “harassing Iranian vessels.”
On Sunday, the IRGC also said it struck an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. did not immediately confirm the purported attack.

Kharg Island, a tiny but strategic island 15 miles off the coast of Iran in the Persian Gulf, plays a central role in the country’s oil industry. There are also military capabilities there, including air defenses and mines buried underground.

The site has repeatedly emerged as a flashpoint during the conflict. U.S. forces struck military targets on the island in March but deliberately spared its oil infrastructure. President Donald Trump said at the time that the U.S. could target the energy facilities if Iran continued interfering with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The island is critical to Iran’s finances. Petras Katinas, a research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, previously told NBC News that Kharg is the “backbone” of Iran’s oil trade infrastructure and the primary gateway for the country’s oil reserves.

Iranian media reported earlier Saturday that a tanker near Kharg had been hit by U.S. missiles and that its crew was being evacuated. No casualties were reported, according to Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency.
